Fifa has scrapped its plan to sell stakes in the World Cup and other tournaments to private investors, after widespread backlash and threats of a boycott.

Fifa president Gianni Infantino proposed the controversial plan in July, declaring that a vote would determine whether or not it would go ahead, but there was anger and concern from many voices in the footballing world.

European football’s governing body Uefa even confirmed a boycott of the World Cup and other Fifa competitions, saying its member nations would not take part if Infantino’s plan was voted through.

The Asian Football Confederation and Concacaf, which represents 41 nations from North and Central America and the Caribbean, backed Uefa in their stance.

Despite Fifa hitting back in a statement that insisted “nobody is selling football”, the sport’s world governing body ultimately backed down.

The immediate response of some association heads is that Infantino still needs to go.

Gianni Infantino has scrapped his plans to sell off a stake in the World Cup ( PA Wire )

A statement from Infantino read: “The Fifa Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our Fifa Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed.

“And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the Fifa Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the Fifa Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders.

“Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place.

“Our purpose has always been - and will always be - to unite and improve. As a result, this proposal will not proceed.

“Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, particularly in those countries that mostly need our support.”

News.title: World Cup boycott latest: Infantino scraps sell-off plan after Trump claims he was never consulted
News.content:
Inside Uefa’s extraordinary World Cup boycott plans – and what Fifa might do next

Gianni Infantino is under mounting pressure from football federations as well as from within Fifa after Uefa’s boycott of the World Cup left his plans to privatise its tournaments in tatters.

Infantino’s long-term adviser Carlos Cordeiro, a key figure within Fifa, has quit in protest of Infantino’s proposals, while Fifa’s chief operating officer has said that Infantino “deceived” staff over his plans. The Asian Football Confederation, meanwhile, has become the third federation to reject them publicly, releasing a strong statement on Friday backing the stance of Uefa and Concacaf, while claiming that confidence in Fifa’s governance has been “undermined”.

Donald Trump meanwhile told reporters on Friday that he has not spoken to Infantino about the plans despite their close relationship and the fact that Josh Kushner, the brother of Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, is expected to lead ⁠the proposed investor group.

It all resulted in Infantino officially scrapping the plans to sell off a stake in the World Cup, but the Fifa president remains under intense scrutiny with many associations feeling his position is untenable.

Bev Craig will succeed Andy Burnham as mayor of Greater Manchester, securing a comfortable Labour victory over Reform on a historically low turnout.

Only one in four of the more than 2 million eligible voters across Greater Manchester cast ballots as Ms Craig defeated Reform UK’s Sian Astley in the second round – the first electoral test of Mr Burnham’s premiership.

Ms Craig won 47.15 per cent of votes in the first round, just short of the 50 per cent needed to win outright in the Supplementary Vote system, with Ms Astley, on 20.99 per cent.

It is the first time that a Greater Manchester mayoral election has gone to a second round, which Ms Craig won with 309,525 first and second place votes, ahead of Ms Astley on 157,178, to give her one of the country’s most powerful political jobs outside of Westminster.

“I will defend this city region with every bone in my body and I will fight for a better life for all of us”, she told the hall at the Co-op Live arena in her victory speech.

When Mr Burnham, who won three mayoral elections – all with more than 60 per cent of the vote, first announced his intention to return to Westminster, the prospect of Labour losing control of Greater Manchester was used as a reason by allies of Sir Keir Starmer to keep him in post.

However, Ms Craig’s victory comes as her party is enjoying a “Burnham bounce” in national polls, with him taking over from Sir Keir in Downing Street sparking a change in Labour’s fortunes.

Greater Manchester mayoral election results Sian Astley (Reform): 157,178 [first and second preference votes] Geraldine Coggins (Green): 64,968 Bev Craig (Labour): 309,525 [first and second preference votes] Phil Eckersley (Conservative): 41,021 Marcus Farmer (Independent): 2,969 Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats): 14,702 Marlon West (Restore Britain): 46,289

Described as Mr Burnham’s “protege”, the Belfast-born incoming mayor has led Manchester City Council since 2021 and worked closely with the prime minister as Greater Manchester Combined Authority’s member for the economy.

"I never believed as a girl growing up on a council estate that one day I would have a chance to stand for the place that I love”, she said.

The turnout was a historic low for a mayoral election in this region, dropping below the first race in 2017, when 28.9 per cent of the electorate turned out.

However, it still took more than 13 hours from verification beginning to the result being declared.

Part of that could be attributed to election fatigue in this part of the country, as Greater Manchester has spent much of the year as the focus of British politics.

This is the third time in 2026 that voters in the parliamentary constituencies of Gorton and Denton and Makerfield have gone to the polls this year, following by-elections and May’s local contests.

Both the Green Party and Reform will be disappointed with their performances, with the former not making it into the run-off.

The Greens won in Gorton and Denton in February and the party’s campaigning suggested that it was a two-horse race between themselves and Reform, having made significant gains in Manchester in May’s local elections, but they did not make it into the second round.

open image in gallery Bev Craig at the vote count for the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election at the Co-Op Live Arena in Manchester ( PA )

Meanwhile, it is Reform’s third disappointment in Greater Manchester this year, after failing to win in Gorton and Denton or Makerfield.

Nigel Farage’s party were made early favourites by the bookmakers when this by-election was first mooted, having performed well in the local elections here, winning 24 of 25 seats available in Wigan in May.

But polls suggested that Ms Craig would secure a comfortable win, helped by Mr Burnham’s taking over from Sir Keir Starmer as prime minister, which proved to be correct.

Mr Burnham showed in Makerfield that his name on the Labour ballot could beat Reform and what is now his party has claimed another important victory in his own back yard – albeit in its worst performance in the history of this contest.

The result in Greater Manchester came on the same day that the prime minister announced that English mayors will be allowed to keep a share of the taxes collected in their area, as part of his pledge to “take power out of Westminster and carry it into every postcode in the country”.

open image in gallery Bev Craig is congratulated after she was declared winner of the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election ( PA )

Mr Burnham’s plans to let mayors keep a slice of income tax and business rates come as part of his bid to incentivise regional leaders to promote economic growth in different parts of the UK.

It means that Ms Craig will have more power than he did during his nine years running this city region.

About that, she told The Independent following her victory: “I've long argued, as did Andy before he became prime minister, that Greater Manchester should have more power and more control.

“So it's absolutely fantastic that in two weeks since becoming prime minister, he's coming good on his long-standing beliefs around power and control.

“And I want to be able to put that to good use. Things like skills and support in our young people, from 16, it's going to make an incredible difference here in Greater Manchester, and I can't wait to get to work.”

A public health researcher at Johns Hopkins University is locked up in an Immigration and Customs Enforcement detention center in Louisiana after her arrest by federal agents while boarding a domestic flight in Baltimore this week.

Fatima Ameaka, a senior analyst at the Center for Outbreak Response Innovation in the Bloomberg School of Public Health, is a former Fulbright scholar originally from Cameroon. Immigration officers arrested her at the Baltimore-Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport for allegedly overstaying a visa.

She was most recently being held at the South Louisiana ICE Processing Center roughly 90 miles from Baton Rouge, according to the agency’s detainee locator system.

Her arrest and detention, first reported by The Baltimore Banner, follows a spike in airport arrests and a growing coordination between ICE and the Transportation Security Administration, with recently unveiled memorandums detailing a data-sharing agreement that grants officers access to passenger information for “aviation security.”

There are myriad reasons why an otherwise “legal” immigrant may have “overstayed” with an expired visa, including time lapsed while navigating the byzantine bureaucracy of visa renewals and seeking permanent legal status. But Donald Trump’s administration has prioritized virtually every case for arrest and removal under the president’s government-wide efforts to deport 1 million people from the country each year.

open image in gallery A public health researcher at Johns Hopkins University was arrested while boarding a domestic flight in Baltimore, the latest ICE arrest in apparent coordination with TSA ( Getty )

The Department of Homeland Security claims Nkempu entered the U.S. on a visa in June 2023 allowing her to stay in the country legally until mid-2024. “Being in detention is a choice,” an agency spokesperson said in a statement.

Her detention also follows a streak of arrests targeting international scholars at prominent institutions across the country.

Johns Hopkins is “deeply concerned” about her arrest, according to a statement from university spokesperson Doug Donovan.

“The university understands the fear and concern this instills in members of our community,” he wrote. “Dr. Ameaka was traveling in a personal capacity, and though we cannot comment on the specifics of her situation, we want to assure our community that the university is actively working to provide support for Dr. Ameaka, including ensuring she has access to legal representation.

A surge of immigration arrests at U.S. airports, some of which have been captured in viral videos, appear to have followed increased coordination between ICE and airport authorities who maintain and share information and “tips” about noncitizen travelers, even if they do not have criminal records.

TSA is providing ICE with the names and birth dates of travelers believed to have been ordered out of the country by an immigration court judge, allowing officers to quickly identify and arrest people in airport terminals.

open image in gallery Newly released documents reveal an apparent data-sharing agreement between ICE and TSA to identify immigrants traveling in American airports who could be targets for removal from the country ( AFP/Getty )

Newly disclosed agreements obtained by watchdog group American Oversight reveal that ICE and TSA have been working together since at least May 2025, appearing to contradict congressional testimony from Acting TSA Administrator Ha Nguyen McNeill about the agencies’ work.

Rep. Dan Goldman asked McNeill if ICE shares information with TSA to determine whether passengers have been ordered removed from the country.

“That is not what is occurring,” she said. “We don’t send the information to ICE, we help ICE check against information.”

The agency is working “within our authorities to share information within the Department of Homeland Security to further the national security mission,” she said.

A memo obtained by American Oversight shows the agencies had established more formal data-sharing information and outlined procedures for ICE to retain information obtained from TSA.

David Cummins, Trump’s nominee for TSA administrator, did not detail the terms of the agreement when pressed during his Senate confirmation hearing this week.

“This agreement pulls back the curtain on the formal partnership between TSA and ICE that the administration refused to explain to the public,” American Oversight Executive Director Chioma Chukwu said in a statement this week.

“Americans provide their personal information to board a plane safely, not to become part of an immigration enforcement system or a government surveillance network,” Chukwu added.

Children’s birthday party hosts are facing backlash online after explicitly asking invited guests to leave cash tips and cover event expenses.

The topic drew attention after Victoria Perry, a baker who specializes in children’s birthday cakes, posted a viral TikTok video detailing invitations she had seen that included phrases like “tipping is encouraged.”

As reported by Parents, Perry cited one invitation that specifically asked guests to send cash to help cover basic costs: “If you plan to bring your child and they plan to eat and play, please send along cash with your child for the tip bucket to go towards party expenses.”

In her video, Perry criticized the practice, arguing that tip requests send an unwelcoming message to invited guests: “If you’re not bringing at least $10, you should not bring your child.”

The practice comes at a time when the financial burden of hosting children's celebrations has escalated significantly. Recent estimates reported by CBC News show the average parent spends at least $445 per event, with one in five spending over $700 and a third of parents going into debt to afford the occasion. Event planners have even reported wealthy hosts spending upwards of $42,000 on extravagant bashes, according to Business Insider.

Children’s birthday party hosts are facing criticism online for asking guests to tip. The topic drew attention after a viral TikTok posted by a baker detailed invitations including phrases such as ‘tipping is encouraged’ ( AFP via Getty Images )

The rising costs — driven by high venue fees, entertainment like bouncy castles or mobile zoos, and lavish social media trends — have led some hosts to seek outside financial help, though the practice has faced pushback from other parents.

“If you are inviting my children to your child’s birthday and you asked me to pay for them to come, nine out of 10 times they're probably not going to be attending," one U.K. parent and financial adviser posted online. Another parenting podcaster said in a March video that one mother had gone so far as to send invoices to invited guests.

Many parents online argue that host families should not throw events beyond their financial means.

As reported by Parents, one commenter wrote, “My RSVP would be a NO. If you need to be tipped for hosting your child’s party, maybe don’t have a party.” Another said that cash demands undermine standard etiquette: “If I’m bringing a tip, then we’re not bringing a present.”

Speaking to CBC News, Ottawa mother Gaelan Jaffray echoed that sentiment.

“I don’t think the rising cost of hosting justifies asking invited guests to subsidize the party," Jaffray said. “To me, bringing a gift is already the guest’s contribution.”

However, others have defended host parents struggling against inflation and intense social pressure.

“Although not polite to ask for money, I would give a tip plus a present,” one commenter wrote. “Affording to throw my kid a birthday party is a privilege not every parent has.”

Experts point out that much of this financial strain stems from what researchers term the “intensification of parenting” and online comparison culture, which was highlighted in a 2024 U.S. Surgeon General advisory regarding parental mental health.

“When it’s financially difficult for families to do this to the extent they have to ask other families to pitch in, we are really getting out of hand," parenting consultant Vanessa Lapointe told CBC News.

Children ultimately focus on how they feel during a party rather than its cost or scale, Lapointe said.

Europe faces a fresh border crisis after around 60,000 migrants from Morocco crossed into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta in just 24 hours.

At least 57 people died as border security struggled to deal with the sudden influx, with extraordinary footage capturing the huge crowds making their way into Spain’s North African territory.

Some drowned in the crossing while others were killed in a stampede at the Tarajal beach fence near a border checkpoint with Morocco.

Spain’s prime minister Pedro Sanchez called the incident an “attack on Spain’s territorial integrity” and vowed to “use all the resources of the state to guarantee security and coexistence”.

open image in gallery Migrants attempting to cross into Ceuta gather on a hilltop during clashes with Moroccan security forces ( AFP/Getty )

Ceuta and the larger Spanish territory of Melilla, which is some 400km (250 miles) east of it, are located on the Mediterranean coast at the tip of Africa. They hold the European Union’s only land borders with Africa.

Andy Burnham, called the scenes a “cause for concern” as the shadow home secretary Chris Philp warned Spain’s border crisis could “rapidly become our border crisis”.

The incident has also sparked a diplomatic row across Europe with Italy’s prime minister Giorgia Meloni suspending the EU's border-free Schengen arrangements with Spain

Thousands of people were seen attempting to breach the border by land and sea by swimming around coastal barriers and forcing their way through land-border infrastructure. It is one of the most significant breaches of the territory’s border in years.

Rachid Sbihi, head of the association representing Guardia Civil officers in Ceuta, described the scenes as “absolute chaos” and said the border had “totally collapsed”. He said the event was a “humanitarian crisis”.

open image in gallery Many of the migrants have been sent back after the border breach ( AFP/Getty )

Spain has deployed police and military personnel to deal with the crisis and promised that those involved will be sent back to Morocco.

On Friday, authorities confirmed that half of the migrants had already returned, many of them voluntarily.

Moroccan forces used water cannons, batons and tear gas at the Ceuta gates to prevent more crowds storming the autonomous Spanish territory.

Mr Sanchez went on to blame gangs for the crisis, saying that they “deceive so many young people, and ultimately lead many of them to their deaths, whether in the ocean or, as in this case, at Spain’s border in the autonomous city of Ceuta”.

Right-wing leaders in Europe were quick to condemn the incident, urging tighter controls of EU borders.

open image in gallery Migrants sit on rocks after swimming through the waters close to the border with Morocco ( AFP/Getty )

open image in gallery Children were among the crowds trying to make it across the border ( AFP/Getty )

Ms Meloni said that the “striking” images confirmed that “uncontrolled illegal immigration poses a concrete threat to the security of Europe’s borders”.

“Italy will not stand by and watch,” she wrote. “We are convening the relevant bodies, and following these meetings, we are prepared to intervene with extraordinary measures to defend the borders and the safety of citizens, including the suspension of the Schengen area with Spain.

“On illegal immigration, we will not yield an inch: defending the borders, stopping human traffickers, and ensuring effective repatriations will continue to be the line of this government.”

open image in gallery Spain’s leader Pedro Sanchez has called the breach an attack on the country’s territorial integrity ( Reuters )

France’s far-right politician Marine Le Pen accused the Spanish government of “encouraging” the crisis.

“Faced with the massive and coordinated influx of migrants into Spain, encouraged by the Spanish government, France must without delay strengthen controls at its borders,” she wrote in a post on X.

“And in 2027, we will put an end to this madness by reserving Schengen free movement for EU nationals.”

President of the EU Commission Ursula von der Leyen called for the swift return of migrants to Morocco, while German chancellor Friedrich Merz said: “The protection of the EU’s external borders is crucial for combating illegal migration.

“I support Spain’s intention not to allow illegal migrants onto the European continent. The EU’s Return Directive must now be implemented without delay.”

The surge is reportedly linked to a recent ruling by Spain’s supreme court, which concluded that migrants intercepted at sea while attempting to reach Ceuta or Melilla cannot be deported or returned back under new rules. The decision does not apply to crossings by land.

Mr Sanchez said that the ruling had been misinterpreted.

“It appears that this interpretation of the Supreme Court’s ruling spread like wildfire over the past few hours through the networks of human trafficking organisations, triggering the kind of mass surge we witnessed yesterday,” he said.

Juan Jesus Vivas, mayor-president of Ceuta, called on the government to declare a national emergency. The interior ministry rejected the calls on the grounds that migration did not constitute a national emergency, but vowed to provide additional resources.

Opposition leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo described the situation as a “national security crisis” and urged the government to take stronger action.

Chancellor John Healey has told cabinet ministers they must prepare for spending cuts to finance Andy Burnham’s new policy pledges.

The directive follows Mr Healey’s announcement that his first Budget, set for 28 October, will be "built on fiscal discipline".

Mr Burnham’s premiership has seen a succession of costly announcements, including cost of living measures such as a cut in VAT on electricity bills and reduced business rates for pubs.

Further plans involve radical devolution across England and an expansion of technical training in schools.

Ministers have been informed, via a joint letter from the chancellor and the prime minister, that no new money is available for these initiatives.

“We’ve written to the cabinet to say that if we’re serious about new priorities as a second-stage Labour government we have to be serious about – and they have to be serious about – reprioritisation of their plans, their budgets,” Mr Healey told The Times.

open image in gallery Healey will face significant challenges as he attempts to find more money for Burnham’s devolution priorities ( PA )

“They need to pay for the new things they want to do this year and next year within the budgets they’ve already got.”

In the letter, he wrote that departments need to be “disciplined on spending, looking at the tough choices and being ready to shift funding away from unproductive or legacy programmes that no longer reflect this administration’s priorities”.

Mr Healey will face significant challenges as he attempts to find more money for Mr Burnham’s devolution priorities and increased defence spending amid warnings the Iran war will further squeeze the public finances.

He will also have to set out how the government will fund £5bn of defence spending announced in May’s Defence Investment Plan (Dip) without details of how it would be paid for.

He will come under pressure to increase that funding further, having resigned as defence secretary ahead of publication of the Dip, arguing it did not provide enough money for the armed forces.

He would not commit to raising defence spending to 3 per cent of GDP by 2030, but suggested it could form part of next year’s spending review.

“At the spending review, we will set out a clear path to meeting our 3.5 per cent Nato commitment in 2035 and we will set a target date on that path for 3 per cent,” he told The Times.

Earlier, he said the Budget would “meet our fiscal rules” and “give businesses and families some of the stability they need to plan for the future”.

Looking back at Mr Burnham’s first two weeks as prime minister, Mr Healey said the new government was “working fast to restore hope and back Britain’s communities” and had “begun to kickstart growth in every postcode”.

Experts have warned Mr Healey that he will need to raise taxes or cut spending elsewhere as pressure on the public finances has left no room for extra borrowing.

The National Institute of Economic and Social Research (Niesr) said on Wednesday the conflict in Iran would mean more persistent inflation and higher interest rates.

open image in gallery Experts have warned that Healey will need to raise taxes or cut spending elsewhere ( PA )

Stephen Millard, Niesr’s deputy director for macroeconomics, suggested Mr Healey should look at the welfare bill or the pensions triple lock as areas for potential cuts.

He also suggested Mr Healey should consider raising income tax, which would break Labour’s 2024 manifesto pledge not to raise that levy, national insurance or VAT.

That pledge, along with the fiscal rules set by former chancellor Rachel Reeves on borrowing, are likely to constrain Mr Healey’s room for manoeuvre.

In a letter to Commons Treasury Committee chair Dame Meg Hillier, the chancellor stressed his commitment to fiscal discipline.

He said: “Fiscal credibility is the bedrock of economic stability and national security.

“That is why we will abide by the fiscal rules, ensuring we retain a buffer to protect us against uncertainty and the impact of instability in the Middle East.”

In her last Budget, Ms Reeves left a £22bn buffer against her fiscal rules, but persistent inflation due to the Iran war could have eaten away at this.

Shadow chancellor Sir Mel Stride said the announcement of the Budget date meant “89 more days of unfunded spending commitments and damaging tax speculation until we get some details”, and “89 more days for Brits to wait before they know how much their taxes are going to go up to fund Burnham’s spending addiction”.

He added: “Only the Conservatives have a plan to cut spending by £50bn starting with the welfare bill, so we can cut taxes, lower your bills and back business to deliver a stronger economy and a stronger country.”

Thousands of Marvel-themed popcorn buckets sold at movie theaters nationwide have been recalled due to a risk of serious injury or death to kids.

Popcorn buckets for blockbuster films have become all the rage with people collecting and even reselling them. The comedically shaped buckets often make sounds and light up, which can be fun for kids but also a potential danger that parents should be aware of.

The popcorn bucket offered to superhero fans during the release of Captain America: Brave New World last year was recalled Thursday by the global cinema concessions company Golden Link.

Federal safety regulators warned that the light-up helmet-shaped souvenirs contain button cell batteries that children can easily access.

If kids get to the small batteries, they could swallow them, causing serious injuries, including internal chemical burns, and even death, the Consumer Product Safety Commission warned in a new notice.

open image in gallery Thousands of Marvel-themed popcorn buckets sold at movie theaters nationwide have been recalled for a risk of serious injury or death to kids ( Getty Images )

open image in gallery The popcorn bucket themed around the 2025 film Captain America: Brave New World was recalled ( Consumer Product Safety Commission )

Golden Link also recalled light-up Invisible Woman and Human Torch cups sold ahead of the release of The Fantastic Four: First Steps last summer over the same issue.

More than 55,000 of these popcorn buckets and cups were sold at AMC Theatres and lesser-known movie theaters, such as Harkins Theatres and GQT Movies.

There have been no reports of injuries linked to the recall as of Thursday, but parents are advised to throw away the popcorn buckets and cups. They can contact Golden Link for a refund via email at productrecall@goldenlinkinc.com.

The Independent has reached out to Golden Link for comment.

open image in gallery Parents have also been warned to throw away the cups that were sold ahead of The Fantastic Four: First Steps film released last summer ( Consumer Product Safety Commission )

open image in gallery The souvenirs contain button cell batteries that children can easily access, posing a risk if swallowed ( Consumer Product Safety Commission )

The Captain America and Fantastic Four souvenirs were recalled just as the latest movie in the Spider-Man franchise came out. Spider-Man: Brand New Day was released Friday, and, of course, there is a collectable all-in-one popcorn bucket and drink cup for it.

This souvenir holds your popcorn in a translucent plastic web that shoots out of Spider-Man’s glove, which serves as a vessel for your soda. There appear to be no light-up or sound-making features included in the souvenir, which is selling for about $50.

open image in gallery More than 55,000 of these popcorn buckets and cups were sold at AMC Theatres and lesser-known movie theaters ( Consumer Product Safety Commission )

AMC Theatres estimates that it will make a staggering $100 million in revenue from collectible popcorn buckets this year, The New York Times reported.

“Seven years ago, this business effectively didn’t exist for AMC,” Nels Storm, the company’s vice president of food and beverage product strategy, told the publication.

“I would never suggest that popcorn buckets are the reason people go to the movies, or that movie-themed merch is saving the industry, but over the last few years they’ve become a big part of the conversation around major releases,” Storm added.

News.title: Battle rages over access to new ‘miracle’ HIV drug
News.content:
For the first time in the four-decade fight against HIV there is a “miracle” drug that can all but eliminate the risk of infection, but in the Latin American countries where it was tested almost no one can get it.

Trials show that Lenacapavir, made by Gilead Sciences, is almost 100 per cent effective in preventing HIV infection. With just two shots a year, those taking it will avoid contracting the virus even when frequently exposed.

The drug, which many believe could bring an end to the global HIV pandemic, costs $14,000 a dose in the United States. Gilead has agreed to licence generic versions of the pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) medication at around $40 a dose in 120 low-and middle-income countries, but almost all of Latin America is excluded.

Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Peru are among those with serious HIV epidemics that are shut out, despite having run some of the clinical trials that proved the drug works.

Their status as “upper-middle income countries” means they are too rich to qualify for the cut price generic version and yet they remain too poor to pay the US price.

News.title: Senior dating: a guide to finding love later in life
News.content:
Whether you’re a widow, widower or divorcee, the thought of online dating in later life can feel daunting. However, more and more people are turning to the internet to find romance. Roughly 16 per cent of UK adults are using online dating services to meet a partner, according to Statista. Among them, there are lots of singles over 50 using dating sites.

So here’s how to navigate your senior dating online, with expert advice from psychologist and dating coach Dr Pam Spurr, and sex and relationship coach Angela Vossen.

How do I know if I'm ready to date again as a senior?

Coming out of any relationship is hard. If you’re hoping to date after a divorce, bereavement or break up, it can take a long time to feel ready to date again. Dr Spurr advises taking your time.

“Many people feel bruised, even traumatised, after coming out of a long-term relationship or having been bereaved,” she explains. “Your feelings naturally vary from day to day about whether you're ready to get back out to look for love – or even for fun. A crucial factor is if you've come to the point where you have more good days compared to bad days”.

Dr Spurr explains that good days are the days on which you feel more optimistic about life generally, and you find your thoughts turning to meeting someone new. “That's an important sign that you are healing,” she says. “However, if you're still feeling deeply insecure or are riddled with self-doubt about your worthiness, take your time. When you feel worthy, you will find someone worthy of you”.

Feeling heartbroken? Learn how to get over a break up

How to start senior dating online

If you’re new to online dating, it can feel intimidating at first. The secret is taking things step by step so that you do things at your own pace. The first step, however, should be choosing a senior dating site that will help match you with like-minded people. This will narrow your search and ensure your dating experience is more successful.

Step 1: Create an online profile

Once you’ve decided on a dating site or app and signed up, you’ll be asked to write a dating profile. This should reflect who you are along with your passions, values and what you seek in a partner.

Try to be authentic rather than creating a fantasy version of yourself. If you exaggerate your accomplishments, your date will only feel deceived once they get to know you. Likewise, don’t be tempted to use a photo of yourself from 10 years ago.

What are you waiting for? |  Single and looking to find true love? Sign up today for Telegraph Dating and join more than 220,000 like-minded people. Join today

Step 2: Spark meaningful chats with potential dates

Once you have signed up to a senior dating site and created a profile, you will be free to start looking at other people’s profiles and sending messages to anyone that catches your attention. But how can you initiate a conversation after an introduction?

“When messaging people on dating sites, ask open-ended questions to spark meaningful chats,” says Angela. A good example would be, ‘I can see you enjoy travel. What place have you always wanted to visit but haven’t yet?’ or “tell me more about your love of tennis? Did you watch the US Open?” If things go really well and the chat seems to flow naturally, you may decide to organise a phone chat or ask them out on a date. An initial chat over the phone can help gauge how well you get on and how easily the conversation flows. If this goes well, meeting in person may feel less nerve wracking and a little less ‘blind’.

Step 3: Prioritise your safety

“While most people are well intentioned online, it’s important to protect your safety,” advises Ms Vossen. “Keep personal details private (like where you live or your social media profiles) until you’ve met in person and built trust”. You should also arrange first dates in public places, share your plans with a friend, and trust your instincts if something feels off.

If the first date or two doesn’t quite hit the mark, try not to be too disappointed and remember that you can say no to another date. Ms Vossen says: “Be patient – online dating takes time, but with practice, you’ll gain confidence and enjoy the journey”.

Traditional ways to meet senior singles

Of course, couples continue to meet in a manner that predates online dating sites. If you’re keen to join the older dating scene but find the online world overwhelming, there are plenty of ways to meet people in real life.

1. Holidays and group trips

We are often our best selves on holiday, so it’s the ideal place to find a single senior woman or to meet men if the opportunity presents itself. Why not organise a trip on which you meet new people while doing what you love, whether that’s cycling, walking, sightseeing or just travelling around a new part of the world. There are many escorted tours that cater to specific age groups and interests. They also take away the stress of organising a trip yourself.

“An organised holiday or trip can be a great place to meet someone new and there are many organisations offering these for the over 50s,” says Dr Spur. “A word of caution though, you can spend a lot of money and there's no guarantee that you will meet that special person. However, if it's a place you've wanted to travel to then go with the mindset that you're going to have a great trip. If you meet someone, that's an added bonus”.

2. Activities and social groups

Whether you enjoy walking, reading or volunteering, taking up a new hobby or joining a social group is a great way to enhance your social life and increase your chances of meeting a new romantic interest.

“Joining a club or taking up a hobby can be a fantastic way of meeting singles who enjoy the same pastimes,” says Dr Spur. “You're doing an activity you enjoy knowing that there might also be someone there that will catch your eye”.

If you do meet someone that you’re interested in at a social event, Dr Spur advises starting with a simple ‘hello’ and an easy question such as how long they've been doing that particular activity or hobby. “This can open-up a friendly conversation that might lead to flirting down the line,” she says.

Start online dating for seniors today

Whichever way you decide to start looking for love, approach it in a way that you feel comfortable with. Signing up to an online dating service is a great way to meet other seniors. Remember, it’s never too late to begin a new chapter.

News.title: UK economy to flatline, warns Bank of England
News.content:
Britain’s economy is set to almost grind to a halt for the rest of the year, the Bank of England has warned.

Growth will drop to just 0.1pc per quarter, the Bank predicted, slowing sharply after a strong start to 2026.

Higher petrol prices and energy bills, a weak jobs market and rising mortgage costs are all draining confidence and spending power from the economy.

Inflation, which slowed to a 15-month low of 2.6pc in June, is also expected to rise again to 3.2pc later this year, the Bank warned.

Andrew Bailey, the Bank’s Governor, said inflation had “fallen faster than we’d expected” but warned that war in the Middle East would lead to a fresh spike.

He added that growth would “weaken slightly further in the near term as the effects of the conflict weigh further on demand”.

The Bank also predicted that unemployment will rise back above 5pc in the coming months, limiting workers’ ability to ask for higher wages to cope with rising living costs.

It presents a challenging backdrop for Andy Burnham and his Chancellor, John Healey, who have pledged to help voters struggling with the cost of living.

The forecasts came as policymakers led by Mr Bailey held interest rates at 3.75pc.

Although three members of the nine-strong Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) voted for higher rates, up from two at the previous meeting, the Governor dismissed suggestions the Bank is moving towards higher interest rates.

The public should “not… [think] the Bank of England is edging towards a hike,” Mr Bailey said.

“Frankly there is nothing I have said, or any of us have said, along those lines. We took a decision today to leave the Bank Rate unchanged and that is the relevant conclusion.”

Clare Lombardelli, a Deputy Governor, said voting to keep rates at 3.75pc “was not a close judgement”, calling the decision “pretty clear” given slowing inflation in the domestic economy.

Officials are monitoring the economy for any signs that increases in oil, gas and petrol prices caused by the war in Iran are creeping into higher costs and wages in the wider economy.

Mr Bailey said: “The possibility of repeated resumptions of conflict, combined with lower than usual European gas stock levels and a fall in global refining output, mean that risks to energy prices lie to the upside.”

He added: “Reassuringly, there are few signs so far that second-round effects are generating more broad-based inflationary pressures.”

Companies are struggling to pass higher costs on to their customers because of the economy’s weakness, he added.

Workers are typically securing only modest pay rises as the weak jobs market leaves them in a poor position to push for bigger salaries.

Mr Bailey stressed there are still major risks to the outlook given the war and promised to “monitor the situation carefully” and was “ready to adjust our stance”.

“It is our job to ensure that inflation gets back to the 2pc target and stays there, and that is what we will do,” he said.

Borrowing costs dropped in financial markets after the decision.

The Government’s two-year borrowing cost fell from 4.44pc to 4.34pc, the sharpest fall in a month.

The FTSE 250 index of mid-sized UK companies rose 0.8pc to a record high of 24,184.10.

Traders still believe the Bank will raise interest rates twice within a year.

However, Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said rate rises “remain more a threat than a reality”.

He said there was evidence of disinflation in the economy and interest rates could be “cut to 3pc in 2027”, adding: “That’s very different to market pricing for rates to be close to 4.5pc in 2027.”

News.title: Arsonists torch more Ebola clinics as misinformation spirals in DRC
News.content:
Two more Ebola treatment facilities have reportedly been burned down in recent days as health officials struggle to overcome violent public mistrust of medical teams.

At least a dozen facilities have now been attacked since Congo declared its Ebola outbreak amid fear, misinformation and suspicion of outside authorities.

The outbreak is the fastest growing on record and officials said the virus had now killed more than 1,500 people.

The official death toll from the outbreak centred on the north eastern Ituri province of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has risen by 500 in only a week.

Sources told the Telegraph the large jump in deaths was largely caused by a “data harmonisation exercise” between different regions, and the new deaths may not have all happened in the past week.

However, the daily confirmed toll has also continued to climb sharply with the latest government update reporting 50 people dying in the previous 24 hours.

Airfinity, a health analytics firm, said the outbreak “continues to outpace detection and the response” and there is a high chance of it spreading further inside DRC.

News.title: Race for vaccine against new Ebola strain gets $8.5m boost
News.content:
The “most promising” vaccine to tackle the Ebola strain behind an explosive outbreak in the Congo has been given an $8.5 million boost, as researchers race to develop an effective shot.

So far at least 3,360 people have been infected and 1,487 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), in an epidemic triggered by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola.

But unlike past outbreaks of the more common Zaire strain, there are currently no approved vaccines to tackle Bundibugyo.

On Thursday, the Coalition of Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (Cepi) revealed up to $8.5 million of funding for the only single-dose inoculation, which was described as the “most promising vaccine candidate” by the World Health Organization (WHO) in an analysis in May.

It is being developed by researchers at Hilleman Laboratories – a unique partnership between the pharmaceutical giant Merck and the British philanthropic powerhouse Wellcome, which is headquartered in Singapore.

The vaccine candidate is a Bundibugyo version of the Ervebo shot, which was created by Merck (MSD in Europe) and has already been approved for Ebola Zaire.

It uses a rVSV platform, where a modified version of VSV virus is used to train the immune system to react to target pathogens – in this instance, the Bundibugyo species replaces Zaire.

News.title: AMR chatbot could prevent drug-resistant infections in African hospitals
News.content:
A phone-based chatbot advising medics how to prescribe antibiotics has helped raise the quality of care in African hospitals and should stop bugs developing dangerous resistance, developers say.

Staff at four hospitals across Zambia and Kenya have been using two digital tools in a pilot project to try to address one of the world’s biggest health threats.

Anti-microbial resistance (AMR) is caused by germs evolving so that medicines such as antibiotics designed to kill them no longer work.

The menace is linked to nearly five million deaths each year and makes it increasingly difficult to treat infections. The annual death toll could nearly double in the next 25 years, according to some forecasts.

The rise in AMR is being significantly driven by the misuse and overuse of antimicrobials in human medicine and in agriculture.

Using antibiotics when they are not necessary, using the wrong ones, or getting the dosage wrong, all add to the chances that bugs will develop resistance.

With a shortage of new drugs in the development pipeline, one push to defeat AMR has been to get medics to stick to existing prescription, dosage and treatment advice.

The Antibiotic Stewardship Programme through Innovation, Research, and Education (ASPIRE) is trying to give them guidance using technology they already have in their pockets.

News.title: Tottenham new boys score in shoot-out win over Sydney FC
News.content:
Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

There was another impressive showing from 17-year-old prospect Luca Williams-Barnett, who is pushing for first-team opportunities this upcoming season.

Penalties followed the final whistle, with Spurs scoring all four of their spot kicks. Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, signed on a free transfer this summer, saved one and Sydney FC’s Josh Lacey hit the post to give Spurs the spoils 4-2.

News.title: Recovery aids and building muscle: Welsh weightlifter Laura Hughes answers your questions
News.content:
Laura Hughes first discovered weightlifting while training at her local Crossfit gym, making the transition from amateur gym-goer to competitive lifting.

Now a member of the Welsh national weightlifting squad, the 33-year-old holds the Welsh record for both the snatch and the clean and jerk (the two official competitive lifts in weightlifting) and is currently third overall in the women’s Welsh rankings. Hughes won bronze at this year’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, following on from her third place at the 2018 Games in Australia.

We caught up with her for our Readers Ask series, where industry specialists answer questions from our Telegraph Recommended Reader Panel.

Who inspired you to get into weightlifting?

Olamilekan, South East

Originally, it was lots of different people, particularly general gym goers who were doing weightlifting at my gym. As I’ve grown as an athlete and become more competitive, I’ve had other inspirations.

Most notably, coming into [the Commonwealth Games], it has to be Gareth [Evans], our coach. Looking back at his performance in 2018 when he won his gold medal is so inspiring. [English lifter] Emily Godley was another competitor in 2018. She won the gold medal in my category and I just remember thinking that she was on fire that day.

What are the best exercises for you to build muscle mass?

Norman, Wales

We spend a lot of time doing our main lifts, so snatches, clean and jerks, but we also do lots of pulls and squats. I spend a lot of time doing accessory work to make sure that my body stays healthy, especially being an older athlete. I’ve put on quite a lot of muscle in this last block just from going heavier and pushing my limits with my main lifts.

What advice would you give to people who want to improve their strength?

David, North West

The most important thing is consistency. As long as you’re doing something, do it regularly, even if it’s twice a week. Don’t be afraid of picking up some dumbbells. If you’ve got somebody that can teach you how to lift weights properly, that’s going to be the best option. Do it safely, do it consistently, and don’t be afraid to try new strength exercises.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes is ‘plug-and-play’ midfielder transfer in Declan Rice mould who can help Arsenal win it all
Sports.content:
BRUNO GUIMARAES will help get Arsenal dancing to a different beat.

The Gunners relied on defensive steel to win the Prem last season but Mikel Arteta is aware of the need to evolve.



And what better way than by adding some Samba flair to the mix?

Midfield ace Guimaraes — set to join from Newcastle — certainly offers that.



And, who knows, there could be even more if Arsenal pull off a sensational swoop for his Brazil team-mate Vinicius Jr.

A mega-money deal for the Real Madrid winger looks very hard to do, yet Emirates chiefs at least hope to get Guimaraes through the door.

A deal for the Newcastle captain, 28, is at an advanced stage and he should arrive for a fee north of £70million.

That is a serious outlay but it makes sense after boss Arteta’s midfield struggles last season. Declan Rice and Martin Zubimendi were run into the ground and there is a clear need for reinforcements in that area.

Guimaraes brings something different to the party and will not be afraid to put his mark on this Arsenal team after becoming a leader at Newcastle.

The midfielder has developed the attacking part of his game since moving to Toon from Lyon in January 2022.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Last season was his most productive and the Brazilian finished it with nine league goals and five assists.

Viktor Gyokeres was the only Arsenal player who bettered that tally — with 14 Prem goals and a solitary assist.

The Gunners lacked an attacking threat from midfield on their way to winning the title but they struggled for creativity, too. Guimaraes showed with his four assists for Brazil at the World Cup this summer how he can help in this area.

That came off the back of a season where he created 45 Prem chances, with Rice and Bukayo Saka the only two Gunners to better that.



But no one in Arteta’s ranks could compete with Guimareas when it came to through balls and passes completed in the final third.

The latter has been a real problem for Arsenal, who especially struggle when teams sit deep.

Guimaraes is excellent at receiving the ball in tight spaces and can help pick the lock of stubborn defences.

His arrival can ease the creative burden on captain Martin Odegaard, who he might play alongside as a No 8.



Rice operating behind the pair would give the champions a solid base and the England star could easily dovetail with Guimaraes — adding attacking fluidity.

The Toon hero is set to join a handy Brazilian contingent at the Emirates — which includes Gabriel Jesus, Gabriel and Gabriel Martinelli. He would also be the latest in a long line of Samba stars to represent Arsenal, following in the footsteps of World Cup winner Gilberto Silva.

The midfielder was a bedrock of that Invincibles side in 2003-04, like fellow countryman Edu — who sparked Arsenal’s interest in Guimaraes.

Edu looked at bringing the midfielder to the Emirates six years ago when working as the club’s technical director.



Guimaraes was playing at Athletico Paranaense then and Arsenal continued to track him when he joined Lyon.

Finally, the playmaker looks on his way to North London — and his hunger to win trophies should prove infectious.

If Arteta was wary about anyone resting on their laurels after title glory, throwing in someone with Guimaraes’ fighting spirit will put paid to that.

And that is the attractive thing about the midfielder — who is able to combine Brazilian flair with English grit.



Per 90 minutes in the top flight last season, he won more duels and tackles than any Arsenal player. Arteta will love that because — as much as there is a need to liven up the Gunners’ attack — the Spaniard is never going to fully abandon his core principles.

Hard work is a huge part of that, and Guimaraes offers it in spades at a time when Arsenal want to kick on with their project.

Arteta is hungry for more success and conscious of the fact the club have never retained the Prem.

The Champions League remains an elusive prize, too, and the heartbreak of last season’s final shootout defeat to Paris Saint-Germain will serve as fuel.



Signing the experienced Guimaraes is an indication of how Arsenal want to win now, not simply build for the future.

The last time they spent this much on a midfielder was three years ago, when they paid West Ham £105m for Rice.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Arsenal chief Josh Kroenke called Rice a “plug-and-play” signing who could hit the ground running straight away.

If a deal gets over the line, Guimaraes will be expected to do the same.

Sports.title: Fifa ‘scrap Infantino’s £15BILLION flogging of World Cup to private investors’ after world of football erupts in anger
Sports.content:
FIFA are set to scrap its hated plan to flog the World Cup amid global fury, according to reports.

Gianni Infantino‘s bid to sell off a chunk of a new sister company in charge of the World Cup has collapsed following Uefa’s boycott promise and a “brand nightmare” for potential investors.



On Tuesday it emerged that Infantino wanted to create a subsidiary called the Fifa Forward Enterprise, which would have presided over money-making assets including the World Cup.

Fifa valued the new branch at £15bn, and was hoping to sell a 20 per cent stake for £3.1bn.



Thrive Capital, led by Joshua Kushner, Donald Trump‘s son-in-law Jared Kushner‘s brother, had been a front-runner to bid, with JPMorgan onboard in an advisory role.

But according to the New York Post the “deal is dead” – with a source telling them of Kushner’s group: “They are not feeling this. There is no way they want to continue to be involved in this mess.

“Kushner will figure out another way to get involved in this space. This is becoming a brand nightmare.”

Uefa chief Aleksander Ceferin strongly opposed Fifa’s project from the start.

And on Thursday, Uefa’s 55 member associations, including England, agreed to boycott the World Cup should the Fifa Forward Enterprise come to fruition.

Fifa attempted to hang on to its plan, dangling £30m payments to its member associations should it be approved by September 19.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

But Uefa’s boycott promise tanked the value of Fifa’s proposed deal – with Europe’s huge markets driving significant commercial interest from TV, sponsors and fans.

Concacaf and the AFC also publicly revealed their opposition to Infantino’s money-making vision, providing a further nail in its coffin.

Early on Friday Infantino was rocked by the resignation of one of his most senior advisers, Carlos Cordeiro.

The former US Soccer president told Sky News: “As a senior adviser to the Fifa president, a former banker, and a lifelong football fan, I cannot stand by while Fifa considers selling a stake in the World Cup.



“Let me be clear: I had no involvement in this proposal, and I oppose it unequivocally.

“It is a bad deal for Fifa’s Member Associations, a bad deal for football, and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game.”

Sports.title: Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha ‘set for stunning transfer U-turn’ despite already being ANNOUNCED by new club
Sports.content:
CAPE VERDE star Vozinha is set for a massive transfer U-turn by snubbing a famous club that already announced his arrival.

The 40-year-old goalkeeper made headlines this summer by leading his underdog country to an historic campaign that saw them picking up famous draws against world champions Spain, Uruguay and Saudi Arabia.



The keeper’s incredible saves led Cape Verde to the play-offs of their first World Cup appearance and came close to stunning Argentina at extra-time before falling heroically in a 3-2 defeat.

Vozinha’s stunning displays between the sticks earned him a place in the World Cup’s team of the tournament alongside superstars like Lionel Messi, Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappe.



And that led to a call-up from Chilean giants Colo-Colo who have been close to signing him as a free agent following his departure from Chaves in June.

According to journalist Raphael Bozeo, however, Moroccan outfit Berkane are set to hijack the deal.



That is despite the fact Colo-Colo already announced Vozinha‘s arrival at the Monumental last week.

However, the Cape Verde international postponed his arrival in Santiago three different times and thus caused uncertainty about his move.

Vozinha was initially expected to arrive in Chile on Tuesday before the flight was rescheduled for Wednesday.

But plans changed again and the shot-stopper was expected on Thursday but nothing came of it.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

And Berkane are now expected to swoop in amid reports suggesting they have also agreed with Vozinha’s Cape Verde manager Bubista to take over as their new head coach.

The same source now claims Vozinha is expecting an official offer from the Moroccans.

This comes after it was revealed the goalie won’t be allowed to don his famous nickname on the back of his shirt with Colo-Colo as per Chilean football rules.

Vozinha, whose birth name is Josimar Jose Evora Dias, will instead have to choose between ‘Evora’, ‘Dias’ or ‘Evora Dias’.

Sports.title: Footie club launch new kit with a THOUSAND sponsors in bid to head off financial crisis
Sports.content:
FOUR-TIME national champions Deportivo Municipal are trying to avoid bankruptcy in truly unique style.

The fallen Peruvian giants have unveiled a new kit plastered with a mind-blowing 1,000 sponsors, raising over £220,000 in the process.



An impending threat of financial liquidation forced the Lima-based outfit to think outside the box, and the top brass responded by turning their shirt into an advertising hoarding.

The hyper-commercial kit marks a new, visually striking chapter in the club’s current off-field firestorm.



As recently as 2017, Deportivo Municipal were going toe-to-toe with South America’s finest in the Copa Libertadores, and the side were still in the domestic top flight just three years ago.

But the debt-saddled club were subsequently dealt a slew of points deductions which saw them relegated to the second division for the 2023/24 season.

Barely a year later, ‘Muni’ were banished to Liga 3 after being unable to fork up the funds for their license to the Peruvian Football Federation.

Earlier this year, their situation reached a new level of desolation when they were disqualified from the professional pyramid and consigned to the Copa Perú.

Before this snazzy new design, Deportivo sported a minimalist shirt, featuring a classy white base emblazoned with a red sash.

While Austrian Bundesliga side Hartberg once made headlines for having 23 sponsors splashed across their kit – including a sperm-boosting brand.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The iconic Peruvian club have now blown that figure out the water.

The astonishing shirt is a unique and desperate fundraising attempt, after dire finances forced the club to carve their kit into 1,000 advertising squares and launch the ‘Los Mil Sponsors del Muni’ (The Thousand Sponsors of Muni’) campaign in January.

Local businesses were quick to snap up the miniature slots, listed for 200 Peruvian soles apiece (roughly £44), selling out the commercial venture within three months.

Muni’s plethora of new backers includes nearby wineries and pet shops, all keen to pump life into the sinking club.



Despite the short-term cash injection and international media storm their kit has whipped up, Deportivo Municipal were knocked out of the Copa Perú last weekend in a bitter blow to their attempted renaissance.

Sports.content:
Chelsea and FA drop Mykhailo Mudryk statement

Mykhailo Mudryk will now be available to play for Chelsea. A statement from the FA confirmed the news, saying: "The FA can confirm that the anti-doping disciplinary proceedings against Mykhailo Mudryk were resolved with the agreement of the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) on 30 July 2026.

"In the context of that agreement, Mr Mudryk has accepted his commission of Anti-Doping Rule Violations (ADRVs) and accepted a period of ineligibility. On 22 October 2024, Mr Mudryk was subject to an out-of-competition doping control, which revealed the presence of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance.

"The FA notified Mr Mudryk of that finding on 4 December 2024 and imposed a provisional suspension. On 23 May 2025, The FA charged Mr Mudryk with ADRVs in breach of Regulations 3 and 4 of its 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations.

"On 7 to 9 January 2026, a hearing took place before an independent Regulatory Commission. The Regulatory Commission found that Mr Mudryk had committed the charged ADRVs and imposed a four-year period of ineligibility. Subsequently, Mr Mudryk filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

"Since then, changes have been made to WADA Technical Document (TD2027MRL) which, while not retroactive, mean that if Mr Mudryk's sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no ADRVs would have resulted.

"Further to that development and to other circumstances of the case, The FA and Mr Mudryk have now - with the agreement of WADA - resolved the appeal proceedings in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the World Anti-Doping Code and Regulation 90 of the 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations.

"As a part of the agreement, Mr Mudryk accepted that he had committed the Anti-Doping Rule Violations charged and acceded to a period of ineligibility equal to the time served at the date of the agreement. Mr Mudryk is no longer ineligible and may return to competition with immediate effect."

Chelsea also uploaded their own statement which said: "Chelsea FC acknowledges today's announcement by The Football Association confirming the resolution of the anti-doping proceedings involving Mykhailo Mudryk.

"From the outset, this has been an extremely difficult period for Misha, both professionally and personally, and we are pleased that the matter has now reached a conclusion which allows him to return to football with immediate effect.

"We have always supported Misha throughout this process while fully respecting the integrity of the anti-doping system and the legal process. We welcome the acknowledgement that advances in the applicable scientific reporting standards for more reliable testing mean that, had Misha's sample been analysed under today's technical requirements, it would not have been reported as a positive test and no anti-doping rule violation would have resulted.

"That is an important part of the context surrounding the agreed resolution and allows everyone involved to move forward. "Misha has consistently maintained that he never knowingly or intentionally used a prohibited substance and did not know how traces of the substance entered his system. Throughout this process he has conducted himself professionally and with resilience during what has undoubtedly been one of the most challenging periods of his career.

"We know how much this opportunity to return means to him. Our focus now is on supporting Misha’s reintegration into the squad and helping him resume his career. Chelsea FC remains fully committed to the highest standards of sporting integrity and compliance with all anti-doping regulations. Everyone at the Club now looks forward to helping Misha return to full fitness, back into the squad and back onto the pitch."

The Gunners have been actively pursuing a new attacking option this summer and were previously linked with Morgan Rogers, before the England international completed a £117million move to Chelsea from Aston Villa.

What ultimately awaits both Guimaraes and Vinicius remains to be seen, with both players currently enjoying their summer break following their participation with Brazil at the World Cup.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford has chance to 'hurt' Man Utd as two transfer moves proposed
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford has chance to 'hurt' Man Utd as two transfer moves proposed

Marcus Rashford is a Manchester United player on paper, but he has been widely expected to leave the Reds in the transfer window

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford is still facing an uncertain summer (Image: Icon Sportswire, Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

Manchester United have been warned not to sell Marcus Rashford to a Premier League rival. Rene Meulensteen, who was Sir Alex Ferguson's assistant manager at Old Trafford. He believes selling Rashford to the likes of Tottenham Hotspur could hurt the club.

‌



Spurs were recently linked with a £30million move for the England international, whose future at the club is uncertain. Barcelona chose not to sign him permanently, and no club has yet come forward with a meaningful offer for the Reds.

‌



Michael Carrick re-integrating him back into the squad is not impossible, but it's widely been believed both parties feel a clean break is best for everyone. If this is the case, Meulenseteen warned United not to sell to a Premier League rival.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Speaking to Andy's Bet Club, Meulensteen, when questioned whether the scenario might mirror United's choice to sell Scott McTominay, who has since flourished for Napoli, responded: "Would selling Marcus Rashford be a repeat of selling Scott McTominay?

"I don't think people see Scott McTominay the same way. He moved because the club wanted to sell, and he has done brilliantly since. People might wonder if United sold him too early.

‌



"But selling Marcus Rashford to a direct competitor like Arsenal or Chelsea could really hurt you. He is still a player who can make a difference. Ideally, if United sell him, they should sell him abroad."

View 3 Images Barcelona chose not to sign Rashford permanently (Image: Aitor Alcalde Colomer, Getty Images)

Meulensteen also suggested Saudi Arabia could be a potential destination or maybe even the MLS, saying: "Saudi Arabia could be an option for Rashford depending on what he wants," before adding: "Perhaps one of the other big clubs will sign him so he can keep playing in the Champions League. Or he might make a move to Saudi or maybe the MLS, who knows?"

‌



Meulensteen also urged Carrick to open up a dialogue with Rashford to gauge his state of mind and establish how he might contribute to the club. He said: "Michael Carrick is the type of person who recognises Marcus's qualities.

"They need an open conversation so Marcus understands what is required. Michael Carrick won't want to bring someone back if it creates another problem. If the clarity is there, he would be happy to bring him back into the fold.

View 3 Images Michael Carrick still has many options this summer (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



"However, with the other players available, there wouldn't be a guaranteed start every week. The fact that it is taking so long to find clarity suggests there is still something brewing in the background. If all parties were happy for him to come back, they would likely have made that clear very quickly."

When it comes to attacking options, United's primary weapons are Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo, Benjamin Sesko and Amad Diallo, with Bruno Fernandes and Mason Mount frequently operating in the pocket just behind the striker.

Patrick Dorgu was also reinvented as a left-winger under Carrick, chipping in with several crucial goals before an injury derailed his progress last season. United still have further pre-season friendlies remaining on the schedule.
