Chermiti and Dan Neil came on for Naderi and Djeidi Gassama as McInnes tried to affect the game at half-time and his side immediately looked more threatening.

Aasgaard forced an excellent diving save from Walton before the Norway international levelled moments later. Shankland’s physical presence caused problems as United were made to defend another high ball and Aasgaard took an excellent touch to take out Joshua Rawlins before firing a left-foot strike into the top corner from 16 yards.

Rangers could not keep up the momentum, and Randall squandered a glorious chance to mark his league debut with a famous winner. Chermiti almost made the home side pay but Walton stopped the striker’s effort with his feet before home substitute Idjessi Metsoko delivered a weak effort straight at Pandur from a decent opportunity.

Sports.title: Franco Baresi was not only the captain but the moral heart of great Milan team
Sports.content:
There are very few players who become bywords for their position, who enjoy universal acclaim. But for anybody who watched football in the late 80s or early 90s, Franco Baresi was the central defender. He was unsurpassed, obviously the best in his position in the world, the definition of the art of the defending. The oddity is, he really wasn’t like very many other defenders at all.

Baresi had just turned 19 when he won his first scudetto at Milan under Nils Liedholm. It was 1979 and Italian football was still dominated by the ideals of catenaccio. Most defences comprised a libero, two man-markers and, if you were lucky, an attacking left-back. But not Liedholm’s. The Swede was a pioneer in Serie A of zonal marking, and the idea that the game was not a series of physical battles but a question of space. Baresi was only 5ft 9in and a teenager. More traditional coaches might not have trusted him. But Liedholm saw an impeccable reader of the game, even at that age. Baresi was an ever-present, not only in the league but in the Coppa Italia and Uefa Cup as well.

That turned out to be a traumatic season for the club, with players arrested on the pitch after the final game of the season as part of the Totonero betting scandal, for which Milan were ultimately relegated. With the club in financial chaos, promotion was followed by another relegation and, although they were promoted again, the future seemed bleak before Silvio Berlusconi took over in 1986. Baresi remained loyal throughout. His parents died before he turned 16 and Milan became a sort of surrogate family.

He never played for any other club, amassing 719 appearances in all competitions over 20 years. And yet, he could easily have been an Inter player. Baresi’s brother Giuseppe, two years his elder, was already at Inter when Franco was offered a trial at the age of 14. Inter wondered if he was big enough to make it and asked him to come back the following year. So Franco went for a trial at Milan – which he insisted had always been his club – and was taken on.

Berlusconi was an outsider, determined to disrupt the establishment. In Arrigo Sacchi, who was appointed in 1987, he found a coach in the same vein: a radical who followed Liedholm’s tentative steps into the world of zonal marking with a giant leap into a full-blown flat back four and hard pressing. In the Serie A of the age it was almost unthinkably revolutionary. Conservatives were sceptical and, when Milan lost their second game of the season 2-0 at home to Fiorentina, and followed that up with defeat to Espanyol in the Uefa Cup and a disappointing draw against Cesena, the joke was that Berlusconi’s new messiah would not make All Saints’ Day, which is 1 November.

Form began to turn around, but Sacchi worried he had pushed the players too hard and eased back on training, at which point Baresi made a decisive intervention. He begged Sacchi to push the players even harder. It was vital, he said, that the players didn’t forget, that they came to learn the new way of playing, of working out their position not according to preset formulas but through constantly evolving reference to opponents, their teammates, the ball and the space, to internalise the processes until they became instinctive.

View image in fullscreen Franco Baresi (kneeling, second left) and his Milan teammates celebrate beating Steaua Bucharest 4-0 to win the 1989 European Cup, for many the high point of their football under Arrigo Sacchi. Photograph: PA Images/Alamy

For Sacchi, it was a huge moment. Baresi was not only the captain, but the moral heart of the team. If he was on board with the revolution, Sacchi realised, the squad would follow. Milan, with their ultra-modern style, won the scudetto in 1988 and backed it up with consecutive European Cup wins, playing some of the most memorable football ever witnessed. Baresi was central to it, not only snuffing out opposing forwards but constantly analysing and organising, and also initiating counterattacks. The clipped forward pass became a trademark, but his greatest skill was his pass selection. He just didn’t give the ball away.

His inspirations were creative players plus Ruud Krol, but Baresi was also tough. Gianfranco Zola called him the best defender he ever played against but observed that afterwards “your feet need loads of ice and anti‑inflammatories”. Baresi dished it out, as defenders in Serie A in those days had to, but he could also take it. He played more than an hour of a Milan derby in 1989 with a broken arm, helping keep a clean sheet, and, at the 1994 World Cup, managed to recover from knee surgery required after tearing his cartilage in the second group game in time to play in the final. Again, he oversaw a clean sheet but, cruelly, failed from the spot in the shootout as Italy lost to Brazil.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen A Milan fan lays flowers next to a shirt of former captain Franco Baresi at Casa Milan. Photograph: Daniele Mascolo/Reuters

International football never quite gave Baresi the highs the club game did. He was part of the World Cup-winning squad in 1982 but didn’t play a minute, and was part of squads that got to the last four of Euro 88 and Italia 90, but he never achieved the same glory with Italy that he did with Milan.

And so the memory of him will always be in the red-and-black shirt, anticipating the game, stepping implacably in front of an opponent, shrugging him off and clipping a perfectly weighted ball in to a forward’s feet, the defining image of Italy’s new era of defending.

Sports.title: Chelsea fined £10m and given suspended transfer ban by FA over agent breaches
Sports.content:
Chelsea have been fined £10m by the FA and served with a suspended transfer ban for multiple violations of transfer rules during the Roman Abramovich era.

The sanction reflects a similar punishment handed to the Blues by the Premier League earlier this year after the club were found to have used unlicensed agents and sought to obscure the nature of their transfer dealings between 2009 and 2022. Deals involving Chelsea legends Samuel Eto’o, Eden Hazard and Willian were among those found to have breached the rules. The commission originally handed down a stronger sanction that would have given Chelsea a suspended six-point deduction, but it was overturned after an appeal by the club.

The offences were self-reported by Chelsea when new ownership entered Stamford Bridge in 2022 and the disciplinary panel praised the club for their actions and cooperation through the hearing. Chelsea, who are also operating under a settlement agreement with Uefa, said they had “worked openly and transparently with all regulators” and were “pleased to confirm that this brings all regulatory proceedings against the club to a close”.

Written reasons published by the FA show the independent commission took a very dim view of the Abramovich-era administration, saying their rule-breaking showed “a shameful and arrogant disregard for the rules of the game … which has done so much to bring the game of football in general, and the name of CFC into disrepute”. They also said, however, that there were aspects of the case brought by the FA that caused them “particular concern”.

While praising the FA’s cooperation on the case, the commission criticised the governing body for both failing to charge individuals related to the misdemeanours and for requesting that a sporting sanction should not be applied as punishment. After a submission by the Premier League, which also argued against a sporting sanction, Chelsea appealed against the commission’s original sanction and the six-point deduction was replaced with a suspended two-window ban on registering new players. While the commission had originally argued Chelsea had sought and gained a sporting advantage from their actions, the appeal board found that there was insufficient evidence to show that any advantage had actually been achieved.

“Chelsea’s lawyers performed a masterclass in non-adversarial diplomacy with both the FA and the Premier League,” said Stefan Borson, a football finance expert who is head of sport at the law firm McCarthy Denning.

“Even where the FA’s independent panel disagreed with the position presented by the FA and Chelsea, it still found a way to discount a 15-point deduction starting point down to a six-point suspended penalty. Ultimately, even that was appealed away, leaving Chelsea to pay a final meagre fine out of its retained escrow from Abramovich’s proceeds.”

Quick Guide Mudryk cleared to resume playing Show Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk can return to playing immediately after the Football Association and the World Anti-Doping Agency “resolved his appeal” against a ban for failing a doping test. The Ukrainian was suspended for four years after failing a drug test which revealed the presence of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance, in 2024. Mudryk filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport while changes to Wada procedures in the interim mean that had his failed test produced the same result now, charges would not have been brought. The FA said: “Changes have been made … which, while not retroactive, mean that if Mr Mudryk’s sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no anti-doping rule violations [ADRVs] would have resulted. Further to that development and to other circumstances of the case, the FA and Mr Mudryk have now – with the agreement of Wada – resolved the appeal proceedings. “As a part of the agreement, Mr Mudryk accepted that he had committed the ADRVs charged and acceded to a period of ineligibility equal to the time served at the date of the agreement. Mr Mudryk is no longer ineligible and may return to competition with immediate effect.” PA Media Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

The Premier League and the FA had been examining tens of millions of pounds in secret payments made by offshore companies that were owned by Abramovich. Details of the transactions were uncovered as part of Cyprus Confidential, an investigation by the Guardian and international media partners, based on a leak of data from Cypriot financial services firms that the Russian oligarch used to manage his vast fortunes.

Deals revealed by the leak included apparent off-book payments to Hazard’s agent and an associate of the title-winning manager Antonio Conte.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Documents published as part of the finding offer a rare insight into the inner workings of Chelsea’s transfer policy during the tenure of Abramovich. They refer to internal conversations at Chelsea about the purchase of Willian in 2013, a deal agreed at the last minute, after the Brazilian had apparently been set to join London rivals Tottenham. According to the documents, an unnamed senior figure at Chelsea felt that to lose Willian was “not good” and that to lose him to Tottenham was “adding insult to injury”.

In its argument, the FA said the unnamed individual may have “loved the power associated with having a bottomless pocket when it came to acquiring players of great quality and/or with great potential, but to seek to suggest that there was no intention to obtain a sporting advantage is stretching our credulity beyond reasonable limits”.

The rulings published by the FA also reveal for the first time that BlueCo, the consortium that bought Chelsea from Abramovich, reached a multi-million pound settlement with HM Revenue & Customs relating to transactions dating back to 2011. The size of the settlement is redacted in the FA’s case against Chelsea but the appeal board’s decision indicated that the club repaid at least £1.35m.

The FA said that the entirety of Chelsea’s £10m fine will be invested into grassroots football.

Sports.title: Arsenal target Bruno Guimarães not on Newcastle’s flight to pre-season camp
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimarães was not on Newcastle’s flight to Murcia on Friday lunchtime as Eddie Howe’s former players prepared to meet their new head coach in southern Spain.

As Guimarães, who is believed to be in Brazil, appeared to inch closer towards a transfer to Arsenal, Matthias Jaissle was completing his managerial move from Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ahli. Howe’s successor is expected to arrive at the club’s pre-season training camp at La Manga at some point this weekend.

By the time, shortly after midday, when the team’s charter plane took off for the Mediterranean, Newcastle had still to provide formal confirmation of Howe’s departure. That did not arrive until late afternoon but it is understood they had been negotiating a financial settlement with their former manager in addition to payoffs for four key members of his backroom staff, including the outgoing No 2, Jason Tindall.

In an emotional message released as part of Newcastle’s statement, Howe said. “It has been the privilege of my lifetime to have been the manager of Newcastle United. After nearly five years of giving my life, heart and soul into this club with unrelenting energy I feel that it is in the best interests of both myself and the club to step away, recharge and take a break. Although it’s been incredibly difficult to make this decision, I know in my heart it’s the right one.”

The amicable nature of the parting was reflected in generous tributes paid by Newcastle’s chief executive David Hopkinson, sporting director Ross Wilson and minority owner, Jamie Reuben. The latter said: “I am proud to have worked alongside Eddie Howe and privileged to call him a friend.” Hopkinson said: “Eddie and his staff leave with the deep gratitude and respect of everyone at Newcastle United and a lasting place in the club’s history.”

Although Howe had told Newcastle of his intention to leave earlier this month, leaks surrounding Jaissle’s imminent installation appeared to catch all parties by surprise. The players had learned of their manager’s departure during a day off on Thursday but had the situation fully explained when Wilson addressed them at the training ground before heading to Spain alongside the squad.

At the same time, Newcastle’s incoming German head coach was understood to be finalising a four-year contract at St James’ Park after an £8m compensation package was agreed with Al-Ahli. Jaissle is already in Europe after remaining in Portugal rather than returning to Jeddah with his squad following the conclusion of a pre-season training camp on the Algarve on Wednesday.

View image in fullscreen Joelinton could be on his way to the Saudi Arabia league this summer. Photograph: Siu Wu/EPA

The 38-year-old former RB Salzburg manager is assembling his own backroom staff and now has only three weeks before his first Premier League season begins with a home game against Liverpool.

One of his first tasks will be to hold talks with Guimarães regarding the Brazil midfielder’s future. Guimarães – who was very close to Howe – is booked on a flight to Spain on Sunday but there are suggestions he could opt to board a London-bound plane instead, should Arsenal offer Newcastle a sum in the region of £75m.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Although Manchester United are exploring the possibility of signing Lewis Hall, Jaissle has reason to be more confident of keeping the influential left back. Newcastle are said to be determined to retain one of their best young players but could be more receptive to any bid from Saudi Arabia for Joelinton. Guimarães’s fellow Brazilian is believed to be keen on a move to the Middle East.

While Besiktas also covet another Newcastle midfielder, Joe Willock, Wilson appears close to securing a new goalkeeper. A £26m deal for the Braga and Czechia goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek is expected to be completed over the weekend.

Should that move for the 24-year-old progress as planned, Nick Pope, Newcastle’s current first-choice keeper, will almost certainly prove yet another departure during a turbulent summer featuring a major changing of the guard on Tyneside.

Sports.title: Who should win the men’s Ballon d’Or?
Sports.content:
Harry Kane

Seventy-three goals in 64 games for club and country – the second most prolific season by any player in history after Lionel Messi’s 82-goal campaign in 2011-12 – not bad for a man who once sat on the bench alongside Jamie Vardy in the Championship. Harry Kane was not a teenage prodigy like a few of the other players on this list but here he is crashing football’s top table at the age of 33.

It feels strange that a player who has scored at least 24 goals in each of the last 12 seasons, has won back-to-back Golden Boots in the Premier League, a World Cup Golden Boot and two European Golden Shoes, has never finished higher than 10th in Ballon d’Or voting.

The numbers were always there but now he is adding the silverware. Kane’s trophy drought ended when Bayern Munich won the Bundesliga last year and that triumph has opened the floodgates. Another Bundesliga title followed this season, alongside the DFB-Pokal and German Supercup.

England did not end their trophy drought at the World Cup but their captain scored six goals and overtook Gary Lineker as England’s top scorer at the tournament, ensuring he remained in contention for the Ballon d’Or.

Lamine Yamal

“It’s about being calm. When I’m in the area with the ball, I decide what happens,” said Lamine Yamal in February after he had scored the first hat-trick of his career in Barcelona’s 4-1 win against Villarreal. For most 19-year-olds this would sound like arrogance, but Yamal is not like most 19-year-olds.

He offered more proof of that this summer. The Spain forward became the first player to appear in a European Championship final and a World Cup final before turning 20 – and he won both. He only scored one goal at the World Cup, which was a modest return by his own lofty standards, but he was influential throughout. He won a gamechanging penalty in the semi-final against France, he made more successful take-ons than Messi across the tournament, and he had a hand in breaking down an Argentina side hellbent on baiting him into a physical duel in the final. He achieved all this after going into the tournament with a hamstring injury. Joe Hart captured the mood best after the final, saying: “Lamine Yamal is 19 years old. What a beautiful day for him. He’s 19 and has completed football.”

Add in the 24 goals and 18 assists he racked up in 45 appearances for Barcelona as they won La Liga and the Supercopa, and he has a strong case to go one better than his runners-up finish in last year’s Ballon d’Or.

Rodri

“We’ll see the real Rodri at the World Cup,” said Pep Guardiola last October, when the Manchester City captain returned to action after suffering an ACL injury. There were doubts that the 2023 Ballon d’Or winner would ever return to his best. But, as with most things in football, Guardiola was right.

Rodri was the heartbeat and the safety blanket in the Spain team, dictating every phase of the game, controlling possession and extinguishing almost every danger posed to his backline – Spain only conceded one goal in their eight matches at the tournament. Rodri completed 756 passes (more than anyone at the tournament) and he also topped the charts for touches, line-breaking passes and passes in the opposition third. In the final alone he completed 101 passes, completely strangling the life out of Argentina to the extent that they did not have a single shot on target.

He lifted the trophy as Spain’s captain, won the Golden Ball as the tournament’s best player and earned a place in one of football’s most exclusive clubs as only the fourth man in history to have won the World Cup, European Championship, European Cup and Ballon d’Or, joining Gerd Müller, Franz Beckenbauer and Zinedine Zidane.

Kylian Mbappé

Kylian Mbappé went toe-to-toe with his old Paris Saint-Germain teammate Lionel Messi at the World Cup. They battled it out for the trophy, the Golden Boot, the Golden Ball and a place in the history books as the competition’s all-time leading scorer. He won two of the four. His two goals in the third-place playoff against England ensured he became the first man to win the Golden Boot twice. It also brought him to 22 goals in World Cups – one more than Messi – and made him the first man to reach double figures in a single edition since Müller in 1970.

And yet, it was not what Mbappé wanted. “I would have preferred not to be the top scorer and to have played in the final,” said the France captain. His domestic season was also prolific but disappointing, bringing goals and individual glory but no silverware. He scored 42 goals in 44 appearances, finishing the season as the top scorer in La Liga and the Champions League, but he did not win either trophy. The goals flowed but the medals did not follow. As Kane has discovered, goals alone are rarely enough to win the Ballon d’Or.

View image in fullscreen Kylian Mbappé has scored 22 goals in 22 matches at World Cups. Photograph: Carlos Barría/Reuters

Lionel Messi

Lionel Messi sat on the floor alone in a stadium of 80,000 people, boots off, staring into the distance as Spain’s substitutes streamed past him in celebration. It was not the fairytale image the Argentina captain had envisioned as he left the world stage. And, given his performances over the previous six weeks, it felt as if he deserved better even if his team did not.

Some expected Messi’s tournament to be a nostalgia act – a former great wheeled out for one last World Cup as he prepares for his 40th birthday. But then he went and scored a hat-trick in Argentina’s first game. He scored twice against Austria, then added another against Jordan. He stamped his authority on the tournament in the group stage and proceeded to drag Argentina through the knockouts: a goal against Cape Verde, a goal and an assist against Egypt, an assist against Switzerland, and two more assists to sink England in the semi-final. Had it not been for Mbappé’s brace in a bizarre third-place playoff, he would have collected the Golden Boot.

Could he win the Ballon d’Or having lost the World Cup final? In only four of the last 19 years has the award gone to a player who did not win the Champions League, World Cup, European Championship or Copa América in the same year. But three of them were won by Messi. A ninth Ballon d’Or is unlikely but the fact he is in this conversation at all – at 39 while playing in MLS having lost a final – is testament to his greatness.

This is an article by WhoScored

Sports.title: Bayern Munich publicly put three players on transfer list including ex-Premier League star
Sports.content:
Joao Palhinha is among three players that Bayern Munich are willing to sell this summer.

Max Eberl, the director of sport at Bayern, has publicly revealed that the players are not part of their plans for the new season.

2 Palhinha is one of three players to be put up for sale by Bayern Credit: Getty

Ismael Saibari was their first summer signing in a reported €50million (£43m) move from PSV Eindhoven.

Bayern then bought Nathaniel Brown, who Manchester United had as a target, in a €55m (£47m) deal with Eintracht Frankfurt.

Players such as Leon Goretzka and Raphael Guerreiro have left at the end of their contracts, and others have gone on loan or permanently.

And according to Eberl, Bayern are keen to let another trio of players depart before the end of the window.

"We have three players we are open to letting go," he explained via @iMiaSanMia on X. "They have no future at Bayern.

"If they want to stay with us, it will be tough because we are not planning with them. Then they won't play a role.

"That's the case with Sacha Boey, Joao Palhinha and Bryan Zaragoza."

Who could Palhinha sign for?

After two solid seasons at Fulham, Palhinha joined Bayern in July 2024 and played a part in their Bundesliga title success that season.

However, he played just 986 minutes across all competitions and then made his way back to the Premier League with Tottenham Hotspur.

The Portuguese midfielder signed on a season-long loan deal, which included an option to buy for £26m.

2 Eberl says the trio do not have a future at the club Credit: Getty

Palhinha played regularly and scored the winner against Everton on the final day to secure the club's status in the top-flight.

Whilst he did impress in north London, the clause that allowed Spurs to sign him permanently has expired.

They have instead signed Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali in deals that cost a combined £185m.

It means Palhinha faces uncertainty over where he will be playing in the new season, although he doesn't seem to be short of interest.

Aston Villa are understood to have been in talks for the 31-year-old, who is keen to stay in England.

Newcastle United are also reportedly keen on Palhinha as a potential replacement for the seemingly Arsenal-bound Bruno Guimaraes.

Sports.title: New FIFA presidential candidate emerges as pressure grows on Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
Victor Montagliani is emerging as a serious contender to rival Gianni Infantino at the next FIFA presidential election, talkSPORT understands.

The potential for the Canadian to become the new FIFA president was exclusively revealed on talkSPORT during the World Cup.



3 Infantino us under increased pressure as FIFA president Credit: Getty

CONCACAF president Montagliani wants to be the top chief at FIFA president one day, as talkSPORT revealed earlier this month, and is now considering whether to put his name forward ahead of the November 18 deadline.

Sources close to the 60-year-old have argued his immediate focus is on being re-elected as CONCACAF president, but it is common knowledge the Canadian has aspirations to be FIFA president one day.

He is now toying with either going head to head with Infantino or pushing for the FIFA president to quit, giving him a more open path.



Sources believe CONCACAF's emphatic rejection of Infantino's plans to sell a stake of FIFA to private investors was in part tactical to align with UEFA and potentially secure votes in the long-run.

It means 96 Member Federations, 41 from CONCACAF and 55 from UEFA, are all against Infantino, and could even block vote against him in the presidential election if a viable candidate emerges.



World Cup chaos

Infantino had already faced scrutiny following the conclusion of the World Cup, including concerns over his relationship with US president Donald Trump, before his controversial plans were revealed.

The FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal would see the football governing body's commercial and operational arms merge as part of an organisation funded by private equity.



All 211 Member Associations were given a $40million (£30m) payment incentive by Infantino to back the project by September 19.

However, there has been stiff opposition to the plans from UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC, and some of Infantino's closest allies at FIFA are understood to also be opposed.

Carlos Cordeiro, the president's senior adviser, has even quit his role in protest of the proposed sale of World Cup stakes.

3 Multiple candidates have been tipped to rival Infantino for the presidency Credit: AFP



It is clear UEFA would welcome a challenger to Infantino if he insists on standing even if FFE fails.

UEFA federations would also welcome Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaifi standing, but sources close to the Qatari businessman insist he has 'no ambition' to do so.

UEFA President Alexander Ceferin would be the most qualified name, but the Slovenian lawyer is understood to be willing to continue in his current role as UEFA President next Spring.

He had initially ruled out standing for a third full term until 2031, but is now willing to seek re-election if no other candidates step forward.



Ceferin is not looking to go head-to-head with Infantino despite clashing on issues on a number of occasions.

talkSPORT also understands senior officials within Bosnian, Norwegian, Swedish, German and Spanish football have all discussed backing other European candidates, including Legia owner Dariusz Mioduski.

3 The FFE plans have been given little to no support Credit: Getty

Should Al-Khelaifi choose not to stand, which is the current expectation, Poland would favour Mioduski as well.



Confederation of African Football president Patrice Motsepe is another name intent on being FIFA president one day.

The South African administrator is highly unlikely to go head-to-head with close ally Infantino, instead preferring to wait until 2031 in the hope of getting an endorsement during an election Infantino can't stand again in.

When do nominations to be the next FIFA president close?

And there appears to be no appetite to table a vote of no confidence against Infantino either despite it being toyed with at the last FIFA Congress.

Most federations will simply view the election itself as a vote of confidence, which is why a growing number of UEFA members are hoping to back another candidate to avoid Infantino winning a new term without a genuine debate.



Nominations for the next FIFA presidential election can be made up until November 18 with the election taking place on November 18 in Rabat, Morocco.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace star declares parents convinced him to snub summer switch to Saudi Arabia
Sports.content:
Daichi Kamada has revealed how his parents helped to sway him from leaving Crystal Palace for Saudi Arabia.

Kamada looked set to leave Selhurst Park as a free agent this summer at the end of the two-year deal he signed in July 2024.



2 Kamada could have gone to Saudi Arabia, but will remain in London Credit: Getty

However, he has committed his future to the Palace by signing a new one-year deal to keep him at the club until 2027.

The 29-year-old has been a key part of the club's success during the past two seasons with FA Cup and Conference League triumphs.

Kamada did enough to attract interest from Saudi Arabia, where he could have been in line for a huge payday amid its lucrative finances.



But, after consultation with his parents, the midfielder opted not to move there and remain in south London.

Staying put

Speaking to TV Asahi Sports, via @Fooootest on X, he said: "Up until last winter, I had an offer from Saudi Arabia and was thinking about going there to secure my future.



"I thought my parents would be thrilled, but they told me, 'At this timing, absolutely do not go.'

"It was an enormous amount of money, so I figured they'd be delighted, but that was not the case at all."



Palace chairman Steve Parish was delighted to see Kamada extend his stay as he commented: "This is fantastic news for Crystal Palace. Over the last two years Daichi has made a great impact in the centre of midfield, as well as becoming a fans’ favourite on and off the pitch.

"I am delighted that he has turned down the many options he had to extend his stay in South London.

"Daichi will now have a well-earned break after his excellent World Cup and join us later in pre-season as we enter a busy Premier League and European season."

2 Kamada will stay at Palace for at least another season Credit: Getty



A new dawn at Selhurst

Palace are set to begin their first season under Pierre Sage, who has replaced Oliver Glasner as manager.

They will also make their Europa League debut, having qualified with their Conference League success in May.

Oscar Mingueza is their only summer signing so far following his free transfer from Celta Vigo.

However, they have banked £52million by selling Maxence Lacroix to Premier League rivals Chelsea.



Palace's pre-season schedule got underway with a 5-1 victory over Swindon Town before defeats to Bromley and Lens.

A 0-0 draw with Famalicao followed, with the Eagles then beating Al Ula 3-1 on Friday night.

Sports.title: Where to watch Chelsea v Tottenham plus UK kick-off time, squads, and location
Sports.content:
Where to watch Chelsea v Tottenham plus UK kick-off time, squads, and location

Add us as preferred source

Chelsea and Tottenham will face off in a pre-season clash in Australia with both clubs looking to build momentum ahead of the new Premier League season.

Spurs enter the fixture on the back of three consecutive wins against MK Dons, Auckland FC and Sydney FC.

3 Roberto De Zerbi has been ambitious with his player recruitment at Tottenham so far this summer Credit: AFP

Meanwhile, the Blues kicked off their summer schedule with an action-packed 6-4 victory over Western Sydney Wanderers.

Both teams will hope to put last year's disappointments behind them after undergoing multiple managerial changes during a turbulent 2025/26 campaign.

Roberto De Zerbi remains in charge after taking over late last season and securing top-flight safety on the final day.

Chelsea are beginning a new era under former Real Madrid and Liverpool midfielder Xabi Alonso following spells in the dugout for Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior.

Where to watch Chelsea v Tottenham

Sports.title: ‘Petulant’ Curtis Jones slammed after furious row with teammate during Liverpool pre-season
Sports.content:
Peterborough owner Darragh MacAnthony believes Curtis Jones threw a 'temper tantrum' during his row with Dominik Szoboszlai during pre-season.

Footage posted on social media captured tension between the two Liverpool midfielders after a 1-0 friendly win against Wrexham.



3 Jones was involved in an argument with Szoboszlai during pre-season Credit: X / @anythingLFC_

Szoboszlai handed the armband to Kostas Tsimikas during the match, a decision that appeared to irk Jones.

The trio were spotted in discussion at full-time and Tsimikas opted to throw the armband onto the floor.

Jones picked it up and slightly pushed an annoyed Szoboszlai away, but then continued to argue with him by the side of the pitch.



His frustrations come amid a potential summer exit from Liverpool, with Inter Milan having two approaches rejected.

Fever pitch

However, MacAnthony was not a fan of his attitude, as he told talkSPORT: "He's acting like a spoilt brat. I saw his behaviour last night on the pitch...



"I understand the frustration that he should have got the armband. He's a Scouser, he's been there 20 years, blah blah blah.

"But to act like that and to carry it on, because it went on for about two minutes."



MacAnthony added: "He was having a go at Szoboszlai, who handed the armband over, I think, to Tsimikas, I believe Curtis Jones had the temper tantrum over that.

"That behaviour can't happen, not from a graduate from the academy, he's too into himself."

With Jones looking to move on this summer, MacAnthony insisted that Liverpool are the ones who control the cards.

3 MacAnthony says Jones' behaviour was 'petulant' Credit: talkSPORT



He stated: "So he wants to leave? Well, OK, now Liverpool have to get the best deal for the football club, that's how it works.

"You don't get to throw your toys out of the pram and do it slowly, knowing him, and then act like that.

"I just don't understand it, you're playing for one of the biggest football clubs in the world, you came through the system. Behave, stop. All eyes are on you, that's not behind closed doors.

"That might go on in training and all those things, but you don't want to see that going on for millions of people to watch."



MacAnthony added: "I hate seeing stuff like that, I really do, I think it's so petulant, do you know what I mean?

"And then you're liking Inter Milan's post (of John Stones signing for the club), OK, we get it, you want to go to Inter Milan, you'll probably last five minutes out there."

3 Jones is looking to leave Liverpool this summer Credit: Getty

What next for Jones?

New Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola is keen to keep Jones at the club, as he remarked: "I rate Curtis very highly, for me, he is a great player.



"It's very important he's Scouse, that he's from here, I also like the personality, I hope we can keep him, not only for this year, more time."

Jones only started only 18 of their 38 Premier League matches last season amid strong competition for places in the midfield.

Szoboszlai, Alexis Mac Allister and Ryan Gravenberch appeared to be the go-to options under former head coach Arne Slot.

However, Mac Allister has been linked with a departure as he has less than two years remaining on his deal at Anfield.



Jones would likely have more chances for minutes if the Argentine was to go, but it looks as though he's keen to leave himself.

Sports.title: Sandro Tonali reveals why he joined Tottenham amid Arsenal and Man City interest
Sports.content:
Sandro Tonali reveals why he joined Tottenham amid Arsenal and Man City interest

Roberto De Zerbi needed just ten minutes to convince Sandro Tonali to sign for Tottenham.

The 26-year-old swapped Newcastle for north London earlier this summer in a £100million deal - becoming Spurs' club-record signing in the process.

3 Tonali left Newcastle for Spurs earlier in the summer at the start of July Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Spurs beat off competition from Arsenal and Manchester City in order to land the Italy international.

And Tonali has since revealed that he was left blown away by the project pitched by De Zerbi.

Enter Sandman

"My first impression was really positive," Tonali told reporters in Sydney during Spurs' pre-season tour of New Zealand and Australia.

"When you are happy after a ten-minute speech, it’s everything, everything is perfect.

"The gaffer was Italian, Roberto. I knew him. Roberto really cares about his work, his football.

"He said, 'The project will be tough but will be perfect for me, for you, for the city, and we can do one of the best seasons, because we have big players. We just have to put a lot of work in.'"

On talks with the club, the midfielder said: "When we spoke with Tottenham, we decided to sign for this team.

"They spoke with 100 per cent passion, 100 per cent seriousness.

"For this city, for my life outside of football for my family, OK, it’s like 10 per cent. Roberto and the director made the difference to the deal.

3 A ten-minute chat with De Zerbi and Spurs was all it took to convince Tonali to move to Tottenham Credit: Getty

"I spoke after two minutes with my wife and my family and I said, 'Probably it will be one of my best decisions of my career.'

"She told me, 'You have 100 per cent the control over this decision'. I wanted to speak with her because it’s our life."

'We decided to return to Italy'

Tonali also revealed that his preference was actually to return to Italy this summer.

The ex-AC Milan star left his homeland in 2023 and had been linked with a return to his country of birth.

However, no Serie A side were able to afford Newcastle's lofty asking price.

"We had decided to come back in Italy, but it was impossible for the money," Tonali continued.

3 Spurs have broken their transfer record twice this summer having also signed Mateus Fernandes for £85m Credit: Getty

"England was our solution and we found the best solution in England for me, for my career, for my football, for my happiness, for my family.

"I spoke with two teams, I understood after ten, 15 minutes that Tottenham would be my next team."

Sports.title: Liam Gallagher buys £4million mansion from Arsenal legend after Oasis reunion tour
Sports.content:
Liam Gallagher buys £4million mansion from Arsenal legend after Oasis reunion tour

Add us as preferred source

Tony Adams is £4million richer after selling his Cotswolds mansion to music icon Liam Gallagher.

The Arsenal legend initially listed the property in 2025, with Gallagher buying the former defender's home following the success of the Oasis reunion tour.

3 Adams has sold the eight-bedroom mansion he'd owned since 2002 Credit: getty

Earnings are reportedly in excess of £100million after Liam and brother Noel returned to the stage.

Adams made the decision to sell the property he had owned since 2002 in order for his wife, Poppy Teacher, to attend university.

London calling

"This is a new era for us," the former Arsenal captain told the Mail earlier this week.

"We’ve sold the house and are returning to London. My wife is going back to school."

On his new home, Adams said: "We are now renting while we find a new home in north London.

"We’re not going back to the Chelsea area where all the Blues are."

Teacher, meanwhile, added: "I told Tony I wanted to do early modern history.

"And he said, 'How do you monetise that?' And I said, 'You don’t!'

"But I think he’s proud. He’s telling everyone I’m doing a PhD, but it’s a masters.

"I’ve brought up the children, but now I need to use my brain again.

3 The eight-bedroom mansion is set across five acres of land Credit: SWNS

3 Gallagher has splashed the case following the successful Oasis reunion tour Credit: Getty

"Tony and I want to have a London life, do things like go to galleries."

As for Gallagher, he has admitted that he's loving life after moving to the Cotswolds.

When asked if he had any friendly neighbours, the singer replied: "They’re absolutely incredible.

"They have not stopped baking me cakes and scones."

Gallagher actually bought the property for £250,000 below the initial £4.25m asking price.

The eight-bedroom country manor is set across five-acres of land, and comes with a swimming pool, tennis courts, stables and a two-bedroom cottage.

Sports.title: Mykhailo Mudryk free to return for Chelsea immediately as doping case is resolved
Sports.content:
Mykhailo Mudryk's doping case has been resolved with the Chelsea winger eligible to return to action immediately.

Mudryk was provisionally suspended in December 2024 following a failed drugs test, as he tested positive for Meldonium.

3 Mudryk can return to action with Chelsea Credit: Getty

He was later charged for breaching anti-doping rules, but is now set to return to Chelsea as per an FA statement.

talkSPORT understands he is set to join the Blues on their pre-season tour, likely in Hong Kong, on Sunday.

"The FA can confirm that the anti-doping disciplinary proceedings against Mykhailo Mudryk were resolved with the agreement of the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) on 30 July 2026. In the context of that agreement, Mr Mudryk has accepted his commission of Anti-Doping Rule Violations (ADRVs) and accepted a period of ineligibility.

"On 22 October 2024, Mr Mudryk was subject to an out-of-competition doping control, which revealed the presence of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance.

"The FA notified Mr Mudryk of that finding on 4 December 2024 and imposed a provisional suspension. On 23 May 2025, The FA charged Mr Mudryk with ADRVs in breach of Regulations 3 and 4 of its 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations.

"On 7 to 9 January 2026, a hearing took place before an independent Regulatory Commission. The Regulatory Commission found that Mr Mudryk had committed the charged ADRVs and imposed a four-year period of ineligibility. Subsequently, Mr Mudryk filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

"Since then, changes have been made to WADA Technical Document (TD2027MRL) which, while not retroactive, mean that if Mr Mudryk's sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no ADRVs would have resulted.

"Further to that development and to other circumstances of the case, The FA and Mr Mudryk have now - with the agreement of WADA - resolved the appeal proceedings in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the World Anti-Doping Code and Regulation 90 of the 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations. As a part of the agreement, Mr Mudryk accepted that he had committed the ADRVs charged and acceded to a period of ineligibility equal to the time served at the date of the agreement.

"Mr Mudryk is no longer ineligible and may return to competition with immediate effect."

Mudryk statement

In his own statement, Mudryk said: "After a long battle, the four-year ban that was imposed on me has been rescinded and I am free to resume my career with immediate effect.

3 Mudryk has spent nearly two years out of football Credit: Getty

"I am grateful that this process has reached a conclusion, that I have been cleared to return to football and that I can now look ahead to my future. This has been the most difficult period of my career.

"As I have always maintained from the outset of this case, I have never knowingly or intentionally taken any banned substance.

"My commitment to competing fairly and representing my club and country with professionalism and integrity has always been important to me.

"I would like to thank my family and friends for their support and belief throughout this period. I also want to express my deep gratitude to everyone at Chelsea FC, my teammates and the Chelsea supporters who have been with me throughout.

"I would also like to thank my legal team and others who assisted for their tireless work on my case. My focus now is on returning to football, working hard every day, and making a positive contribution on the pitch.

"Thank you to everyone who continued to believe in me. I look forward to the next chapter of my career."

3 Mudryk has described his suspension as the 'most difficult period' of his career Credit: Getty

Chelsea added: "Chelsea FC acknowledges today's announcement by The Football Association confirming the resolution of the anti-doping proceedings involving Mykhailo Mudryk.

"From the outset, this has been an extremely difficult period for Misha, both professionally and personally, and we are pleased that the matter has now reached a conclusion which allows him to return to football with immediate effect.

"We have always supported Misha throughout this process while fully respecting the integrity of the anti-doping system and the legal process.

"We welcome the acknowledgement that advances in the applicable scientific reporting standards for more reliable testing mean that, had Misha's sample been analysed under today's technical requirements, it would not have been reported as a positive test and no anti-doping rule violation would have resulted. That is an important part of the context surrounding the agreed resolution and allows everyone involved to move forward.

"Misha has consistently maintained that he never knowingly or intentionally used a prohibited substance and did not know how traces of the substance entered his system. Throughout this process he has conducted himself professionally and with resilience during what has undoubtedly been one of the most challenging periods of his career.

"We know how much this opportunity to return means to him. Our focus now is on supporting Misha’s reintegration into the squad and helping him resume his career.

"Chelsea FC remains fully committed to the highest standards of sporting integrity and compliance with all anti-doping regulations.

"Everyone at the Club now looks forward to helping Misha return to full fitness, back into the squad and back onto the pitch."

Mudryk has made 73 appearances since his move from Shakhtar Donetsk in January 2023.

His last appearance for the club came in their 2-0 win against FC Heidenheim in the Conference League in November 2024.

Chelsea went on to win the competition, and Mudryk received a winners' medal despite his absence during the rest of the season.

Sports.content:

Mudryk, 25, was handed a four-year ban after being charged by the Football Association for failing a doping test, with his last appearance coming in November 2024 in the Conference League away at Heidenheim. He scored in that 2-0 win over their German opponents.

It is a seismic resolution which has been struck after changes to the 'scientific reporting standards'.

Throughout this process he has conducted himself professionally and with resilience during what has undoubtedly been one of the most challenging periods of his career.
