It is not yet known whether he will be staying with Chelsea for the 2026-27 season after so long without playing. Sources have confirmed the current plan is for him to join his team-mates on their pre-season, however. Xabi Alonso is due to speak next after their friendly versus Tottenham Hotspur in Sydney on Saturday night, which kicks off at 7.45pm local time in Australia.

Mudryk has insisted from the very beginning that he never knowingly or intentionally took a prohibited substance. An important factor in the agreed resolution is the change made by the World Anti-Doping Agency to the scientific reporting standards used by accredited anti-doping laboratories when analysing samples for meldonium.

The laboratories use a qualitative testing method, meaning they estimate concentration levels rather than measure them precisely. Following developments in the scientific guidance, WADA increased the reporting threshold to provide greater confidence that samples reported as positive exceed the minimum reporting level.

In a statement, the FA revealed the entire timeline, explaining: ‘On October 22, 2024, Mr Mudryk was subject to an out-of-competition doping control, which revealed the presence of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance.

The FA notified Mr Mudryk of that finding on December 4, 2024 and imposed a provisional suspension. On May 23, 2025, the FA charged Mr Mudryk with ADRVs in breach of Regulations 3 and 4 of its 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations.

Mudryk has maintained his innocence throughout his ban and trained independently

The banned substance meldonium is believed to be behind the Ukrainian's failed test in 2024

‘On January 7 to 9, 2026, a hearing took place before an independent Regulatory Commission. The Regulatory Commission found that Mr Mudryk had committed the charged ADRVs and imposed a four-year period of ineligibility. Subsequently, Mr Mudryk filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport. Since then, changes have been made to WADA Technical Document (TD2027MRL) which, while not retroactive, mean that if Mr Mudryk's sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no ADRVs would have resulted.

‘Further to that development and to other circumstances of the case, the FA and Mr Mudryk have now – with the agreement of WADA – resolved the appeal proceedings in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the World Anti-Doping Code and Regulation 90 of the 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations. As a part of the agreement, Mr Mudryk accepted that he had committed the Anti-Doping Rule Violations charged and acceded to a period of ineligibility equal to the time served at the date of the agreement.

He encouraged fans not to give up on him even when he had to train away from Chelsea

‘Mr Mudryk is no longer ineligible and may return to competition with immediate effect.’

The precise source of the exposure has never been entirely identified. It is believed it occurred away from England while on international duty with Ukraine in September 2024.

Chelsea sources say they are grateful to both the FA and WADA for working constructively to reach a fair resolution in light of the updated scientific standards. The club's focus is now completely on supporting Mudryk’s return to football and helping him reintegrate into the squad.

Sports.title: PR nightmares, an incompetent commissioner and now a trans war... JAMES COHEN reveals why the WNBA must make a change now or risk fumbling Caitlin Clark and its big chance at success
Sports.content:
PR nightmares, an incompetent commissioner and now a trans war... JAMES COHEN reveals why the WNBA must make a change now or risk fumbling Caitlin Clark and its big chance at success

On paper, the WNBA should be celebrating a glorious new era.

The league kicked off 2026 riding the crest of a massive 11-year, $2.2billion TV deal - the kind of money that would have seemed impossible to secure just five years ago.

Television numbers are up 12 percent on this stage of last season and All-Star ratings surged by a staggering 44 percent in further examples of the league's growth.

Furthermore, for the first time in history, more fans packed out the stands for the WNBA All-Star game in Chicago than the men's NBA equivalent. Add in a brand-new video referee system and the product on the court has never looked better.

Yet beneath the surface, the league is sinking in a swamp of its own making.

Every single week seems to bring another toxic PR crisis, another culture war or another administrative embarrassment. Seldom is there a quiet week in the WNBA - and it's rarely ever to do with what's actually happening on the basketball court.

On paper, the WNBA should be celebrating a glorious new era yet, in reality, the league appears to be sinking in a swamp of its own making amid a myriad of controversies lately

Questions have been asked about the leadership credentials of commissioner Cathy Engelbert

The league have been accused of 'killing' their golden goose, Caitlin Clark, in recent years

Make no mistake: The relentless narrative issues surrounding the WNBA aren't entirely its fault, but the league doesn't seem to have any strategy for fixing things.

And nowhere is this incompetence more blatant than the appalling treatment towards Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark - who has been subjected to controversy ever since being drafted into the league in April 2024.

Clark is, undoubtedly, the greatest cash cow the sport has ever seen. She single-handedly put millions of eyes - and dollars - into a league that desperately needed them. Yet the WNBA's handling of its biggest star borders on outright negligence.

Rather than wrapping their golden goose in cotton wool, league bosses have allowed Clark to be thrown to the wolves, on multiple occasions. She has been left at breaking point, battered by non-stop analysis, commentary and physical confrontations.

In a recent interview on ESPN's SportsCenter, a visibly drained Clark admitted she was 'emotionally exhausted' by the circus surrounding her every move.

She described how she cannot walk out of a locker room without dreading what the next storyline about her will be, adding: 'It makes your shoulders tense. People don't want to talk about the basketball, they just wanna stir it up and make something else.'

But instead of jumping to her defense, the basketball establishment turned on her.

ESPN analyst Monica McNutt publicly blasted the young star, demanding Clark take 'accountability' for the discourse. Think about that for a second. A 24-year-old taking the brunt of unprecedented hate was being told to apologize for it.

WNBA star Clark recently admitted she is 'emotionally exhausted' and drained by the non-stop controversy surrounding her - as she opened up in a rare and candid interview with ESPN

Alyssa Thomas ignited outrage after she was seen punching Clark in the neck during a game

Clark has constantly been the target of on-court conflict since arriving in the league in 2024

ESPN's Monica McNutt sparked backlash on ESPN's Women's Sports Sunday studio show after telling Clark to take 'accountability' regarding the controversy that surrounds her

And on the court, it's even worse. Opponents treat Clark like an open target.

This year alone she has absorbed a string of hard fouls, including one from Alyssa Thomas that connected with her throat and prompted the league to hand down a one-game ban - which felt like nothing more than a shrug from WNBA higher-ups.

Then there was the poster. As part of its 30th anniversary celebrations, the WNBA released a commemorative print featuring 30 of its past and present stars.

Clark - the league's biggest ratings generator, merchandise seller and the reason for that record-breaking media deal - was nowhere on it. The league later put the omission down to licensing technicalities rather than a deliberate snub.

But optics matter and this was an organization that has repeatedly struggled to read a room. Fans reacted with fury and analysts including Outkick's Clay Travis accused the league of doing 'everything they can to kill' its golden goose. It is hard to disagree.

Which brings us to the person who is meant to be steering the ship but, in reality, whose leadership looks increasingly threadbare: Commissioner Cathy Engelbert.

Players across the league openly admit they have zero relationship with the woman running the sport - which isn't exactly a great reflection on her tenure in charge.

Las Vegas Aces superstar A'ja Wilson - a four-time MVP and three-time champion - was blunt when recently asked about her relationship with the commissioner.

The WNBA posted an image showing some of the league's most famous faces, past and present, to celebrate its 30th anniversary - yet Caitlin Clark was nowhere to be seen

A number of stars revealed that they have no relationship with WNBA commissioner Engelbert

Las Vegas Aces superstar A'ja Wilson - a four-time MVP and three-time champion - said: ''My only relationship with Cathy is when she hands me awards'

At All-Star Weekend, she said: 'My only relationship with Cathy is when she hands me awards, which is great. I love to see her in that light. But I think when it comes to leadership, I'm always big on bonds... big on connection on a deeper level.'

That is not the description of a healthy partnership between a league and its brightest asset - it is a description of a landlord, not a leader.

Wilson is far from a lone voice. Napheesa Collier openly criticized Engelbert's leadership last season and ESPN's Chiney Ogwumike voiced her own concerns that the commissioner is falling short of building relationships with the league's top stars.

With Engelbert's contract set to expire this year, the WNBA has the chance to reset. Whether it takes it will say everything about how seriously it takes the warning signs.

The league's inability to navigate the political currents swirling around the sport without making things worse only adds to the image of an organization without a plan.

Compare that to most other major leagues, where these flashpoints rarely spill into public farce and the WNBA's struggles almost look self-inflicted.

Take the recent outrage following Sophie Cunningham's comments on trans athletes.

The Indiana Fever guard drew intense scrutiny recently when she spoke out about 'protecting' girls from playing against biological men in an interview with ESPN – before later doubling down on her comments amid a fierce wave of fan backlash.

Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham recently sparked controversy when she spoke out about 'protecting' girls from playing against biological men in an interview with ESPN

People gathered in support of Cunningham in Seattle before the game started on Tuesday night

Cunningham's rival, Stefanie Dolson, wore a t-shirt which read 'trans rights are human rights'

Celeste Keaton (right) has been suspended by the WNBA for berating two women at a game

The women (left) accused Keaton of calling them 'f***ing insane' and berating them over their support for Sophie Cunningham

The backlash was instant as rival Stefanie Dolson turned their pre-game tunnel into a political battleground, rocking up in a t-shirt reading: 'Trans Rights are Human Rights.'

Then things got truly unhinged.

A viral video captured Seattle Storm co-owner Celeste Keaton screaming at fans in the stands, branding them 'f***ing insane' for daring to support Cunningham.

The WNBA suspended Keaton for five games and issued a fine. Compare that with the NBA, which forced Donald Sterling to sell the Los Angeles Clippers entirely over racist remarks made in a private conversation.

As one widely-shared observation on social media put it: the NBA forced out an owner for offensive private comments, while the WNBA suspended one for a handful of games after she was filmed berating teenage girls at a public game.

The disparity in consequence speaks for itself.

To make matters worse, the league keeps scoring embarrassing own goals.

In a mind-boggling blunder this week, the official WNBA X account uploaded a video showing Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers placing a $400 cash bet on their game.

The WNBA deleted a video of Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers gambling on their own game

Bueckers was then asked about the bet before Wednesday's game, in the now-deleted clip

Reese and the Dream beat Buckers' Wings in their first game after the WNBA's All-Star break

In an era where sports betting rules are fiercely enforced, promoting your own players gambling on league games is institutional madness.

The post was quietly deleted after public outrage, followed by a limp PR statement admitting the video 'missed the mark' and promising to 'reemphasize' betting policies to its players. It was amateur hour at its absolute finest.

Add to that the backlash the league received after its players declined to wear 'USA 250' badges during All-Star weekend, breaking the practice of every other major American league marking the nation's 250th anniversary, and a pattern starts to form.

None of these episodes, individually, are catastrophic. But collectively they paint a picture of an organization that is being carried by the brilliance of its players - while its own decision-making saps away the goodwill that success should be generating.

The WNBA has genuinely never had it this good. It also, right now, does not appear to have the first idea how to hold onto it.

Sports.title: FIFA's World Cup plot turns to rubble: Deluded Gianni Infantino's controversial plan is dead as key allies rebel and more nations unite to oppose bid to sell off football
Sports.content:
FIFA's World Cup plot turns to rubble: Deluded Gianni Infantino's controversial plan is dead as key allies rebel and more nations unite to oppose bid to sell off football

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Gianni Infantino's divisive plan to sell stakes in the World Cup appears to be dead after the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) joined UEFA and CONCACAF in opposing the plot - while two senior FIFA figures turned against him.

Carlos Cordeiro, a retired American investment banker and senior adviser to Infantino, has resigned from his role at FIFA - becoming the first internal figure to do so.

It comes after UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC all opposed FIFA’s plans to generate £3.1billion in private investment in FIFA tournaments.

135 FIFA members are now publicly opposed to the FIFA Forward Enterprise, bringing the dissidents above the required 106 threshold to block the plans with dignitaries now joining the calls for Infantino to scrap his plans.

Releasing a statement, Cordeiro - who served on the White House task force for the 2026 World Cup - distanced himself from Infantino’s plans and ripped into the proposals.

Cordeiro urged his now former FIFA colleagues to follow suit and speak out against the plans, which he describes as a bad deal for football. Infantino had promised member associations a £30million incentive to force the deal through.

'As a Senior Advisor to the FIFA President, a former banker, and a lifelong football fan, I cannot stand by while FIFA considers selling a stake in the World Cup,’ Cordeiro said.

'Let me be clear: I had no involvement in this proposal, and I oppose it unequivocally. It is a bad deal for FIFA's Member Associations, a bad deal for football, and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game.

'It has been the privilege of a lifetime to serve FIFA for more than five years and to work alongside dedicated, principled people who care deeply about the game. I hope they, too, will speak up, because decisions of this magnitude should be made in the interests of football, not those who stand to profit from it.'

FIFA’s chief operating officer Kevin Lamour responded to Cordeiro's call to action and publicly turned against Infantino.

While Lamour stopped short of resigning as chief operating officer, a post he has held for two years, the Frenchman has put his job at risk by speaking out against FIFA’s chief.

In a statement to the Associated Press, Lamour said: ‘It is the project of one person. Not only must this project not go ahead, but the time has now come for football political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions.

‘If that means I lose my job, then so be it. I will understand and respect that decision. At least I’ll sleep well tonight.’

FIFA issued a statement on Friday morning doubling down on plans to sell £3.1 billion in shares for FIFA tournaments after UEFA announced a boycott of competitions and CONCACAF - the North, Central, American and Caribbean federation - opposed the plans.

On Friday night CONMEBOL, who govern the 10 South American nations, said they would seek more information from FIFA before taking a stance on the proposals.

But the AFC choosing to stand with the rebels leaves Infantino's project - and potentially his FIFA presidency - facing a terminal threat.

In a statement, the AFC said: 'The AFC stands in solidarity with UEFA and CONCACAF in expressing serious concerns over FIFA's proposal to introduce private investment into FIFA's flagship competitions and the decision-making process around FFE.

'The fact that the situation has reached the point where the real possibility of a FIFA World Cup boycott has entered public discourse should concern everyone who cares about the future of our game. Football should never have been placed in such a position.

Gianni Infantino's controversial plan to sell off the World Cup appears to be dead in the water after the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) joined UEFA and CONCACAF in opposing the plot

Infantino's senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro (right) has also now resigned in protest at the plans

'Against this backdrop, and in light of the clear positions expressed by UEFA and CONCACAF, as well as the unprecedented divisions that have emerged across the football world, the AFC believes that the proposed FFE cannot realistically achieve the necessary broad consensus and unity required to move forward.

'The FIFA World Cup is the pinnacle of global football and derives its strength from the participation of all Confederations and the world's leading football nations.

'Any proposal that risks undermining the unity and universal character of the competition must be reconsidered.

'While the immediate debate centres on FFE, the AFC considers this issue extends far beyond a single proposal.

'Rather, it has exposed fundamental weaknesses in FIFA's consultation and decision-making processes that must now be addressed.

'While the AFC notes FIFA's latest clarification on the proposal, the central concerns surrounding governance, institutional process and meaningful consultation remain unanswered.

'A proposal of such significance, with the potential to affect the commercial, sporting and strategic future of world football, must not emerge through processes that leave Confederations, Member Associations (MAs) and even FIFA's own governing bodies, including the FIFA Council, feeling sidelined.

'The primary objective for world football must be to ensure that decisions of such magnitude are being developed through processes that are anchored on transparency and command the confidence of the football community.

'This is not the first occasion where major stakeholders have been confronted with significant initiatives after the direction of travel appears to have already been determined.

'Such an approach undermines confidence in FIFA's governance framework and diminishes the authority of its statutory bodies.

Join the discussion Should the World Cup ever be used as a tool for private profit, or does selling stakes betray the spirit of the game?

FIFA issued a late-night response to furious backlash over the controversial plan to sell World Cup stakes to private investors by blaming the media for the uproar

'No subsequent consultation process, however well-intentioned, can replace early engagement with the appropriate FIFA bodies and the football family.

'The AFC believes this moment must become a catalyst for strengthening institutional reform. While every FIFA MA must have the opportunity to consider and determine proposals affecting the future of world football, meaningful democracy is not measured solely by the opportunity to vote.

'It begins with transparent governance, timely consultation, informed deliberation and genuine participation throughout the decision-making process.

'Accordingly, the AFC calls upon FIFA to undertake an urgent review of its governance and decision-making framework to ensure that proposals of global significance are developed through proper consultation, meaningful engagement and appropriate oversight by FIFA's statutory bodies.

'The FIFA World Cup, and the game itself, belong to the entire global football family. Their future must always be shaped collectively, through institutions that reflect the voices of all Confederations and MAs.'

The AFC's statement criticises FIFA's clarification of their proposals released on Friday morning, where they blamed the media for misconstruing their plans and made a dig at UEFA for holding FIFA to account.

FIFA said: 'We have heard the feedback provided by the respective confederations in relation to the proposed establishment of FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) and would like to address the issues that have surfaced since the initial media reporting on Tuesday.

'We respect the feedback and concern aired in public and reaffirm our commitment to an open and democratic consultation.

⁠'Our planned consultation process was disrupted by incorrect media reports. We will proceed with this consultation process to ensure that each MA has the ability to express its vote based on facts.

'FFE has been proposed solely to ensure that all FIFA Member Associations (MAs) have the opportunity to take meaningful ownership of the commercial opportunity of football in their respective countries, and that this does not come at the cost of either the spirit or the governance of FIFA or football itself.

Infantino has been widely criticised for his decision to put the World Cup 'up for sale'

The core investor would be a New York investment firm created by Joshua Kushner (pictured earliere this month in California), the brother of Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner

'Nobody is selling football. This is not something FIFA would ever entertain.

'Everyone has the right to express their opposition and to seek further clarification but no single entity can claim to represent all 211 MAs around the world. Each MA should be allowed to review the proposal and have a say in shaping their own future. These are the democratic principles of FIFA.'

They continued by outlining the plans, subject to consultation with member nations.

There is frustration across the international football landscape, however, that such proposals have been unilaterally developed - with proposed investors already lined up - in complete secrecy despite an eventual 'consultation'.

UEFA nations are boycotting all FIFA competitions so long as the proposals remain on the table. All 55 UEFA nations met virtually on Thursday, with more than 40 federations providing testimony.

Daily Mail Sport were told associations expressed ‘outrage’ on the call with ‘total unanimity’ against the proposal, before deciding to abstain from FIFA competitions.

Daily Mail Sport also understands there is growing opposition to Infantino's presidency, with CONCACAF nations losing - or having already lost - confidence in the Swiss football administrator.

UEFA and their member associations are yet to be drawn on that matter. Infantino is seeking a fourth term as FIFA president next year.

One international football insider told Daily Mail Sport: ‘UEFA’s response is at the nuclear button end of the spectrum, which is impressive. We thought Infantino would survive the Trump refereeing intervention - but he has overreached this time.'

In a statement, UEFA said: 'UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one. We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA's proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors.

'The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football's greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.

'It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game. This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA's duty as the custodian of world football.

'National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football's greatest competitions or bear the consequences. This is not a 'democratic decision', but governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game.

'But our opposition goes far beyond process.

'The moment external investors acquire ownership interests in FIFA competitions, football changes forever. Commercial return becomes a permanent obligation. Investor expectations become a daily pressure. From that moment onwards, every decision on the international calendar, every decision on competition formats and every decision shaping the future of football is no longer driven by what best serves the game, but by what best serves shareholders.

'This model has no place in world football. Football's future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return. Nor can the interests of national associations, leagues, clubs, players and supporters become subordinate to investor returns. Football cannot mortgage its future for financial gain.

'Europe's position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation.

'As a result of today's discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership.

'Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination.

'There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise. This is one of those moments.

'Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale.’

An FA spokeswoman added: 'We stand shoulder to shoulder with our European colleagues and fully support the collective view. We oppose FIFA's plans - the FIFA World Cup belongs to football and always will.’

Concacaf later added: 'Concacaf is a confederation united by the love of our game, where football comes first. Guided by this philosophy over the past ten years we have built, from the ground up, an organisation founded on service, transparent governance, and the long-term stewardship of football.

'History has shown FIFA and the football family what happens when the custodians of the game lose sight of these values.

'With this in mind, Concacaf today convened a meeting of the presidents of its 41 Member Associations, together with its President, Council members, and its FIFA Council members, to discuss a proposal developed and presented by the FIFA President to establish 'FIFA Forward Enterprise' and sell interests in the FIFA World Cup to private investors.

'During the meeting, the membership expressed deep concerns about the lack of due process surrounding the proposal, the artificially short deadline imposed, and the absence of any review or approval by the relevant FIFA governance bodies. In addition, the need for private equity investment to fund new and existing FIFA Forward programs following the most profitable FIFA World Cup in history was questioned.

'The discussion reinforced the need for greater transparency and proper governance.

'For these reasons, Concacaf and its 41 Member Associations have: Rejected the proposal; Tasked their FIFA Council Members with engaging FIFA to determine how existing FIFA reserves could be used to increase FIFA Forward funding for football development across our region; and Tasked their FIFA Council Members with instructing the FIFA President to ensure that any matter follows the proper governance processes via staff and FIFA Council, in accordance with the FIFA Statutes.

'Through these actions, Concacaf reaffirms that football's future - and its greatest asset - must remain in the hands of our football family.'

Sepp Blatter, the FIFA president before Infantino, took to social media to renew his attacks on his successor by writing on Friday evening: 'The FIFA is not a private equity fund. It is an association with statutes, regulations, and a fiduciary responsibility to protect the global game. If you sell football's crown jewels to private investors, you also sell part of the game – especially its soul. Money matters, but it must never become everything.'

And Prime Minister Andy Burnham added his voice to those condemning Infantino, telling GiveMeSport: 'It's a feeling I've had for a while and it's clearly not a sustainable situation. When UEFA and CONCACAF can't have confidence, that is a large chunk of world football saying that this is not acceptable.

'I had some concerns about the 2022 World Cup, on the pitch and all the rest of it. It didn't feel right. It hasn't felt right. And after everything that FIFA have been through before, I was prepared to give his [Infantino's] era the benefit of the doubt, and I did give it the benefit of the doubt until this point.'

Sports.title: Erling Haaland and Michael Jordan cross paths in the Mediterranean as fans joke Norway striker 'looks like a minion' next to basketball legend
Sports.content:
Michael Jordan's annual summer cruise of the Mediterranean has crossed paths with Erling Haaland's own seasonal voyage, resulting in a memorable photo of the two from the South of France.

'No caption needed,' Haaland captioned the picture of himself and Jordan on X.

The smiling 63-year-old Chicago Bulls legend is seen in a white T-shirt, khaki shorts and a baseball hat in the photo, while the 26-year-old Haaland sports a grin and has his arm draped around Jordan's shoulder.

Although Haaland is reliably the tallest person in most photos, the supposedly 6ft 5in (1.95m) Norwegian striker appears a couple of inches shorter than Jordan, who has been listed at 6ft 6in since 1981.

'Erling you look like a minion next to Jordan,' read one comment on X.

Another added: 'I love how athletes could look so tall in their own sport until they stand next to basketball players.'

Michael Jordan's annual summer cruise of the Mediterranean has crossed paths with Erling Haaland's own voyage, resulting in a memorable photo of the two from the South of France

Jordan and wife Yvette are known to travel the Mediterranean on their $115m yacht

Many other reactions focused on the usually stoic Jordan, who couldn't contain his mutual excitement.

'I've never seen Jordan smile like this,' one fan wrote. 'Everyone loves Haaland.'

For Jordan, summers have increasingly centered on the Mediterranean, where he and wife Yvette have been regularly seen aboard a family yacht estimated to be worth $115 million. And they don't travel alone, but rather, are often accompanied by the likes of David and Victoria Beckham, Magic Johnson and even Samuel L. Jackson.

Such travels could become habit forming for Haaland, who has been on his own Mediterranean odyssey since the Manchester City star led Norway to the quarterfinals of the World Cup.

On Thursday, Norway's favorite son was joined by his brother and friends at the five-star Hôtel du Cap-Eden-Roc, where he was seen boarding a boat for an excursion at sea.

Fans were surprised to see Jordan standing taller than Haaland, who stands 6ft 5in (1.95m)

City stars Erling Haaland and Mateo Kovacic, joined by their partners Isabel and Izabel, and were among the guests. Haaland later led party-goers in Norway's iconic 'rowing' celebration

Haaland then posted a picture of himself wearing a Viking helmet on his summer holiday

A week earlier, the Manchester City striker attended teammate Gianluigi Donnarumma's wedding in Southern Italy with partner Isabel Haugseng Johansen. The Norway star, fresh from accumulating an army of new fans at the World Cup, opted for a black suit, bow-tie and sunglasses as he happily walked hand-in-hand with Johansen.

He was later filmed leading a group of guests in recreating Norway's iconic 'rowing' celebration from the tournament in North America.

Prior to that, Haaland turned 26 alongside Johansen in Sardinia, where he was pictured wearing a Viking helmet.

'26 years,' he wrote on Instagram. 'Nice.'

Haaland's extended off-season break is nearly over. He was allowed to miss the team's Asian tour, but will be expected to rejoin Manchester City prior to the Community Shield match with Arsenal on August 16 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

Sports.title: A Man United wonderkid keen to impress Michael Carrick, Chelsea's Brazilian star and the Premier League's youngest ever goalscorer... five teenagers primed to shine this season
Sports.content:
As Premier League clubs continue their money-spinning tours around the globe, one of the key dynamics to pre-season is which youngsters are given an opportunity to shine.

On Wednesday, for example, Tottenham's Luca Williams-Barnett, 17, scored a panenka against Sydney FC and Rio Ngumoha, 17, impressed for Liverpool in their victory over Wrexham.

Many of those youngsters are there to make up the numbers while first-team stars return from the World Cup, and several will then head out on loan to the EFL.

Yet some of those teenagers excelling ahead of the campaign may be breaking through at exactly the right time, preparing themselves for a bumper Premier League campaign.

So, in light of the pre-season calendar and younger players being given some exposure, Daily Mail Sport has picked out five teenagers primed for a big season.

For context, we have chosen youngsters who are yet to establish themselves as regulars, meaning Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly and Fulham's Josh King are among those discounted.

Liverpool wonderkid Rio Ngumoha impressed in their pre-season victory over Wrexham

Rio Ngumoha, Club: Liverpool, Age: 17

Ngumoha needs little introduction given the hype surrounding him, which only increased after his memorable goal against Newcastle at the start of last season.

Arne Slot was cautious with the winger for the rest of the campaign though as he made just five Premier League starts, all of which came after February.

At 17, he is still so young yet no doubt Ngumoha is one of the most talented players of his generation, and he again showed signs of his quality when making his England debut ahead of the World Cup.

With Mohamed Salah's exit, there is a vacancy on Liverpool's right wing, and while Ngumoha - alongside Cody Gakpo and potential new signing Bradley Barcola - prefers to play on the left, this could be the perfect opportunity for the 17-year-old to have a proper breakthrough campaign.

Rio Ngumoha announced himself to the Premier League at the start of last season

Max Dowman, Club: Arsenal, Age: 16

Like Ngumoha, the world is well aware of Max Dowman, the youngest scorer in Premier League history.

However, despite the hype surrounding him, he rarely featured for Arsenal last season as Mikel Arteta tried to protect him.

Yet with Bukayo Saka toiling during the latter part of the season and looking like he needed a rest at the World Cup, this could be a perfect moment for Dowman, particularly if the Gunners struggle to bring in the attacking reinforcements they are searching for.

Max Dowman could benefit from more gametime if Bukayo Saka is rested by Mikel Arteta

Estevao, Club: Chelsea, Age: 19

Estevao showed glimpses of his incredible talent last season, yet he was hampered by various injuries and Enzo Maresca's desire to ease him into his first campaign of English football.

The Brazilian announced himself with a dramatic injury-time winner against Liverpool in October, and also impressed in Chelsea's memorable 3-0 victory over Barcelona in the Champions League the following month.

Xabi Alonso is the third Blues boss he has worked under, and the Spaniard is renowned for developing young attacking talents, meaning Estevao could go to another level in 2026-27.

Chelsea's Brazilian wonderkid Estevao could be in for a big season under Xabi Alonso

Ayden Heaven, Club: Man United, Age: 19

It was back in February 2025 when Ayden Heaven made the bold choice to switch Arsenal for Manchester United in search of first team football.

And while Heaven has only played 24 times for his new club, the defender has shown significant promise and enjoyed a couple of lengthy runs in the team last season.

With Lisandro Martinez coming back late from the World Cup, plus injury concerns with Matthijs de Ligt, Heaven may find himself up the pecking order, particularly as United return to European football and face an increasingly hectic schedule.

Ayden Heaven could be given more opportunities amid defensive absences elsewhere

Shea Lacey, Club: Man United, Age: 19

Man United fans always love a homegrown attacking hero and Shea Lacey had been shining in their academy for several years before he made his debut against Aston Villa last December.

Lacey did suffer the ignominy of being sent off in just his third United appearance, yet he has impressed again in pre-season.

With a lack of natural wingers at Old Trafford, an issue partly caused by Ruben Amorim's squad-building for a formation with wing-backs, Lacey should find himself part of the first-team squad.

Michael Carrick is believed to be a fan and reports broke earlier this week that he wants to keep Lacey around the squad for the first half of the campaign instead of loaning him out.

Sports.title: How Glasgow's hometown hero Josh Kerr is relishing his battle for Commonwealth gold after shattering fastest mile world record, writes NIK SIMON... as Georgia Hunter-Bell cruises to 800m glory
Sports.content:
Step off the train at Glasgow Central and one of the first things you see is an enormous billboard of Josh Kerr.

It is a giant image of the hometown hero, letting out a cathartic roar after he shattered the world record for the men's outdoor mile two weeks ago.

Scotland expects their 28-year-old runner to win gold but this weekend’s big-ticket race promises to be the highest quality showdown of these scaled-down Games.

It is the first time the mile has featured for 60 years – having been replaced by the 1,500 metres – and organisers hope it will stir up memories of the historic duel between Roger Bannister and John Landy.

Kerr faces world class opposition. Former world champion Jake Wightman – also of Scotland – defending Commonwealth champion Oliver Hoare and breakthrough star Cameron Myers complete a formidable field.

‘I thrive in a pressure environment,’ said Kerr, who turned his bedroom into an altitude chamber before breaking the record.

Josh Kerr set a new world record for the fastest mile - with a time of 3mins and 42.66secs

Scotland expects their 28-year-old star to win gold at the Commonwealth Games this weekend

‘I want as much pressure on me as possible. I’m here to show up and get a gold medal for Scotland, and hopefully we can put more people on the podium than just me.

‘I think the other Scottish guys are looking great, and Jake’s run an awesome kilometre, so I’m just happy to be rubbing shoulders with these guys again and going after the big medals.’

The conditions at Scotstoun will be a far cry from the perfect settings Kerr enjoyed for his world-record run. There will be no pacemakers and the Scottish weather is unpredictable. It will be a tactical battle of pacing, positioning and the final kick.

‘It is very different to go from racing a clock to racing these guys - these are some of the best milers in the world,’ added Kerr. ‘Just trying to battle against them and try to win at my tactical battle.

‘It's going to be a war out there. It's the home crowd, it’s our track, it's where we learnt, it's our crowd. The rest of the guys want to take what’s ours. They will have to come with something because they are not going to get it easy.’

Kerr trained at Scotstoun as a teenager and also watched his older brother, Jake, play rugby there for Edinburgh against Glasgow Warriors. Fellow Scot Wightman is also familiar with the surroundings and believes the headline event can provide the moment of the Games.

‘I looked down every single start list of the track events and there are so many missing every other event,’ said Wightman. ‘When you look at ours, there’s not one person you probably could have added into this to make it any stronger.

‘The irony is that I think every event you’d say that the European field would be harder than the Commonwealth; whereas ours the Commonwealth is so much harder than the European one. It will bring the whole world’s attention onto it.

‘I think sometimes the Commonwealths get stuck in our bubble of nations that are competing and you speak to Americans sometimes and they haven’t even heard of it; whereas I feel like there’s enough interest in the mile, especially after what Josh did.

It is the first time the mile has featured for 60 years - having been replaced by the 1,500 metres - and the race promises to be the highest quality showdown of these scaled-down Games

‘I think there’s going to be a big audience around the world tuning in for this, which would be cool for the legacy of Commonwealth and for an event that seemed like it might not keep happening just because of the funding and who’s going to pick it up.

'I think if we can put on a good show on Saturday it’s a real good thing for Commonwealth sport in the future. If we can write headlines because it’s an amazing race and there’s something really good to see then maybe it will help keep pushing the Commonwealths to get back to where it should be.’

Hunter-Bell cruises to 800m glory

As tears streamed down her face on the podium, Georgia Hunter Bell reflected on her journey from office job to gold medallist.

She became England’s first 800 metres champion at the Commonwealth Games Diane Edwards won in 1990.

Hunter Bell beat Kenyan world champion Lilian Odira, dominating the field with a time of 1min 59.81secs.

The 32-year-old was competing in Parkrun events during Covid lockdown but this was her sixth medal since she quit her job in cyber security two years ago.

Georgia Hunter-Bell was streets ahead of her rivals as she claimed gold in Glasgow

‘It was very emotional,’ she said. ‘I know lots of people reflect on being a kid – doing it for the kid version of themself. I more think of the young woman version of myself who was 23 or 24 and really gave up and didn’t know what she was doing with her life. I feel sorry for that girl and then I feel proud of making it through that and coming back here.

‘Glasgow is very special to me because it was after the Glasgow indoor championships that I decided to quit my job. I came fourth then and it showed me that I was good but I had to make a lifestyle change.’

With Olympic champion Keely Hodgkinson not competing in Glasgow, Hunter Bell seized her opportunity.

She led the race from the starting gun, before charging clear in the final 200m.

‘I felt calm,’ she said. ‘I really feel like I was composed. The race didn’t go to plan. I did not think I would lead it for the whole thing. I wanted to lead with like 200 to go, but I found myself at the front, so I thought I'll just control it, keep it relaxed, not too fast, and then when I feel that pressure on me with the move being made, I'll be ready to go.’

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham gets a hero's reception on his return to Birmingham City... as England superstar's boyhood club beat Barcelona on penalties!
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham gets a hero's reception on his return to Birmingham City... as England superstar's boyhood club beat Barcelona on penalties!

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jude Bellingham was welcomed back to Birmingham City like a hero on Friday night as he watched his boyhood club triumph on penalties against Barcelona.

Barcelona travelled over to St Andrew's for a pre-season friendly against the Championship club, giving Blues fans plenty to cheer about as they were given a rare opportunity to see the LaLiga champions in action.

The occasion was made even more special for those inside St Andrew's when England superstar Bellingham, who began his glittering career at Birmingham before leaving to join Borussia Dortmund in 2020 and later Real Madrid in 2023, was unveiled at the start of the game.

Before kick-off, Birmingham City's official social media account showed Bellingham taking his seat and waving to fans in a touching video captioned: 'Jude. He's home.'

As he raised his arms aloft to greet the adoring fans, Blues supporters loudly bellowed 'Jude' to honour their former starlet and fervently chanted 'he's one of our own' in a special moment for the England midfielder at St Andrew's.

Bellingham is still enjoying some richly-deserved time off after playing an integral role for England at the World Cup this summer and thus has not yet returned to Real Madrid to begin the new season under Jose Mourinho.

Jude Bellingham was given a warm reception as he watched Birmingham defeat Barcelona

Bellingham posed for selfies with Birmingham fans who once cheered him on as a teenager

The £113million midfielder cheered jubilantly as he watched his boyhood club triumph over Real Madrid's bitter rivals, winning on penalties after drawing 2-2 in normal time.

August Priske Flyger and John Solis were both on the scoresheet for the Blues, while Hamza Abdelkarim netted a brace for the Catalans.

Goalkeeper James Beadle was the hero in the shootout as he saved spot-kicks from Roony Bardghji and Brian Farinas, while Jordi Pesquer crashed his effort into the crossbar to hand Birmingham a 3-2 win on penalties.

Few clubs have a fonder view of an academy player than Birmingham City have of Bellingham, who at 23 has already become one of the best midfielders in world football.

Bellingham burst through the ranks at Birmingham as a youngster, starring for the U18s as a 14 year old and later making his debut for the U23s at the age of just 15.

The midfielder was then promoted to the Blues' senior squad for the 2019-20 season, becoming the youngest first-team player in the club's history at 16 years and 36 days old.

Bellingham could hardly believe what he was watching as Birmingham triumphed on penalties

The England international was seen wearing his No22 Birmingham jersey - which was officially retired by the club when he left them to join Borussia Dortmund back in 2020

After making 41 appearances that campaign, Bellingham joined Borussia Dortmund for a £25m fee and became the youngest player ever to have his shirt retired by a professional club, with Birmingham officially retiring his No22 jersey.

Despite arriving at St Andrew's in a white t-shirt, Bellingham finished the match wearing his retired No22 Birmingham jersey, which appeared to give the hosts luck as they pulled off a comeback to force the decisive penalty shootout.

Sports.title: Revealed: Chelsea avoided sanction that would have RELEGATED them from the Premier League as secret talks get six-point deduction overturned following 'illegal' signings under Roman Abramovich
Sports.content:
Chelsea avoided a 15-point deduction over payments to unregistered agents that would have relegated them from the Premier League because they reported themselves for breaching the rules and co-operated with the investigation.

In the written reasons document in the case between Chelsea and the FA, the governing body said a 'starting point of 15 points is appropriate', before the club's self-reporting and co-operation was taken into account.

Chelsea would have been relegated had the punishment been imposed in the 2025-26 campaign. The Blues finished 13 points ahead of West Ham, who went down in 18th place on 39 points.

'The starting point will accordingly be reduced by 1/3 to 10 points to reflect the general mitigation under the heads of self-reporting and cooperation...' the written reasons state.

Chelsea were initially given a six-point deduction suspended until June 2027 and a £10m fine from an independent regulatory commission.

However, after appealing, the club will now only pay for their financial penalty with a suspended two-window transfer ban added in.

Chelsea have overturned a six-point deduction following 74 breaches of financial rules under former owner Roman Abramovich

The FA's 'starting point' for the sanction was 15 points before Chelsea's self-reporting and cooperation was taken into account

The Stamford Bridge side were hit with 74 charges by the FA and admitted to their chargesheet. The charges related to the use of and the making of payments to unregistered agents between 2011 and 2018.

Earlier this year, the Blues were fined £10m and handed a suspended transfer ban by the Premier League after admitting to making £47m in secret payments to unregistered agents and third parties between 2011 and 2018.

Chelsea's owners BlueCo voluntarily reported themselves to several footballing regulators previously upon taking over from Roman Abramovich in 2022, as they were understood to notice their financial irregularities while doing their due diligence amid that takeover.

Now that they have reached settlement agreements with UEFA and the Premier League, and concluded their charges with the FA, it finally brings an end to Chelsea's issues from their old ownership.

In a statement, Chelsea said: 'In 2022, the club self-reported potential historical rule breaches to all applicable regulators. Following that report, it has worked openly and transparently with all regulators, including voluntarily and proactively disclosing many thousands of documents.

'As previously announced, settlement agreements have been entered into with UEFA and the Premier League concerning the same self-reported regulatory matters and topics that have been addressed before. The club is pleased to confirm that, now the FA process has concluded, this brings all regulatory proceedings against the club to a close. We are grateful to UEFA, the Premier League and the FA for their engagement with the club throughout these processes.'

A statement from the FA read: 'A financial sanction of £10m and a suspended two-window registration ban have been imposed on Chelsea FC for breaches of the Football Association Football Agent Regulations, Regulations on Working with Intermediaries and Third Party Investment in Players Regulations. The FA charged Chelsea FC with 74 breaches of FA Rule E1.2 after its current ownership self-reported misconduct upon its purchase of the club. The FA is continuing to investigate individual misconduct arising out of this case.

'Chelsea FC admitted to the 74 breaches of FA Rule E1.2 prior to a hearing and an independent Regulatory Commission imposed a six-point deduction, which was to be suspended until June 30, 2027, and a £10m fine.

'The club appealed against the suspended points deduction and an independent Appeal Board allowed the appeal and set aside this sanction following a further hearing.

'In its place, the Appeal Board imposed a registration ban for two complete and consecutive transfer windows which is suspended until 30 June 2027.' The £10m fine was not subject to appeal and the full amount will be invested into grassroots football.

The punishment relates to activity under Chelsea's old ownership prior to BlueCo.

The Blues were hit with a £10million fine for making seven 'illegal' signings including David Luiz (left) and Ramires (right)

With the Premier League in March, Chelsea were previously fined £10m and handed a suspended transfer ban after admitting to making secret payments to unofficial agents between 2011 and 2018. That related to several transfers such as Eden Hazard, Samuel Eto'o, Willian, Ramires, David Luiz, Andre Schurrle and Nemanja Matic, though it should be noted that there is no suggestion of any wrongdoing on the part of those players. The £10m fine topped the £5.5m fine given to West Ham in 2007 over their signings of Javier Mascherano and Carlos Tevez.

Chelsea also received a nine-month academy transfer ban and a £750,000 fine over the registration of academy players between 2019 and 2022.

The Premier League did say at the time that the £10m fine would have been £20m, but was reduced by 50 per cent after Chelsea proactively self-reported and co-operated.

It was also concluded that Chelsea would not have breached the Premier League's Profitability and Sustainability rules during the applicable seasons in which they were investigated – even if the payments had been registered properly.

Sports.title: Tennis latest: US Open hit by withdrawal as Carlos Alcaraz stuns fans
Sports.content:
Tennis latest: US Open hit by withdrawal as Carlos Alcaraz stuns fans

The latest tennis headlines ahead of the last major of the season

View 3 Images Carlos Alcaraz has shocked his social media following (Image: Pablo Cuadra/Getty Images for Laureus)

An Australian tennis star who once beat the iconic Serena Williams has withdrawn from the US Open. Meanwhile, Carlos Alcaraz has left fans gobsmacked with a new look ahead of his impending return.

‌



The Spaniard has been sidelined for most of the 2026 season due to a recurring wrist injury. However, fans are building excitement for Alcaraz's return to Flushing Meadows as he shares recovery snaps on Instagram.

‌



Meanwhile, one star who won't be heading Stateside is Ajla Tomljanovic, who bid farewell to a "tough" campaign marred by minor injuries. The Australian announced her withdrawal from the US Open on social media and insists her focus is on the upcoming 2027 season.

‌



Here, Mirror Sport has all the latest tennis news.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Andrew Castle confirms immediate Wimbledon return after emotional BBC exit READ MORE :

Carlos Alcaraz stuns fans

Alcaraz is no stranger to reinventing his hairstyle, but his striking cornrow look has left supporters completely speechless. The Spaniard has experimented with a host of bold styles, having shaved his head at last year's US Open and drawing comparisons to a young David Beckham in the process.

‌



The 23-year-old went platinum blonde with cropped hair before the Laver Cup, before allowing it to grow back to his natural brunette shade ahead of the 2026 season. Following his Australian Open triumph and a string of injury-enforced withdrawals, Alcaraz reverted to a longer, more relaxed style.

This was the very same hairstyle he sported at the World Cup final, where he cheered on his beloved Spain as they defeated Argentina to lift the trophy. Now, eagle-eyed fans have clocked the tennis ace showcasing cornrows in a recent Instagram post.

View 3 Images Carlos Alcaraz is enjoying some new hairstyles (Image: Instagram)

‌



This snapshot was one of 16 images featured in the 'Insta dump' but supporters were most taken aback by this photograph. One branded the look the "unexpected hairstyle of the summer."

Another commented: "For 2 hot seconds... I thought I was looking at a young Drake, sorry Carlos, but glad you're enjoying the summer."

A third noted: "From Blondecaraz to Cornrowlitos, he keeps tennis stylish & fun!" Supporters also mentioned his eagerly-awaited return to tennis while praising his fresh appearance. One stated: "Can't wait to see you and the braids back on court."

‌



Meanwhile, another observed: "The hair we need you to take to the US Open!!"

Tomljanovic withdraws

View 3 Images Ajla Tomljanovic will not compete at Flushing Meadows (Image: Cameron Smith/Getty Images for LTA)

Tomljanovic has withdrawn from the US Open due to minor injuries that have coincided with a 'tough' season. The 33-year-old confirmed on social media that she won't be competing at Flushing Meadows next month and is focused on preparing for next year.

‌



Posting on Instagram, the Australian said: " It has been a tough year battling minor injuries, so I've decided to end my season earlier than planned to be healthy and ready for 2027."

Following her withdrawal, German tennis player Ella Seidel has been entered into the main draw. Tomljanovic's major tennis highlight came at the 2022 US Open, where she knocked Serena Williams out in the third round.

This proved to be Williams' last match ahead of her initial retirement, and the Australian paid tribute to her following the win. She said: "I'm feeling really sorry, just because I love Serena just as much as you guys do. And what she's done for me, for the sport of tennis, is incredible... she is the greatest of all time."

Sports.title: Glorious Goodwood tips: Saturday's best bets for EVERY race from our top tipster Newsboy
Sports.content:
Glorious Goodwood tips: Saturday's best bets for EVERY race from our top tipster Newsboy

The Coral Stewards Cup is the highlight of the final day of Glorious Goodwood and Newsboy has provided detailed analysis of that and all the other races on Saturday

View 7 Images Newsboy provides tips for Goodwood (Image: PA)

1.50 Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap: VALEDICTORY has the going-places profile, not to mention the local knowledge, to bid his rivals ‘adieu’.

‌



The gelded son of Cracksman, trained in tandem by John and Thady Gosden, has taken his form to a new level since stepping up to a mile and three quarters and being equipped with cheekpieces.

‌



The combination worked a treat when Valedictory beat six opponents over course and distance at the end of May with a length-and-a-half beating of Spinning Wheel. And William Buick’s partner defied a 5lb rise in the weights at Newmarket’s July Festival 22 days ago, getting the better of Roaring Legend by a neck.

‌



Danny Mullins fined £2,500 for conduct near crowd on fractious Willie Mullins horse READ MORE :

Rising star jockey makes history by completing huge Galway Festival double READ MORE :

The latest intervention from the British Horseracing Authority number cruncher means Valedictory, with another 3lb on his back, competes from a mark of 95 today.

But the four-year-old is only just finding his feet and, with more to come, Valedictory has strong claims on the hat-trick. Align The Stars landed this race two years ago and the Northumberland Plate hero has to be respected, along with the Joseph O’Brien pair Aeronautic and Small Fry .

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 VALEDICTORY, 2 ALIGN THE STARS, 3 AERONAUTIC

‌



View 7 Images Al Aasy: fancied by Newsboy (Image: PA)

2.25 Coral Glorious Stakes: AL AASY is evergreen - and ripe for the Glorious Stakes hat-trick. At nine years of age, William Haggas’s stable stalwart is well into the veteran stage of his career but continues to be more than a match for younger legs.

His 12 victories from 30 outings - that’s an impressive 40% strike-rate - include eight triumphs in Group 3 company.

‌



In 2024, Al Aasy beat Relentless Voyager for this prize and he returned 12 months ago to defend his title with a three-length humbling of Meydan.

That effort was all the more meritorious when one considers he carried a 3lb penalty for his success in the same-level Gordon Richards Stakes at Sandown Park in the spring.

There is no such encumbrance today and a return to winning form in Beverley’s Listed Charlie Wood Stakes at the beginning of the month will set Tom Marquand’s mount up perfectly for today

‌



The biggest danger may come from fellow Somerville Lodge trainee Opportunity, with In My Teens and Enfjaar taken to fight it out for the bronze.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 AL AASY, 2 OPPORTUNITY, 3 IN MY TEENS

View 7 Images Willam Haggas: trains Santorini Star (Image: Photo by Alan Crowhurst/Getty Images)

‌



3.00 Qatar Lillie Langtry Stakes: SANTORINI STAR merits the chance to bounce back from a no-show at Royal Ascot last month.

Her challenge for the Group 2 Hardwicke Stakes on the final day of the fixture went badly awry as the William Haggas-saddled mare, a 16-1 chance, came home last of 12 behind Giavellotto.

But forgive that effort - Santorini Star was stepping back to a mile and a half and wearing cheekpieces that are dispensed with today - and the five-year-old daughter of Golden Horn is a definite player here.

‌



Having beaten Consent for the Group 2 Park Hill Fillies’ Stakes at Doncaster in September - the runner-up reversed the form in the top-level Prix de Royallieu at Longchamp next time - Santorini Star made a winning comeback under Tom Marquand against male opposition in the Group 2 Jockey Club Stakes at Newmarket in May.

And she ran another cracker when beaten a short neck by Caballo De Mar for the Group 1 Prix Vicomtesse Vigier over two miles at Longchamp 20 days later, before her Ascot flop.

Santorini Star, a course winner from her only previous visit to Goodwood, will be more at home back up in distance and shouldn’t be written off. Waardah and Danielle finished first and second 12 in this months ago, and should be in the firing line once more.

‌



View 7 Images Sondad: Newsboy's pick (Image: Niall Carson/PA Wire)

3.35 Coral Stewards' Cup: SONDAD has landed two big sprint-handicap pots this season, and a third could be on the way.

The fitting of a visor saw the Washington DC-sired gelding take one step forward after another for the father-and-son training combination of Mick and David Easterby in 2025.

‌



Having scored at Ascot in May of last year, Sondad followed up in a six-furlong event on Derby day at Epsom, finishing his campaign with podium efforts in competitive sprints won by Candy at Ayr (Ayr Silver Cup) and Aramram at Ascot.

And the five-year-old has continued his upward curve this term, stepping forward from a down-the-field effort behind Dark Thirty at York in May to retain his crown at Epsom the following month.

The draw gods didn’t play ball in the Wokingham Handicap at Royal Ascot a fortnight later - his berth in stall two could hardly have been worse - and, in the circumstance, a ninth behind Double Rush rates a commendable effort.

‌



But there were no such issues in another big-money affair on the Irish Oaks undercard at the Curragh last time, when Sondad and Easterby snr’s grand-daughter Jo Mason accounted for old rival Dark Thirty by half a length. He’s 1lb well in under a 6lb penalty and a draw in stall 21 should put Sondad in the thick of the action.

In a typically fiendish Stewards’ Cup, Far Above Dream, Annaf, Stratusnine and 2024 victor Get It are just four horses capable of getting involved.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 SONDAD, 2 FAR ABOVE DREAM, 3 GET IT

‌



View 7 Images Karl Burke: trains Newsboy's tip (Image: PA)

4.10 Phase Eight Handicap: NAVAL LIGHT and 3lb claimer Jack Nicholls are expected to prove a potent combination for the third time in a row.

The winner’s enclosure proved elusive for Havana Grey’s son on his first six visits to the racecourse. But, on the back of a sixth to Ten Carat Harry in a six-furlong handicap at Newmarket on 2,000 Guineas day, Naval Light, ridden by Nicholls for the first time, enjoyed a red-letter day when justifying odds of 2-5 in a maiden over the same trip at Pontefract 20 days later.

‌



Karl Burke then returned the gelded three-year-old to handicap company as Naval Light and Nicholls took on three rivals over seven furlongs at Catterick Bridge.

Sent off at 7-2, my selection swept through from the back of the field to lead inside the final furlong and account for Woodstock by a length and three-quarters.

Hot favourite Haaderr disappointed that day and more is need after a 5lb rise in the weights. But it will be a surprise if Naval Light can’t summon up another personal best and he’s fancied to go in again.

‌



We’re Goosers found the draw, and possibly the one-mile distance, against him in the Britannia Handicap at Royal Ascot and he heads the list of dangers, which also includes Ghost Mode and Ironwill.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 NAVAL LIGHT, 2 WE’RE GOOSERS, 3 IRONWILL

View 7 Images James Doyle: rides Newsboy's tip (Image: PA)

‌



4.45 British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes: MARKET LEADER did enough on his debut at Windsor, despite a defeat at odds-on, to be of interest here.

Punters were falling over themselves to back the 450,000-Euro breeze-up purchase when he took on eight opponents for a six-furlong novice stakes at Windsor 19 days ago - Market Leader went off the 4-5 hotpot.

But they were soon biting their nails when James Doyle’s partner made a sluggish exit from the starting stalls and trailed the field during the early exchanges.

‌



Market Leader then appeared nonplussed when his jockey urged him forwards inside the final quarter mile but did learn on the job in coming home in third, four lengths behind winner Real Bullet.

Given his obvious lack of streetwisdom, Market Leader, who holds an entry in the Group 1 Vincent O’Brien National Stakes at the Curragh next month, looks capable of a big step forward, and the seventh furlong should help.Regency Royal, Speakers Corner and Leadlight all performed with promise first time up and should improve

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 MARKET LEADER, 2 REGENCY ROYAL, 3 SPEAKERS CORNER

‌



View 7 Images Clive Cox trains Newsboy pick (Image: PA)

5.20 Coral Rewards Shaker Handicap: BLUE COURVOISIER, another horse who missed out on the luck of the draw at Royal Ascot, makes plenty of appeal under Saffie Osborne.

The debut winner of a Leicester novice stakes on his first of two outings as a two-year-old in 2025, the son of Sea The Stars made the frame in handicaps at Newmarket and Ascot when returning in the spring.

‌



With Osborne on board for the first time, Blue Courvoisier gave his trainer Clive Cox a third Silver Bowl triumph when holding Langstone by a length and a half at Carlisle - the one-mile handicap was switched from Haydock Park - at the end of May.

Blue Courvoisier couldn’t get involved from stall one when 18th of 30 in the Britannia Handicap but shouldn’t be written off.

In a wide-open meeting finale, Crest Of Fire, El Matador, Boyfriend and Great Chieftain are names to throw into the mix.

Sports.title: Real Madrid make final Vinicius Jr decision as Arsenal put on transfer red alert
Sports.content:
Real Madrid make final Vinicius Jr decision as Arsenal put on transfer red alert

Vinicius Jr has just one year left on his deal at Real Madrid and Arsenal hope to tempt the forward to join them at the Emirates Stadium this summer

View 2 Images Vinicius Junior is a transfer target for Arsenal (Image: (Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty Images))

Real Madrid have tabled a final take it or leave it contract offer to Vinicius Junior as he continues to attract interest from Arsenal. The Gunners have enquired about the Brazil international, as boss Mikel Arteta wants to sign proven talent this summer.

‌



Vinicius fits the bill, winning 14 trophies and scoring 128 goals in 375 matches for the Spanish giants, but he only has one year remaining on his current deal. Real have tried to renew Vinicius' deal and opened further talks with him earlier this week, but with no progress made, they have now hit their star man with an ultimatum.

‌



According to Spanish publication Marca, the La Liga giants have informed the 26-year-old’s camp that the latest contract offer they submitted is final and there will be no further increase nor another round of negotiations. If Vinicius accepts, his deal will be renewed, however, if he rejects the offer Real will open the door to a sale this summer to prevent the Brazilian from entering his final year of contract year and leaving for free later, according to Marca.

‌



The Gunners have already bolstered their attacking options this summer with the £34million signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge earlier this month. Arteta admitted he will 'require a better squad and better individuals' for the forthcoming season in an interview with the club’s inhouse media channels earlier this week.

He said: “This has to be the start and this has to be the standard. Excellence has to be our standard and this has to drive us to attack the future.

Sports.title: Matthias Jaissle can hand Newcastle chance to sign title winner and help fill Anthony Gordon void
Sports.content:
Matthias Jaissle can hand Newcastle chance to sign title winner and help fill Anthony Gordon void

Newcastle United look to be closing in on appointing Matthias Jaissle as the replacement for Eddie Howe.

View 2 Images Newcastle United look set to appoint Matthias Jaissle as their new head coach. (Image: Yasser Bakhsh/Getty Images))

It’s set to be all change for Newcastle United this summer, both in the dugout and on the pitch. After five years in charge of the club, Eddie Howe has left St James’ Park.

‌



The news broke just a matter of hours after the 4-1 friendly defeat against Championship side Bristol City. It seems to be a time of Chaos for Newcastle.

‌



The manager is said to have made the decision, which follows the sales of Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon earlier this summer. Gordon moved to Barcelona for a fee of £69.3 million, with Tonali completing a £100 million transfer to Tottenham.

‌



The Premier League special edition is on sale now READ MORE :

Bruno Guimaraes pushes for Arsenal transfer with Newcastle agreement imminent READ MORE :

There is also speculation over the futures of both Bruno Guimaraes and Lewis Hall. Arsenal are being strongly linked with Guimaraes , and Manchester United interested in Hall.

For Newcastle, the focus will be on bringing in replacements for Howe and handling any outgoings between now and the Premier League opener. The Magpies seem to be closing in on a deal for Al-Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle.

If that appointment is made, then it could potentially open up the door for Newcastle to move for a former Premier League title winner, who could help to fill some of the void of the quality left by the sales.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

While at Al-Ahil, Jaissle has worked closely with Riyad Mahrez. Under the German coach, he played 122 games, scoring 37 times and providing 50 assists.

The 35-year-old officially left the club this summer and is now available on a free transfer. He could be a player who Jaissle could turn to as he looks to make an impact at Newcastle.

‌



Mahrez’s age and the fact that he has been playing in Saudi Arabia means that he may not be expected to start every game. Newcastle have already brought in a replacement for Gordon in Bazoumana Toure.

View 2 Images Riyad Mahrez is available on a free transfer this summer. (Image: Ercin Erturk/Anadolu via Getty Images)

But, Mahrez, who has won five Premier League titles with Leicester City and Manchester City, would no doubt add some Premier League know-how and quality to Newcastle’s squad.

‌



Speaking about his relationship with Mahrez in December 2024, Jaissle told RMC Sport: "Mahrez is a fantastic footballer, I have a very good relationship with him. And I think if you ask him, he'll probably tell you the same thing.

“I can only say that I'm really happy to have him on the team. He's an incredible player, he's won everything. And he's showing it again this year with the difference he's able to make during matches.”

Mahrez captained Algeria in this summer’s World Cup, scoring twice and providing an assist in his four appearances in the competition. He announced his retirement from international football following the tournament, meaning he’ll be concentrating on his club career.

Article continues below

Fabrizio Romano reports that he is keen to return to Europe, with Serie A Clubs showing an interest. Despite his age, having the chance to sign someone of Mahrez’s quality may be one that Newcastle shouldn’t turn down.

Sports.title: Newcastle United confirm Eddie Howe exit with statement issued as replacement lined up
Sports.content:
Newcastle United confirm Eddie Howe exit with statement issued as replacement lined up

Eddie Howe ended Newcastle United's barren run without a major trophy but will now depart the club after nearly five years of service

View 2 Images Eddie Howe has walked away from his role as Newcastle United boss (Image: MI News/NurPhoto)

Newcastle United have confirmed Eddie Howe has resigned from his position as manager. Earlier reports had stated the Englishman was set to walk away from the club after nearly five years at the helm.

‌



He was the first permanent manager to be appointed by the club after the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund's takeover toward the end of 2021. The ex-Bournemouth manager guided the Magpies into the Champions League on two occasions and won the League Cup to end their 70-year wait without a trophy.

‌



However, things grew more difficult for Howe when Alexander Isak joined Liverpool for £125million and while around £240m was spent on new signings, the club struggled to a 12th placed Premier League finish. After seeing Anthony Gordon join Barcelona, Sandro Tonali join Tottenham Hotspur for £100m and Bruno Guimaraes inform the club he also wants to depart, Howe's resignation has been confirmed.

‌



Newcastle confirmed the news in a statement, which read: "Newcastle United can announce that Eddie Howe has informed the club of his decision to step down as head coach.

Bruno Guimaraes pushes for Arsenal transfer with Newcastle agreement imminent READ MORE :

Bruno Guimaraes given separate Newcastle plan as showdown transfer talks scheduled READ MORE :

"The club has accepted Eddie’s decision and would like to thank him for his extraordinary contribution.

"Also leaving the club are coaches Jason Tindall, Graeme Jones, Stephen Purches and Simon Weatherstone, and head of performance Dan Hodges."

‌



Howe went on to issue an emotional farewell message to Newcastle fans, with the 48-year-old saying: “After a period of personal reflection, I have decided that now is the right time for me to step away from my role as head coach of Newcastle United.

“After nearly five years of giving my life, heart and soul into the club with unrelenting energy, I feel that it is in the best interests of both myself and the club to step away, recharge and take a break.

“Although it’s been incredibly difficult to make this decision, I know in my heart that it’s the right one. I have always put the best interests of Newcastle before my own in every single decision I have made whilst I’ve been here and this one is no different.

‌



“It has been the privilege of my lifetime to have been the manager of Newcastle United.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

“It is difficult to put into words what this club, the city and its supporters mean, and will always mean, to me and my family. From the moment myself, Jason and all of the staff arrived nearly half a decade ago, Newcastle instantly felt like home and the people here welcomed us with open arms. We took huge pride in representing the club from day one and this city will always hold a very special place in our hearts.

‌



“There have been so many incredible moments in our time here. From fighting relegation in our first season to the numerous unforgettable nights at St. James’ Park in the Champions League soon after. The progression was fast.

“Everyone came together, united and what a force we became, culminating in bringing home our first domestic trophy in 70 years. These are all memories that I will cherish for the rest of my life.

“I would like to put on record my sincere thanks and appreciation to Yasir Al-Rumayyan, Jamie Reuben, Jacobo Solís and everyone at PIF, David Hopkinson, Ross Wilson and the entire ownership and leadership group for placing their trust in me and for giving me the opportunity to lead this special football club.

‌



“I remain incredibly positive and enthusiastic about the future of Newcastle. The club is in fantastic hands with a great leadership team and I have no doubt together, alongside whoever comes in to replace me, they will continue to deliver success on the pitch.

View 2 Images Eddie Howe has officially left Newcastle United (Image: David Davies/PA Wire)

“Thank you to Jason Tindall, Graeme Jones, Stephen Purches, Simon Weatherstone, Dan Hodges, Andy Howe and Jordan Tribe for their incredible loyalty, support and dedication and to all of the amazing staff behind the scenes whose hard work and loyalty makes this club what it is.

‌



“A special thank you to all of the players who have represented the club during my time here. Without you, nothing would have been possible and it’s been an honour to have coached you all.

“Finally, and most importantly, thank you to our incredible supporters. Your passion and loyalty have inspired me every single day. To stand on the touchline at St. James’ Park as your manager with the honour of representing your club has meant more to me than you will ever know.

“While my journey as manager has now come to an end, the affinity and love I will always hold for Newcastle United never will.

‌



“Thank you for everything. I wish the club every success for the future.”

Matthias Jaissle, 38, is expected to become the next Newcastle manager having previously coached Saudi Arabian side Al-Ahli, who he guided to two Asian Cup titles, the continent's version of the Champions League.
