World.title: Croatia–US Economic Relations: Tax Changes Open Doors for Diaspora Business
World.content:
July the 31st, 2026 – Croatia-US economic relations have seen a new chapter in the (apparently very long) book penned, opening doors for diaspora business.

These new and upcoming tax changes will open doors for businesses operating between the two countries, as well as for the Croatian diaspora who might need another more concrete reason to seek citizenship.

For very many decades, the relationship between Croatia and the United States has been built on more than diplomacy. It has been shaped by migration, family ties, investment, and the millions of people of Croatian heritage who have made the United States their home. Now, a brand new step in that relationship could reshape how Croats and Americans do business, invest, and maintain connections across the pond.

the old double taxation hurdle…

A long-awaited agreement on avoiding double taxation between Croatia and the United States is finally moving closer to implementation, bringing the possibility of greater financial certainty for individuals and companies operating between the two countries. Until relatively recently, this all seemed to move at a glacial pace, with many in both Croatia and the diaspora forgetting about much movement at all on the issue.

For Croatian citizens living abroad, especially the large Croatian-American community, the changes represent more than a technical tax issue. They are part of a broader trend: Croatia is becoming increasingly connected economically, legally, and professionally with its diaspora. For a great many descendants of Croatian emigrants, that renewed connection may raise an important question about whether or not now be the right moment to formally reconnect with Croatia and gain citizenship.

croatia and america, a story of immigration, migration and struggle

Ancient Croatia and the very new United States have a relationship that extends far beyond modern state diplomacy that we see all countries at least attempting to engage in in the modern day. From the waves of Croatian migration that took place back during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, to the creation of strong Croatian communities across major US cities such as Chicago, Cleveland, Pittsburgh, and New York, generations of Croatian-Americans maintained cultural and family links with their ancestral homeland.

During Croatia’s struggle for independence in the 1990s, the diaspora played a significant role in raising awareness of Croatia’s position internationally. Since Croatia gained independence back during the 1990s, relations with the United States have expanded into security cooperation, tourism, technology, investment, and trade. Looking at the situation as it is today, this relationship is entering a new economic phase, one where easier movement of capital, business opportunities, and legal certainty are becoming increasingly crucial.

Why this Tax Agreement Matters (in more ways than one)

Obviously, the primary goal of the Croatia–US income tax agreement is to reduce uncertainty for people and companies that have financial ties to both countries. Currently, individuals and businesses operating across borders often face complicated questions about where exactly any income actually be taxed, and how this problematic double taxation can be avoided.

They’re the basic questions. It becomes more complex as you delve deeper, with questions about what rules apply when investing, opening a company, receiving dividends, or earning income abroad often becoming too much for many. Understandably so.

The agreement aims to provide clearer rules and reduce situations where the same income could potentially be taxed twice. It includes measures related to withholding taxes, information exchange, dispute resolution, and mechanisms designed to create a more predictable environment for cross-border activity. A protocol signed in 2026 further addressed outstanding issues and is intended to support the treaty’s progress toward US Senate consideration.

For businesses, this could mean greater confidence when investing between Croatia and the United States. For individuals, especially those with connections to both countries, it could simplify financial decisions and encourage closer economic links.

A New Opportunity for americans with croatian ancestors who might want croatian and eu passports

The Croatian diaspora has always been one of Croatia’s greatest assets. Indeed, there are now more ethnic Croats born and living outside of Croatia than there are living in it. Millions of people around the world have Croatian roots, but many have never formally explored their legal connection to Croatia. There are a wide array of reasons for that. For descendants of Croatian emigrants, being granted Croatian (and as such EU) citizenship can represent more than a passport. It can be a practical bridge to easier access to life, work, and property ownership in Croatia and the European Union, much stronger connections with family heritage, new business and investment possibilities and the ability to participate more directly and concretely in Croatia’s future.

For many Americans with Croatian ancestry, the gap between loving dida’s war stories or enjoying Dalmatian gregada was comfortable, but there wasn’t enough of an urge there to try to get a Croatian passport. America is a country filled with people who value economic success and the grind in a way few in Europe do. For many, pursuing citizenship would need an extra push wrapped in a more economic bow.

As Croatia becomes more economically integrated with countries such as the United States, citizenship can become increasingly valuable for those who want to maintain a meaningful connection with their ancestral homeland, all while seeking business opportunities without getting ravelled up and ultimately strangled in red tape. Many members of the diaspora already visit Croatia every year. Some invest in properties, start businesses, or consider spending more time in the country. Formal citizenship can be the next step in turning a cultural connection into a legal and practical one, all without the threat of Croatia’s infamous bureaucracy on steroids.

From Tourism to Investment: Croatia’s Changing Image Abroad

For decades, Croatia’s global reputation was primarily connected to tourism. It would be a lie to say that is no longer the case, but things are altering. Now, the country is increasingly positioning itself as a place for investment, entrepreneurship, technology, and international cooperation. A more predictable tax environment with the United States could encourage additional economic activity, particularly among Croatian-Americans who already understand both markets. The massive Croatian diaspora has a unique advantage: many already have knowledge of American business culture while maintaining personal ties to Croatia. That combination can create opportunities in areas ranging from technology and renewable energy to tourism, manufacturing, real estate, and services.

What Comes Next and what does this all really mean?

In practical terms, the implementation of the Croatia–US tax agreement will depend on completion of the necessary procedures in both countries. There are still a few hurdles to jump, but the direction is clear and the track is getting shorter. Croatia and the United States are moving toward a closer economic relationship, and the Croatian diaspora is positioned at the centre of that connection.

For descendants of Croatian emigrants who have always felt connected to Croatia but never explored citizenship, this may be a moment worth genuinely considering. As Croatia strengthens its global economic position, those with Croatian heritage are increasingly asking not only where their ancestors came from and exploring their origins for emotional reasons, but what concrete, economic and business opportunities their Croatian identity can provide today.

croatianbydescent – turning heritage into opportunity

Croatian by Descent has helped many Americans pursue their interest in gaining Croatian citizenship, as it goes without saying that few know where to even begin. For the vast majority of the Croatian diaspora, the connection to Croatia has always existed through family traditions, language, memories, and annual visits to the coast and islands. However, as Croatia’s role in the European and global economy continues to grow, more descendants of Croatian emigrants are exploring what it means to make that connection official.

Obtaining Croatian citizenship is increasingly viewed not only as a way to preserve family heritage, but also as an opportunity to strengthen personal and professional ties with Croatia and the European Union. For those who qualify, citizenship can open the door to greater mobility, easier long-term stays, investment opportunities, and a deeper relationship with the country their ancestors once called home.

Navigating the Croatian citizenship process, however, can involve complex documentation, historical records, and legal requirements, especially for descendants whose families left Croatia generations ago. The attitude you’re likely to receive as you attempt to do all this is also a bit of a culture shock for many Americans used to smiles and client-facing service. This, is, let’s say… not so common in Croatia!

It’s precisely why many choose to work with the likes of Croatian by Descent, who understand both Croatian regulations and the unique challenges faced by applicants living abroad. They have noted an uptick in those seeking their services and help as more and more of the diaspora look to Croatia as more than just sunshine and sea in their ancestral village each summer. As Croatia and the United States enter a new era of economic cooperation, reconnecting with Croatia through actual citizenship may become an increasingly valuable step for a new generation of Croatian-Americans looking to turn their heritage into a permanent, unbreakable connection cemented with (another), stronger blue passport.

World.title: Svetac: The Remote Island Where History and Nature Meet
World.content:
July the 31st, 2026 – Svetac is a very remote Croatian island where abandoned history and wild, untamed nature come together in perfect harmony without any interference from humanity.

Hidden far out in the Adriatic Sea, just west of the far-flung island of Vis, the small island of Svetac is one of Croatia’s most isolated destinations. Also known as Sveti Andrija, the small offshore island is renowned for its dramatic cliffs, fascinating past, unique wildlife and complete and utter absence of permanent residents.

Located around 30 nautical miles from the mainland, Putni kofer writes that Svetac belongs to the Vis archipelago and lies just 2.5 kilometres from the volcanic islet of Brusnik. Throughout history it has been known by several names, including Sant’Andrea during Venetian rule and the local name Štondrija.

“a place for dreamers and madmen”

The island’s rugged coastline makes landing difficult. Towering cliffs surround much of the shore, leaving Slatina Bay on the southeastern side as the only practical place for boats to come ashore. Above the coast rises Kosa, the island’s highest peak at 316 metres, while strong sea currents and open waters add to its reputation as one of Croatia’s most challenging islands to reach. Croatian poet Tin Ujević famously described it as a place “for dreamers and madmen.”

Svetac also stands out for its climate. It is considered the warmest location in Croatia, with temperatures never falling below freezing. The island’s average annual temperature is around 17.4 degrees Celsius, comparable to Mediterranean locations such as Malta.

uninhabited since the year 2000…

Despite its isolation, Svetac has a long history of human settlement. Archaeological discoveries include ancient anchors, Roman remains and the ruins of a Byzantine fort. Benedictine monks lived on the island during the 15th and 16th centuries before ownership later passed to the Zanki family, who arrived from Italy’s Gargano Peninsula in the mid-18th century. The family originally settled there to harvest pine resin, leading many people to refer to Svetac as “the island of the Zankis.”

The island’s harsh environment has always made life difficult. There is no natural source of drinking water, strong winds frequently batter the coast and powerful southerly storms have claimed lives over the centuries. For generations, fishermen provided the islanders’ only connection to the outside world, sometimes becoming stranded themselves when rough seas prevented them from leaving. The final permanent resident died in January 2000, leaving the island uninhabited ever since.

wildlife and nature – svetac’s greatest treasures

Nature remains one of Svetac’s greatest treasures. Carob trees grow across the island, while it provides habitat for Eleonora’s falcon and Europe’s largest owl species. Mediterranean monk seals once frequented its shores, and the surrounding waters were historically rich in lobsters.

The island also carries a darker legend. Its pine forests were once heavily exploited for resin used in shipbuilding, while shepherds grazing church-owned sheep were said to have killed English shipwreck survivors. According to local tradition, this earned Svetac the nickname “Devil’s Island” among British sailors, reinforcing its reputation as a mysterious and forbidding place.

Today, although no one lives permanently on Svetac, its untouched landscapes, remarkable history and remote location continue to fascinate travellers looking to discover one of Croatia’s last truly wild islands.

World.title: Croatia Plans Taxi Fare Caps to End Excessive Charges
World.content:
July the 31st, 2026 – Croatia is planning to finally deal with the taxi fare issue with caps and a hope to end excessive charges and frequent tourist rip-offs during summer.

Croatia is preparing to introduce a new set of rules for the taxi industry that will allow the government to cap fares, aiming to protect passengers from excessive prices while ensuring drivers can continue operating sustainably. Poslovni reports that the measures form part of amendments to the Road Transport Act, which have already been approved by Parliament and are expected to reshape the country’s taxi market.

Under the new legislation, the Minister of Maritime Affairs, Transport and Infrastructure will be authorised to set maximum fares for all key components of a taxi ride, including the starting fare, per-kilometre rate, waiting time, and per-minute charges. The goal is to prevent extreme price spikes that have generated negative publicity, particularly in tourist destinations.

The reform follows several high-profile incidents in which passengers, including foreign tourists, were charged hundreds or even thousands of euros for relatively short journeys. Those cases prompted calls for stronger consumer protection and greater transparency across the industry.

The government says the new framework is intended to strike a balance between protecting customers and ensuring taxi drivers receive fair compensation. Officials have been working with representatives of the taxi sector, digital ride-hailing platforms and consumer groups to develop a pricing model that avoids both unreasonably low fares and excessive charges.

The legislation also introduces several additional changes designed to improve oversight of the sector. Every taxi vehicle will require its own operating permit, while specially designated TX licence plates will make licensed taxis easier to identify. Authorities are also strengthening checks on drivers and expanding enforcement powers to police, customs officers and municipal inspectors.

Digital ride-hailing platforms will face tighter regulation as well. They will be required to work only with properly licensed operators and maintain records that allow authorities to verify compliance with Croatian transport regulations.

The government believes the reforms will create a more transparent, competitive and reliable taxi market, improving confidence among both residents and the millions of visitors who use taxi services each year. The new rules are expected to take effect following the implementation of the amended Road Transport Act.

World.title: €20 Million Investment Aims to Transform Continental Croatian Tourism
World.content:
July the 31st, 2026 – A massive investment is aiming to totally transform continental Croatian tourism, with the majority of the focus on the overlooked Daruvar Spa.

Croatia has officially unveiled the fully renovated and expanded Daruvar Spa, a €20 million project that the government says marks a major step in strengthening the country’s continental tourism and positioning it as a leading European destination for health and wellness travel.

Poslovni reports that Prime Minister Andrej Plenković attended the opening ceremony, describing the project as one of 15 major investments designed to reshape Croatia’s tourism offer beyond the Adriatic coast. He noted that €13.2 million of the investment was financed through the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (NPOO), while the overall goal is to create a year-round tourism industry with high-quality facilities that attract visitors throughout all seasons, not just the summer months.

The renovation has transformed one of Croatia’s oldest spa resorts, whose history stretches back nearly 2,000 years, into a modern wellness and rehabilitation destination. The project included the complete reconstruction of 77 existing accommodation units and the construction of 13 new rooms at the Hotel Termal.

Guests can now enjoy newly renovated thermal pools featuring massage zones, an expanded sun deck, and a modern pool bar. The investment also introduced a new recreational and tourism centre with a multifunctional sports hall that will be used by both spa visitors and Croatian war veterans staying at the nearby Veterans’ Centre.

Among the new wellness facilities are beer baths, oak baths, salt rooms, cryotherapy chambers, and hyperbaric chambers. Spa director Ratko Vuković described the beer and oak baths as unique products that reflect Daruvar’s local identity and wellness tradition.

Local officials called the redevelopment a turning point for the region. Daruvar Mayor Damir Lneniček said it is the city’s largest investment in the past 45 years, adding that it will stimulate not only tourism but the broader local economy. Bjelovar-Bilogora County Prefect Marko Marušić said the upgraded spa has the potential to become the “locomotive” of Croatia’s health tourism sector by setting new standards in quality and visitor experience.

The project also focused on sustainability and digitalisation. Alongside modernising the facilities, the investment included a digital transformation of operations, the installation of photovoltaic power systems, and electric vehicle charging stations to improve energy efficiency and reduce environmental impact.

According to Plenković, the Daruvar project is part of a broader national strategy involving 15 spa and health tourism developments, with 10 located in continental Croatia and five along the coast. The wider programme is backed by a €356 million tourism investment package, of which €320 million comes from the National Recovery and Resilience Plan.

Other destinations included in the programme are Veli Lošinj, Stubičke Toplice, Lipik, Varaždinske Toplice, Topusko, Terme Bjelovar, Biograd na Moru, Makarska, Crikvenica, and the island of Korčula. The government says the investments are intended to diversify Croatia’s tourism offer, reduce seasonal dependence, and strengthen the country’s position in the growing European health and wellness tourism market.

Although continental Croatia currently accounts for less than five percent of the country’s total tourism traffic, officials believe projects such as the redevelopment of Daruvar Spa will help unlock its significant growth potential by attracting domestic and international visitors throughout the year while creating new economic opportunities for local communities.

World.title: Chevron CFO bullish on Iraq after West Qurna 2, Nassiriya agreements
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Chevron boasts “significant potential” to expand its activities in Iraq over the next decade, according to Chief Financial Officer Eimear Bonner, highlighting the US oil company’s increasing trust in the country’s energy sector after recent deals with Baghdad.

Speaking to Bloomberg, Bonner said that Iraq remained one of Chevron’s top priority markets for future production expansion after the signing of preliminary agreements to pursue negotiations on the massive West Qurna 2 and Nassiriya oil fields.

She added that Chevron has been encouraged by its interaction with Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi and Iraq’s Ministry of Oil while discussions continue and that the corporation is also collaborating with Baghdad on diverse crude export routes to boost Iraq’s long-term energy security.

The statements bolster rising trust among foreign energy corporations after Al-Zaidi’s visit to the United States earlier this month, during which Iraq inked more than $60 billion in investment deals covering energy, infrastructure, banking, and technology.

World.title: Syria joins Saudi Arabia, Jordan in warning Iraq over Iran-backed militias
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Syria has joined Saudi Arabia and Jordan in warning Baghdad that strikes conducted from Iraqi soil against neighboring nations may result in military strikes against the armed groups responsible, according to Syrian military officials cited by regional media.

According to Al Jazeera and the US-funded Al Hurra, a senior Syrian military source said that Damascus will react to any strikes from Iraq by attacking the “terrorist militias” involved inside Iraqi territory.

The purported warning comes amid a steep increase in regional tensions after US-Saudi bombings against Iran-backed militias in Iraq in retaliation for drone assaults on Saudi oil installations, which Riyadh said were conducted from Iraqi territory.

The Iraqi government has frequently said that it would not allow Iraqi land to be used as a launchpad for attacks on neighboring nations.

Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi recently issued an order establishing a comprehensive security strategy aimed at enhancing state authority and preventing armed organizations from endangering regional security.

The new threat puts further pressure on Baghdad, as more neighboring nations indicate they may take direct action if cross-border assaults continue.

Iraqi authorities have attempted to prevent such a situation, claiming that security activities should be overseen by the Iraqi government rather than foreign forces.

Several Iran-backed organizations operating inside Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) are at the heart of the conflict, including Kataib Hezbollah, Asaib Ahl al-Haq, Harakat al-Nujaba, and Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada.

While the PMF is technically part of Iraq’s security system, some of its sections have strong links to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and have been accused by regional governments of carrying out strikes outside of Baghdad’s jurisdiction.

For Iraq, the diplomatic stakes go beyond security.

Baghdad has been attempting to reestablish ties with Syria as part of greater regional economic integration, including talks on resurrecting the old Iraq-Syria oil pipeline to the Mediterranean, which is considered strategically crucial for diversifying Iraq’s export routes outside the Gulf.

The purported Syrian warning comes at a critical moment for Al-Zaidi’s administration, which has spent recent months bolstering relations with Washington, Ankara, Riyadh, and Damascus while portraying Iraq as a secure destination for global investment.

The mounting threats from neighboring Arab governments highlight the importance of Baghdad demonstrating its ability to prevent armed groups from conducting strikes independent of the state.

Failure to do so risks increasing regional military tensions and jeopardizing Iraq’s aspirations to boost commerce, energy cooperation, and infrastructure projects with its neighbors.

The Syrian government has not issued an official warning, and IraqiNews.com has not independently confirmed the statements ascribed to the Syrian military source.

However, the claims reflect rising regional worry that strikes by Iran-backed militias operating from Iraqi soil could further destabilize the area and hamper Iraq’s diplomatic and economic goals.

World.title: Iran-backed militias threaten Iraq’s ties with US and Gulf
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Escalating tensions between Iran-backed militias are providing one of the most serious hurdles yet to Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s ambitions to deepen ties with the United States and Gulf states while luring billions of dollars in international investment.

The most recent crisis followed US-Saudi airstrikes on Iran-aligned armed groups in Iraq, when Saudi Arabia accused militias operating from Iraqi territory of firing drones at oil installations in the kingdom’s Eastern Province.

Riyadh claimed that the operation targeted the militias responsible for the assaults rather than the Iraqi state or its military forces, but Baghdad denounced the strikes as a breach of national sovereignty.

The recent tensions are being fueled by numerous prominent Iran-aligned organizations operating inside Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), notably Kataib Hezbollah, Asaib Ahl al-Haq, Harakat al-Nujaba, and Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada.

While the PMF is technically part of Iraq’s security apparatus, many of its groups have strong links to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and have occasionally conducted operations outside of Baghdad’s chain of command.

Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi responded by calling an emergency meeting of the Ministerial Council for National Security, canceling a planned trip to Saudi Arabia, and announcing a comprehensive security strategy to prevent Iraqi territory from being used to launch attacks on neighboring countries.

The administration also reiterated its resolve to keep all weapons entirely under state control.

That vow has gained importance after Al-Zaidi’s visit to Washington earlier this month, during which Iraq and the United States reiterated their commitment to completing the US-led coalition operation by the end of September 2026.

During the visit, Al-Zaidi pledged to ensure that all weapons eventually come into the control of the Iraqi state, citing it as a cornerstone of his government’s security strategy and a crucial step toward bolstering Iraq’s sovereignty and stability.

Since entering office, Al-Zaidi has maintained a policy of balancing Iraq’s ties with rival regional and international forces.

During recent travels to Washington, Ankara, and Tehran, he achieved huge investment and cooperation deals totaling tens of billions of dollars in the energy, banking, technology, infrastructure, and industrial sectors.

His administration has also attempted to strengthen connections with Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Turkey, and other Gulf nations via new transportation corridors, energy alliances, and trade agreements aimed at diversifying Iraq’s economy beyond oil and positioning the country as a regional center linking the Gulf to Europe.

According to analysts, Baghdad’s approach is highly dependent on proving that the Iraqi state, rather than armed groups, controls the country’s security and foreign policy.

Continued strikes from Iraqi territory risk eroding the country’s reputation with major regional allies and international investors, at a time when foreign investment has risen after years of turmoil.

The stakes rose when US President Donald Trump said that recent US-Saudi operations against Iran-backed militias were coordinated with the Iraqi government, a claim Baghdad has denied.

Observers believe it reflects rising discontent among Iraq’s leadership with armed groups accused of dragging the nation into regional conflicts that contradict Baghdad’s diplomatic and economic interests.

Al-Zaidi is currently facing the most significant test of his leadership.

Delivering on his promise to place all weapons under state control will be critical not only for Iraq’s internal security but also for maintaining trust with the United States, Gulf Arab states, and international investors, many of whom support many of the country’s largest economic projects.

Baghdad’s dilemma now extends beyond managing ties between Washington and Tehran.

It demonstrates that the Iraqi state possesses both the authority and the political will to prevent Iran-backed militias from using Iraqi territory to launch attacks that risk isolating the country, harming relations with Arab neighbors and the United States, and jeopardizing Iraq’s long-term economic recovery and investment goals.

World.title: Iraq faces growing fiscal strain
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is under increasing financial strain as plummeting oil earnings tighten government budgets, with Health Minister Abdul Hussein al-Mousawi saying that ensuring monthly public-sector wages has become the government’s top priority.

Speaking at a public meeting, al-Mousawi stated that the government requires approximately 10.8 trillion Iraqi dinars ($8.2 billion) per month to pay public-sector salaries, while current monthly oil revenues have fallen to approximately 2.5 trillion dinars, highlighting the growing gap between government obligations and income.

The statements are one of the most direct public acknowledgements by a top Iraqi official of the government’s financial challenges after months of decreased oil prices and fewer export profits.

Iraq’s government finances remain very vulnerable to variations in global energy markets because the vast bulk of public revenue comes from crude oil.

Official figures published this week indicated that oil accounted for over 84% of federal income in the first five months of 2026, but collections decreased by more than one-third compared to the same time the previous year as oil prices and export profits plummeted.

The health minister also warned of financing restrictions in the healthcare sector, citing worries about the supply of medications and the government’s capacity to sustain public services if financial pressures continue.

The fresh warnings follow weeks of increased regional tensions, which disrupted oil markets and added uncertainty to Iraq’s economic prospects.

As OPEC’s second-largest producer, Iraq relies on oil exports to fund wages, pensions, social welfare, and the majority of government expenditure, making the budget susceptible to long-term reductions in crude prices.

Economists have long cautioned that Iraq’s reliance on oil income makes the nation susceptible to external shocks, while a hefty public-sector pay bill constrains the government’s budgetary flexibility.

Previous administrations attempted to diversify income streams via tax changes and non-oil investments, but hydrocarbons remain the economy’s backbone.

The financial pressure comes at a critical time for Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s government, which has been promoting Iraq as a destination for billions of dollars in foreign investment following agreements signed with US, Turkish, and international companies in energy, banking, technology, and infrastructure.

Continued budgetary strain may make it more urgent to accelerate economic reforms, raise non-oil income, and improve public financial management to lessen Iraq’s reliance on petroleum exports.

They also emphasize that preserving investor trust will be contingent on the government’s ability to maintain macroeconomic stability while continuing to fund big development projects.

Despite the present issues, Iraq has large foreign currency reserves, which act as a financial cushion for the government.

However, experts warn that while reserves might help absorb short-term shocks, they are not a substitute for the fundamental changes needed to diversify the economy and reduce its dependence on unpredictable oil earnings.

World.title: Iraq expects record 22 million pilgrims for Arbaeen
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is prepared to welcome around 22 million pilgrims for this year’s Arbaeen pilgrimage, including up to 5 million overseas tourists, in what officials believe to be one of the country’s greatest religious gatherings and a significant boost to tourism and the local economy.

According to Iraqi official data, well over 22 million people are anticipated to attend the annual pilgrimage to the holy city of Karbala, with 4.5 million to 5 million pilgrims coming from outside Iraq.

The government has announced that tens of thousands of volunteers would be deployed to assist pilgrims, and Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has urged officials to boost the number of buses and other transport services to facilitate travel during the festival.

The surge of foreign tourists is projected to have a substantial impact on Iraq’s tourism, hospitality, transportation, and retail industries, with hotels, restaurants, transit operators, and local businesses benefitting from increased demand during the pilgrimage season.

Officials have extended transportation networks in preparation for this year’s pilgrimage, including more rail services, buses, and logistical assistance, as part of larger measures to boost connectivity and promote Iraq’s tourist industry.

The government has increasingly highlighted religious tourism as a crucial pillar of economic diversification, with millions of people visiting the country’s holy sites at Karbala, Najaf, Kadhimiya, and Samarra each year.

According to officials, continuing investment in infrastructure and tourist services will help Iraq become one of the Middle East’s major religious tourism destinations, while also creating jobs and helping local economies around the country.

World.title: Reports: Iraq PM threatened to resign over militia disarmament
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi has threatened to resign if Iran-aligned armed groups do not cooperate with his government’s efforts to bring all weapons under state control, according to reports citing political sources, highlighting the growing pressure on Baghdad to address one of its most difficult security challenges.

According to sources, Al-Zaidi warned leaders of Iraq’s Shi’ite Coordination Framework that if armed groups did not react to government efforts to disarm and completely submit to state authority, he would stand down.

IraqiNews.com was unable to independently verify the claims, and the Prime Minister’s office had no immediate response.

According to the sources, Al-Zaidi has been more dissatisfied by what he sees as a lack of cooperation on one of his administration’s fundamental commitments: guaranteeing that all weapons stay solely under the control of the Iraqi government.

The claims came days after US-Saudi airstrikes struck Iran-backed groups in Iraq in response to drone assaults on Saudi oil installations, which Riyadh said were launched from Iraqi territory.

The bombings forced Al-Zaidi to call an emergency security conference, cancel a planned trip to Saudi Arabia, and unveil a new security strategy aimed at preventing Iraqi territory from being used to launch attacks on neighboring nations.

Armed organizations have emerged as one of Al-Zaidi’s most pressing problems.

Since entering office, he has attempted to solicit billions of dollars in foreign investment with trips to Washington, Tehran, and Ankara, while portraying Iraq as a stable location for oil, infrastructure, and technological projects.

Analysts believe Baghdad’s economic objectives are strongly dependent on its ability to show that the state, not armed groups, controls Iraq’s security strategy.

Repeated strikes conducted from Iraqi territory have strained ties with regional allies and risk weakening investor trust.

According to Western diplomatic sources published by Asharq Al-Awsat, key Iraqi officials, including Al-Zaidi and members of Iraq’s security apparatus, have received threats in connection with the government’s attempts to restrict weaponry outside of state control.

Unlike many regional leaders, Iraq’s prime minister leads by wide political agreement rather than a legislative majority, restricting his power to make unilateral choices.

Major security and political changes usually need agreement among Iraq’s different political blocs.

Al-Zaidi’s biggest power may not be the threat of resignation, but rather the international backing his administration has garnered as a result of recent accords with the United States, Turkey, and other allies.

These agreements, which span energy, finance, technology, and infrastructure, have boosted hopes that Iraq will attract tens of billions of dollars in investment if security improves.

Whether Al-Zaidi can translate that international momentum into domestic reforms will ultimately depend on gaining broader political support for his pledge to keep all weapons under Iraqi state control, which has become one of his government’s most closely watched tests.

World.title: Iraq denies launching strikes from its territory against neighboring nations
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The military spokesperson for the Iraqi commander-in-chief, Sabah al-Numan, confirmed on Thursday that neither a foreign nor local body has presented proof that recent regional drone attacks were launched from Iraqi territory.

In a statement to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), al-Numan urged accusing parties to submit reliable proof, saying that Baghdad has yet to receive such data.

The development comes following statements made by the Saudi Ministry of Defense, alleging that drone attacks targeting key oil infrastructure in the past few days originated in Iraq.

The Iraqi official indicated that the government will neither tolerate unilateral military acts from within its borders nor accept foreign violations of its territorial sovereignty.

Al-Numan’s remarks come a day after the United States and Saudi Arabia launched coordinated airstrikes targeting several bases of Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), killing and injuring many fighters.

The joint operation targeted several logistical and weapons storage locations in different provinces in Iraq, escalating the current regional battle.

The PMF described the joint US-Saudi strike as a dangerous escalation and a clear breach of Iraqi sovereignty.

World.title: Iraqi oil flows to continue via Turkey’s Ceyhan as renewal deal is discussed
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Turkish sources told Reuters that crude oil shipments from northern Iraq to the Turkish port of Ceyhan will continue while the two countries seek an arrangement to extend the pipeline’s operation for another 12 months.

On July 27, a bilateral agreement that had been in place for decades ended. Despite expectations, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi did not sign a 12-month renewal deal during his meeting with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Ankara on Tuesday.

According to a Turkish official, oil flows via the Iraq-Turkey pipeline, which is Baghdad’s only operational export pipeline, will continue while negotiations for a renewal deal are still in progress.

Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar recently announced a 12-month extension agreement between the two countries.

During a joint press conference in Ankara, Erdogan stated on Tuesday that Turkey hopes to finalize a comprehensive energy cooperation agreement as soon as possible.

An extension is intended to provide additional time for discussions on a complete accord. Turkey aims to fully utilize the 1.5 million barrels per day pipeline and consider expanding it to oil fields in southern Iraq.

Turkish data suggests that the pipeline currently transports approximately 170,000 barrels per day.

World.title: Monsoon likely to be ‘below normal’ in Aug-Sept: IMD
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Average rainfall in India during the second half of monsoon season (Aug-Sept) is most likely to be âbelow normalâ, IMD said Friday, flagging the continuing risk of El NiÃ±o, which is associated with a weak monsoon.

Last month, IMD had cited El NiÃ±oâs impact to forecast below normal rains in July. The monthâs rainfall turned out to be normal due to plentiful showers in central India. The met department attributed this to âintra-seasonal variabilityâ, saying a record 24 days were under the influence of âlow pressure systemsâ (LPS) in July against normal of about 13.5 days.

âFour LPS were formed over Bay of Bengal that led to good rainfall from Odisha to Gujarat.

We need to further analyse the reason (for better-than-expected July rains). These LPS couldnât be captured by our long-range forecast model,â said Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, IMD chief.

July rain gives hope to farm sector

Two long wet spells, one during the first week of July and the second from July 22 onwards, helped reduce the overall monsoon rainfall deficit in the country from 35% in June to nearly 13% at the end of July. Since the âmonsoon core zoneâ, where farming operations remain mainly rain-fed, largely coincides with central India, good rains in the region could aid recovery of acreage in the month.

World.title: 16.4% deleted in Haryana draft roll; 10.8% in Andhra Pradesh
World.content:
Nearly 16.4% of the electorate in Haryana and 10.8% in Andhra Pradesh were excluded in draft voter rolls published for the two states Friday as part of phase 3 of special intensive revision (SIR).

In Haryana, the total strength of electors in the draft roll was 83.6% of 2.1 crore at the start of SIR on May 14. Of those deleted in the enumeration phase, 3.7% (7.7 lakh) have been marked by booth-level officers as dead; 11.7% (24.1 lakh) as permanently shifted, absent or untraceable; and 1% (2 lakh) as enrolled at more than one place.

Andhra draft roll

drops 44.9L names

Over 89.2% of 4.2 crore electors enrolled in Andhra Pradesh at the start of Special Intensive Revision submitted their enumeration forms, with the remaining 3.7% found deceased; 5.3% permanently shifted, absent or untraceable; and 1.8% enrolled at multiple places.

The draft roll published Friday lists a total 3.7 crore electors in Andhra, after deletion of 44.9 lakh voters.

AP chief electoral officer (CEO) Vivek Yadav and Haryana CEO A Srinivas attributed the non-collection of 10.6% and 16.4% enumeration forms, respectively, to the corresponding electors having enrolled in another state or UT, not being found by BLOs, not having submitted the form within the deadline (July 24), or simply not willing to register as an elector.

Genuine electors can still be added back in the electoral rolls during the claims and objections period, which will run from July 31 to Aug 30, by filling up Form 6, along with the prescribed declaration form.

World.title: Tahir Hussain gets life for IB staffer’s killing in 2020 riots
World.content:
'

Only death sentence will be justiceâ

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Bringing the six-year-long trial in the murder of Intelligence Bureau staffer Ankit Sharma to a close, a Delhi court on Friday sentenced former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and four others to life imprisonment, holding that Sharma was lynched âsolely on account of his religionâ during the 2020 northeast Delhi riots.Additional sessions judge Parveen Kumar Singh, however, declined the prosecutionâs plea for the death penalty, ruling that while the brutality of the crime was undeniable, the prosecution had failed to prove any specific act committed by each convict during the murder.Pronouncing the sentence, Singh described the murder as one of exceptional brutality committed during the âcommunal violence that erupted in the wake of the protests against CAA/NRCâ.The court held that the prosecution failed to prove allegations that Hussain had âaided, abetted, instigated or led the unlawful assemblyâ. Singh rejected the other convictsâ pleas that they were sole breadwinners. However, he did consider their educational background as a mitigating factor.On July 13, the court had convicted Hussain and four others, holding that the five were part of âa large crowd which, with animus against Hindus, had assembled...with a common object to commit rioting, loot, arson and to cause damage to the property and person of members of the Hindu communityâ, before murdering the IB staffer on Feb 25, 2020, whose body was later recovered from a drain.Hussain was sentenced to six monthsâ RI under IPC Section 188, three years under Section 153A, two years under Section 147, three years under Section 148, seven years under Section 365 and imprisonment for life under Section 302. All sentences will run concurrently. He was also fined Rs 1,000 under Section 188, Rs 20,000 each under Sections 153A, 147 and 148, Rs 50,000 under Section 365 and Rs 5 lakh under Section 302, with default sentences in case of non-payment.âThe manner in which it was committed was of the utmost brutality. The victim was sucked in by the murderous mob, baying for blood... The assault was so fierce, unrelenting, and from such close quarters that even in death, the body did not immediately slump to the ground,â the judge held.The court noted that the violence did not end with Sharmaâs death. His body, it observed, was strapped âlike an animalâ, dragged to Chand Bagh pulia and thrown into a drain. Calling it an âaggravating circumstance of immense magnitudeâ, the judge remarked, âAs if the hatred had still not been satiated, the dead body was thereafter thrown into the nala. Therefore, the barbarity with which this horrendous murder was committed is nauseatingly sickening. âSaying the âcrime testâ tilted the case towards the ârarest of rareâ category, the judge weighed aggravating and mitigating circumst-ances before declining the capital punishment sought by special public prosecutor Madhukar Pandey, who maintained that the offence was part of âwell-orchestrated communal violenceâ rather than a crime committed und-er sudden provocation.The court zoomed in on what it found to be the prosecutionâs principal shortcoming â the lack of specificity regarding the individual role of each convict. Observing that âbefore a life is ordered to be extinguished by a judicial decreeâ, something more than mere membership of an unlawful assembly had to be proved, the judge held that the prosecution had failed to bridge that gap. While acknowledging the stateâs contention that the use of a heavy cutting weapon reflected pre-planned and cold-blooded intent, the court said the time for drawing such inferences was long past and treated the lack of specificity as a âhuge mitigation. âJudge Singh rejected the convictsâ pleas that they were sole breadwinners and noted that the âmonstrosity of the crime committed outweighs this mitigating circumstanceâ. At the same time, he found no material to conclude that they were beyond reform.It also noted that allegations of Hussainâs house being used as a âlaunchpadâ for the riots were neither part of the charges framed nor specifically proved during trial. The judge also took note of the âentirely satisfactoryâ custodial conduct of Hussain, Kasim and Nazim, barring minor infractions by Kasim.Another mitigating factor, the court said, was the educational background of the convicts. It observed that âvested interestsâ had spread misinformation and whipped up a âreligious frenzyâ, making the uneducated co-convicts âmore gullible and susceptible to such propagandaâ, and held that this vulnerability to manipulation was relevant while determining the sentence.Hussainâs co-convicts were awarded life imprisonment under Section 302 IPC with a fine of Rs 25,000 each. They were also sentenced to six months under Section 188, three years under Section 153A, two years under Section 147, three years under Section 148 and seven years under Section 365 IPC, along with fines ranging from Rs 1,000 to Rs 10,000 under the respective provisions. All the sentences will run concurrently.As Hussain was being led out of the courtroom by police after the sentencing, he turned to those present and said, âHigh court se insaaf milega. Der aaye, lekin durust aaye.âSpeaking to TOI, Ankur Sharma, brother of the IB staffer, said, âFrom day one, this has been a ârarest of rareâ case. While we appreciate that the trial court has delivered a conviction and handed down life imprisonment, true justice wonât be served until the perpetrators receive the death sentence, a demand we will aggressively pursue in the high court. The sheer brutality of the crime still haunts our family every single day; knowing he was inflicted with 51 wounds, subjected to acid, and dumped in a drain is a pain that never truly goes away. â

World.title: Floating solar plants get Rs 5,000cr push
World.content: Seeking to increase the Floating Solar Photovoltaic (FSPV) capacity to 5,000 mw from 700 mw, the Centre Friday cleared a Rs 5,070 crore scheme to push development of floating solar projects along with storage set-ups with a minimum capacity of 2 hours. World.title: Reaction teams to flag 'fake info' on E20 blending
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Learning from the recent CJP-led protests govt has set up a team of officials from multiple ministries to counter online "misinformation" on E20 fuel through coordinated efforts by vehicle manufacturers, dealers, vehicle testing agencies, oil marketing companies and fuel pump dealers and other stakeholders, reports Dipak Dash.

World.title: Waqf registrations rise by 35,000 in West Bengal after UMEED portal launch
World.content:
Kolkata

The Union Minority Affairs Ministry has informed Parliament that 1,15,551 Waqf properties in West Bengal have been validated and approved on the Unified Waqf Management, Empowerment, Efficiency and Development (UMEED) portal as of July 15, 2026, up from 80,548 properties reported in February 2025. A rise of around 35,000 registrations in a year.

“As on date 15.07.2026, a total of 1,33,417 waqf properties were initiated by the Board of Auqaf, West Bengal for uploading on the UMEED Central Portal–2025. Out of these, 1,15,551 waqf properties have been validated and approved by the approver, while 12,720 properties have been rejected during verification. Thus, the Board of Auqaf, West Bengal has complied with the extended statutory deadline,” an answer by the Minister of Minority Affairs, Kiren Rijiju, said to a question raised by Bharatiya West Bengal State President Samik Bhattacharya.

The State Waqf Board already had 80,548 properties registered under them.

Former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee opposed the Waqf Amendment Bill and said that she would protect the Waqf properties in the State. She issued an  in the papers in January 2026 stating that the State Waqf Board had filed a Writ petition against the issue at the Supreme Court.

However, the Ms Banerjee government also told people that they must register their properties on UMEED. “Therefore, there is no truth in such propaganda that registration of property details in the new portal [UMEED portal] will result in transfer or alienation of Waqf properties,” the newspaper  later said after many criticised Ms Banerjee for opposing the bill yet asking people to register.

In June 2025, the Central government launched the UMEED portal to start central registration of properties after the Waqf Amendment Bill was passed in the Parliament and became an Act.

Also Read |​Communal cauldron: On a communal divide in West Bengal

“The number of registrations in the past year may be more because the UMEED portal started in 2025. But these properties have remained unregistered in the past 15 years since the board did their last survey. So, the numbers have increased in the past 15 years; the registration has happened in the past year,” a source in the State Waqf Board told The Hindu.

The issue of Waqf has long been a matter of much heated political debate in West Bengal since the Bill was introduced in 2024. The State Assembly had passed a resolution in December 2024 opposing the Bill. The bill triggered many protests in the State, including an incident of communal violence in Murshidabad, killing at least three.

World.title: Modi, Burnham discuss trade, technology, Hormuz over phone
World.content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his British counterpart, Andy Burnham, spoke on the telephone on Friday (July 31, 2026), agreeing to cooperate closely on several sectors and “fully harness” the recently operationalised trade agreement between New Delhi and London, as per the government.

“We agreed to work together across sectors such as technology, innovation, defence, security, clean energy, education and people-to-people ties and take the India-U.K. Comprehensive Strategic Partnership to new heights,” Mr. Modi wrote on social media site X.

Delighted to speak with Prime Minister of the United Kingdom Andy Burnham. Congratulated him on assuming office and conveyed my best wishes for a successful tenure.



We agreed to work together across sectors such as technology, innovation, defence, security, clean energy,… — Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) July 31, 2026

“We will also collaborate closely to fully harness the trade and investment opportunities,” he added. The trade deal was operationalised on July 15, during the final few days of Keir Starmer’s two years in office.

Mr. Burnham discussed the strength of the relationship and the significance it had on local communities in Britain, as per a Downing Street spokesperson.

“The Prime Minister [Mr. Burnham] praised the contribution Indian communities in the U.K. make to the fabric of U.K. society, with Prime Minister Modi noting the links between the two leaders’ own home cities of Manchester and Ahmedabad, in Gujarat, which he called the ‘Manchester of India’, “the spokesperson said. Mr. Burnham was, until recently, the mayor of Greater Manchester - which is home to a sizeable Indian-origin population.

Mr. Burnham conveyed to the Prime Minister that he was personally committed to the U.K.-India Technology Security Initiative (TSI), according to the Downing Street readout. The TSI was launched in July 2024 as a platform to enhance cooperation in AI, health-tech, semiconductors, critical minerals and so forth.

Both the Prime Ministers noted the potential to work together in AI, Downing Street said. Mr. Burnham has officially elevated the government’s AI strategy by appointing a cabinet minister to head AI policy. The Minister, Indian-born Kanishka Narayan, was previously operating at the level of a Minister of State in the Starmer administration.

The two men also discussed the U.S.-Iran war, agreeing to work “closely together” towards de-escalation and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, Downing Street said.

World.title: Cabinet approves scheme to promote ‘floating’ solar plants
World.content:
The Union Cabinet on Friday (July 31, 2026) approved the Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana (PM-SSY), a ₹5,070-crore scheme aimed at accelerating floating solar power by providing central financial assistance (CFA) of up to ₹1 crore per MW for projects installed on reservoirs and other water bodies.

The programme targets 5,000 MW of floating solar capacity by 2030-31.

The scheme, to be implemented by the Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI), comes at a time when India has only about 0.7 GW of installed floating solar capacity despite an estimated technical potential of 102 GW.

Projects receiving support under the scheme will have to include battery energy storage equivalent to at least two hours, amounting to 10,000 MWh across the programme.

India’s flagship project, the Omkareshwar floating solar park, located on the Narmada in Madhya Pradesh’s Khandwa district is the country’s largest at 278 MW, with plans to scale to 600 MW output. However, it doesn’t have onsite battery storage.

Officials said the financial support was intended as a “nudge” to the industry to develop an alternative stream of solar capacity rather than a permanent subsidy. Solar development in India has remained concentrated in Rajasthan and Gujarat because of their vast tracts of inexpensive land and high solar radiation.

Reservoir-based projects are expected to “diversify” installations geographically, particularly in States with large water bodies but limited land availability.

Land constraints

The policy is also designed to address two of the biggest constraints facing ground-mounted solar projects: acquiring large contiguous parcels of land and the rising costs associated with rehabilitation and resettlement.

Ground-mounted solar, which accounts for the overwhelming majority of India’s roughly 100 GW of installed solar capacity, typically requires three to four times more land per megawatt than the area the solar panels physically occupy.

Land acquisition has increasingly emerged as a bottleneck as India pursues its target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel electricity capacity by 2030.

Potential and advantages

A recent assessment by the National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE) estimated that India could host 102.18 GW of floating solar after factoring in multiple variables including perennial water availability, suitable depth, adequate solar irradiation and proximity to roads and substations. Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Odisha, and Telangana account for the largest share of this potential

Floating solar offers several operational advantages over conventional ground-mounted systems. By using reservoirs and industrial ponds, it avoids competition for agricultural land while reducing water evaporation. Cooler operating conditions over water also reduce soiling losses and can improve panel efficiency.

The Cabinet note says the scheme will also encourage domestic manufacturing of specialised components while generating an estimated 16,000-17,000 jobs.

Cost and engineering

The technology, however, comes at a premium. Government estimates place floating solar system costs at ₹4.9-5.2 crore per MW, about 25% higher than comparable ground-mounted projects due to the additional expenditure on floating platforms, anchoring and mooring systems.

The mandatory battery storage further increases project costs. Developers have also reported engineering challenges at existing projects, including wear on floating structures and cable failures. The Centre nevertheless expects the higher upfront costs to be offset by the strategic value of creating a geographically diversified solar fleet with integrated storage reducing dependence on land-intensive projects while making renewable electricity more dispatchable.

World.title: The Hindu brings the historic 1947 Independence Day edition back to life
World.content:
When India awoke to freedom on the morning of August 15, 1947, The Hindu was there to chronicle the birth of a newly independent nation. Now, as the country prepares to celebrate its 80th Independence Day, the publication is offering readers a rare opportunity to step back into that exact moment in time.

To honour this defining milestone, The Hindu has reproduced its landmark August 15, 1947, edition in its entirety. The original 32-page edition has been meticulously reproduced exactly as it appeared nearly eight decades ago.

Within its pages, readers will find rare photographs documenting the hard-fought freedom struggle and the country’s first proud steps forward. It features deeply personal Independence Day greetings from monumental figures including Jawaharlal Nehru and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

Alongside these historic messages are vivid, on-the-ground reports of the very first flag-hoisting ceremonies that swept the nation. Even the vintage s offer a fascinating, nostalgic glimpse into India’s social and commercial landscape of the era.

Starting August 1, 2026, limited copies of this collector’s edition will be available exclusively on Zepto across major Indian cities. It is a unique chance to own and hold history in your hands.

World.title: Kochi metro records operational profit, lowers net loss
World.content:
Kochi Metro Rail Limited (KMRL) claimed to have registered an operational profit of ₹52.64 crore in 2025-26. The year also saw its net loss fall from ₹430.50 crore in 2024–25 to ₹352.49 crore, said a KMRL release.

The operational profit will go up when the metro’s second phase connecting the city with Smart City and Infopark in Kakkanad is commissioned, hoped KMRL managing director Loknath Behera.

The metro also saw average daily ridership crossing the one-lakh mark during the year, reaching 1.01 lakh passengers.

Of the total operational revenue of ₹224.65 crore, ₹76.33 crore (nearly 34%) came from non-fare sources.

World.title: Supreme Court asks Centre to facilitate DNA testing of Indians killed in Russia-Ukraine war
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Friday (July 31, 2026) directed the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) to appoint a nodal officer to facilitate DNA testing of the mortal remains of Indian nationals killed on the frontlines of the Russia-Ukraine war, ensuring families can claim them for last rites.

A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant asked the Ministry to forward the details of the nodal officer to the family members of the deceased once the appointment is made.

The court was hearing a petition filed by families alleging their kin were victims of illegal overseas recruitment, trafficking, and exploitation. According to the petitioners, the youths were lured by recruiters with promises of high-paying jobs, only to have their passports seized and be pushed into the war zone.

The petitioners sought the whereabouts of Indian nationals believed to be dead or missing, urging the court to intervene for the repatriation of bodies and the payment of monetary compensation by Russian authorities.

Compensation claims

The court on Friday (July 31) ruled that complete records for filing compensation claims with Russian authorities must be provided to the families, who can submit their claims through the Ministry. The Bench added that families should receive legal aid for these filings, along with DNA verification certificates and translated versions of any Russian documents.

The court clarified that compensation claims should not become a ground for delaying the handing over of mortal remains or the performance of funeral rituals.

Diplomatic efforts

The Union government informed the court that nearly 220 Indians had joined the Russian Armed Forces during the conflict, with 139 released from contractual agreements.

Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, stated that the government successfully negotiated with Russian authorities for the discharge of Indian nationals. Out of the 51 Indians died in the battleground, the remains of 29 individuals have been brought back to India, she added.

The petitioners also highlighted the necessity of identifying and prosecuting illegal overseas recruitment rackets that exploit vulnerable citizens with false promises of foreign employment.

World.title: Kin of injured Delhi police personnel want their views to be discussed in Parliament
World.content:
Family members of four Delhi Police personnel who were injured during the crackdown on the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led march to Parliament on July 20, demanding the resignation of then Education Minister Dhrmendra Pradhan, on Friday (July 31, 2026) called for a discussion in Parliament on the injuries suffered by the policemen on duty. They said the public discourse so far has been “one-sided”.

Addressing a press conference at the Constitution Club, the family members—the wives of an ACP and an ASI, and the children of two injured police officers—took turns to recount what had transpired that day and said that “their side of the story” of the June 20 violence needed to be heard.

Slideshow presented

The families presented photographs of injured and bleeding police personnel through a slideshow, that claimed that more than 250 police personnel were injured in the violence, while over 110 barricades, 300 body protectors, 350 helmets, 20 loudhailers, 10 hand-held metal detectors and one X-ray baggage scanner were damaged, with more than 25 government vehicles and private property vandalised.

They alleged that several anti-social elements had joined the students who attacked the policemen.

The wife of an ASI who sustained injuries during the violence said, “Students should be released after their records are verified, but the miscreants who attempted to disrupt the students’ protest, tarnish its image and undermine the dignity of Parliament should be held accountable for their actions and should not be spared.”

A Delhi University student whose father, a sub-inspector, was injured in the clashes, said he had served for 15 years as a Marine Commando in the Indian Navy before joining the police. She said that her father returned home with his uniform soaked in blood, but when she opened social media, he had already been declared a criminal.

Another family member of an injured ACP said, “Whenever I go online, I see videos portraying only the police as criminals. There is no discussion, even in Parliament, about the police personnel who were injured. We only want our side to be heard.”

Several questions have been raised over the alleged use of excessive force against protesters during the July 20 march. Videos circulating on social media name and identify some of the men in uniform using excessive force, while some clips also show police personnel in plain clothes wielding batons.

On July 28, the Supreme Court observed that it would consider constituting a high-powered investigating team to conduct a “thorough, fair and independent” inquiry into allegations of police excesses during the recent student protests in Delhi.

World.title: Triumph of justice vs Hussain a BJP man: parties trade barbs after Tahir Hussain verdict
World.content:
A war of words broke out between the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Opposition Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on Friday (July 31, 2026) following the sentencing of former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and four others to life imprisonment for the murder of Intelligence Bureau officer Ankit Sharma during the 2020 north-east Delhi riots.

While the BJP hailed the court order for “establishing how AAP-backed miscreants spread riots in north-east Delhi”, the Opposition party hit back, claiming that Hussain was “indirectly working for the BJP”.

Welcoming the order, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said people in Delhi are now demanding answers from AAP.

“Tahir Hussain was arrested on charges of murder, yet even after that, [AAP chief Arvind] Kejriwal and [AAP leader] Manish Sisodia stood in his support! They kept trying relentlessly to save him! Why? Will Mr. Kejriwal tell the people of Delhi? Was it under their patronage that people like Tahir Hussain conspired to incite riots? Today, justice has triumphed. This verdict further strengthens the faith of every citizen of the country in the law and the judiciary,” Ms. Gupta posted on X.

Delhi BJP president Harsh Malhotra said, “Kejriwal should be ashamed for not only sheltering such criminals within the party but also for repeatedly using his influence to protect them. The true character of the Aam Aadmi Party is now well understood not only by the people of Delhi but also by the people of Punjab.”

Delhi Law Minister Kapil Mishra said the sentencing was “the beginning of justice”.

‘Hussain a BJP man’

Addressing a press conference, AAP’s State unit chief Saurabh Bharadwaj said his party had expelled Hussain as soon as an FIR was registered against him in the Ankit Sharma murder case. Mr. Bharadwaj said Hussain had contested the Mustafabad Assembly election last year on an All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen ticket as part of a “well-planned strategy by the BJP” against AAP.

“There are dozens of instances where the BJP has embraced individuals involved in the most heinous crimes. In reality, Tahir Hussain was a BJP man. If anyone gained political advantage from the Delhi riots, it was the BJP,” said the former Health Minister.

He accused Mr. Mishra, who was earlier with AAP, of backing Hussain and propping him up as a politician. “Kapil Mishra’s own election office and MLA office were located in Tahir Hussain’s house, where weapons or stones allegedly used in the riots were found stored. It was Kapil Mishra who inducted Tahir Hussain into the party [AAP],” said the senior AAP leader.

World.title: Govt cuts petrol price by 12 paisas, diesel by 66 paisas for the next three days
World.content:
The government on Friday reduced the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by 12 paisas and 66 paisas per litre, respectively.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs336.03 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs392.38 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs110 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs96 per litre on diesel.

The Petroleum Division’s notification said that the new prices would be applicable from August 1 to August 3.

Meanwhile, in a bigger price shock, the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) notified a record 32pc increase in the price of regasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG) for August, taking it to $25.83 per mmBtu for SNGPL and $25.09 per mmBtu for SSGCL.

This will translate into a retail price of Rs7,204 per mmBtu. The price is based on five imported cargoes from the spot market, as no shipment could be secured from Qatar because of the US-Iran war. This is the single biggest jump in RLNG rates in its decade-long history.

This comes on top of an about 15pc increase in the RLNG price fixed last month at $19.52 per mmBtu (Rs5,446 per mmBtu) for SNGPL and $18.63 per mmBtu for SSGCL.

Compared with $10.45 (Rs2,916) per mmBtu in February this year, the RLNG price hike works out to around 148pc for August.

This mainly results in a substantial increase in fuel costs for power generation. This can be seen from the fact that the fuel cost for RLNG-based power generation in May worked out to Rs31 per unit, compared with Rs13.72 per unit in April.

The diesel price has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan this week.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Search operation for climbers missing after Broad Peak avalanche suspended due to bad weather
World.content:
GILGIT: The search and rescue operation for foreign climbers missing after an avalanche at Broad Peak was suspended late Friday due to adverse weather conditions in the region.

Three bodies of missing climbers — one each from the United States, Nepal and Oman — were airlifted from Broad Peak to Skardu by Pakistan Army helicopters. Drone footage also indicated the presence of more climbers during the search operation.

Earlier reports had said that four bodies were recovered; however, the toll was later revised down to three. Seven climbers remain missing.

According to a press release issued by the Commissioner Baltistan Division, the search and rescue operation was launched following a formal request from tour operators.

A three-member civil rescue team, led by renowned mountaineer Sarbaz Khan, was airlifted to Broad Peak Base Camp by Pakistan Army Aviation helicopters.

The team recovered the bodies of three climbers, identified as Oman’s Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy, Nepal’s Pur Bahadur Gurung and Mallory Geis from the United States. The bodies were later shifted to CMH Skardu by Pakistan Army Aviation helicopters.

The press release said the rescue operation had been temporarily suspended due to poor weather conditions and would resume on Saturday once conditions improved. Other Sherpas involved in mountaineering expeditions at the peak would also assist in the operation.

The rescue team said signs indicating the presence of more climbers had also been spotted through drone footage.

Despite the challenging terrain and harsh weather conditions at such high altitudes, the search operation was continuing with the cooperation of the Pakistan Army, local expert mountaineers and rescue teams.

The Gilgit-Baltistan government expressed condolences to the families of the deceased climbers and assured them that all possible assistance would be provided in the rescue operation and the repatriation of the bodies to their respective countries.

Experts said the chances of survival for the missing climbers were diminishing with each passing hour.

Earlier, the Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) said that the 10-member team included six Nepalese climbers, a Pakistani, an Omani, an American and a climber from China. The climbers from Nepal were identified as renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja, Pur Bahadur Gurung, Kili Pemba Sherpa, Nima Sherpa, Nawang Thindu Sherpa and Gyalu Sherpa.

It identified the remaining climbers as Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy from Oman, Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi, Wang Zhong from China and Mallory Geis from the United States.

Rescue operation

In a statement issued earlier in the day, ACP Senior Vice President Karrar Haidri said two Pakistan Army Aviation rescue helicopters, carrying rescue personnel and additional specialised equipment, had been dispatched to support the ongoing search and rescue operation.

The statement said the ACP president, along with the club’s senior leadership, remained in constant contact with the highest government authorities and relevant agencies to facilitate the rescue operation.

“Every possible effort is being made to ensure that helicopter support and all available rescue resources are mobilised at the earliest opportunity, subject to weather and operational conditions,” it added.

The club said it was closely monitoring the situation and coordinating with all relevant stakeholders while expressing solidarity with the climbers’ families and the international mountaineering community.

ACP’s General Secretary Ayaz Shigri told Dawn that several expedition teams had jointly begun their summit push before the incident.

He said GPS locations received from some of the missing climbers indicated that the avalanche had swept the group about 1,000 metres downhill, leaving them trapped.

Shigri said there were also fears that some local high-altitude porters might have been affected by the avalanche.

“We pray for the safety of all the climbers. It is a big incident,” he said.

Meanwhile, Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Amjad Hussain Advocate directed all relevant departments to remain on high alert and expedite the search and rescue operation in coordination with the Pakistan Army, according to an official statement.

He instructed the district administration and concerned authorities to utilise all available resources to ensure the climbers’ safety.

Gilgit-Baltistan Minister for Tourism, Sports and Culture Naiknam Karim also expressed sorrow over the incident and said the provincial government was making every possible effort to locate and safely rescue the missing climbers.

In a statement, he said “all relevant departments are in constant coordination and that every available resource was being utilised to support the ongoing search and rescue operation”.

Expressing hope that the missing climbers would be found safe, the minister directed the concerned authorities to further expedite the rescue operation and ensure that all necessary logistical and operational support was provided to the teams working in the field.

Purja, 43, who served with Britain’s Brigade of Gurkhas before joining the elite Special Boat Service (SBS), has broken multiple climbing records since becoming a full-time mountaineer and tour guide.

He climbed all 14 “eight-thousanders” (peaks above 8,000 metres, or 26,000 feet) in six months and six days between April and October 2019 — then a record. In 2021, Purja completed the first winter ascent of K2 along with a team of nine other Nepalese climbers.

Separately, in a post on X, the UK Embassy in Pakistan expressed concern at the incident. Seemingly referencing Purja, it also took note of a British-Nepali national missing in the expedition.

“We are concerned by reports that several climbers have gone missing during a Broad Peak expedition, including a British-Nepali national,” the embassy said, adding that it remained in contact with Pakistani authorities.

Sakhi, who hails from Hunza, had successfully summited Kanchenjunga (8,58­6m), the world’s 3rd highest mountain, in Nepal earlier in May. He had previously scaled K2, Nanga Parbat, Gasherbrum I and Gasherbrum II without supplemental oxygen, establishing himself among the country’s strongest high-altitude climbers.

Additional input from AFP

World.title: Good governance 'quintessential' for security and stability of Pakistan: DG ISPR
World.content:
Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry on Friday termed good governance “quintessential” for Pakistan’s security and stability.

He made the remarks while addressing a press conference on the country’s overall security situation, particularly the situation in Balochistan.

The DG ISPR, during his presser, commented on Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s remarks about the need for new administrative units in Pakistan: “We have been saying this earlier also as a primary stakeholder in security that good governance is essential for the security and stability of Pakistan.”

Without this, he stressed that none of Pakistan’s issues could be resolved.
